title: Missions in GTA San Andreas
text: This is a comprehensive list of storyline missions in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. There are 101 missions in total, which makes this game the Grand Theft Auto singleplayer title with most missions.

title: Missions in GTA San Andreas
text: Protagonist Carl Johnson returns home to Los Santos and needs to reestablish himself in the neighborhood. Years previously, the death of his brother, Brian Johnson, was blamed on him by his elder brother, Sweet, and Carl moved away for a fresh start in Liberty City. Following the death of his mother in a drive-by shooting by the Ballas, he returns and decides to stay for good. Missions involve him working for the prominent members of the Grove Street Families: his brother Sweet, the childhood friend and junkie Ryder, and cryptic childhood friend, Big Smoke. Other than those three, CJ participates in illicit street racing with his sister Kendl's boyfriend, Cesar Vialpando, who faces a lot of prejudice from Sweet, who looks down on Cesar being Mexican.

CJ also does missions for OG Loc, a GSF associate obsessed with his "gangsta" rapper image, but in reality, his crimes range from parking fines to joyriding. Meanwhile, C.R.A.S.H., led by Officers Frank Tenpenny and Eddie Pulaski, exploit CJ into doing their dirty work, under the threat of framing him for Officer Pendelbury's murder, which they committed themselves.

There are 29 missions (including the opening sequence) in Los Santos.

title: Missions in GTA San Andreas
section: Countryside Missions (Red County, Flint County, Whetstone)
text:
CJ has stumbles onto something that is much bigger than himself. It appears that his childhood friend and fellow Grove Street Families member, Big Smoke, is in an alliance with Tenpenny, and helps demolish the established influence and territory of the GSF—allowing the Ballas to take over as the dominant gang in Los Santos in exchange for money and power. Tenpenny warns CJ to stay away from Big Smoke, otherwise Sweet, who was arrested, will suffer in prison. Tenpenny has a few loose ends that need to be taken care of, and Carl takes care of them while trying to keep himself and his sister out of danger. Unknown to Tenpenny, Carl attempts to gain money and connection through robberies with his sister's boyfriend's cousin, Catalina. 

There are 14 missions in the countryside (including 4 missions that are cutscenes for the robbery missions).

title: Missions in GTA San Andreas
text:
CJ is starting to build his own name in San Fierro while still working for Tenpenny. The Truth, who used to be Tenpenny's supplier before he was double-crossed by him, introduces him to certain people with talents to assist him. Woozie, a Chinese Triad leader whom CJ met at a race, gives him work to further establish himself. With the help of Cesar, The Truth, Woozie, and the others, CJ manages to inflict major damage on the drug trade in Los Santos that provides for Smoke's new empire.

There are 26 missions in San Fierro.

title: Missions in GTA San Andreas
text:
Mike Toreno, a member of a clandestine government organization who CJ originally thought to be involved with the drug ring, reveals that it was a decoy of himself that CJ killed previously. Mike reveals that the Loco Syndicate was a front to finance his agency's operations in Latin America. Toreno tells CJ the truth about Tenpenny's crimes. In return for the assurance that Toreno will keep Sweet safe while in prison and will try to use his connections to release him, CJ will need to do missions for him. This will also serve as a way for CJ to make up for sabotaging Toreno's drug peddling operation. Meanwhile, in the desert, The Truth and CJ do missions involving alien cover-ups by the military.

There are 9 storyline missions in the desert.

title: Driving School
text:
The Driving School consists of 12 lessons in the form of selectable courses, each completed by achieving at least a bronze medal in the final results. All these lessons are required to expand the Doherty Garage operation to the nearby Wang Cars. It is not required for main storyline progression and can be done after the story completion. All of the aforementioned activities, including the Driving School, are required for 100% Completion.

When the player enters the Driving School for the first time after completing the mission Deconstruction, there will be a red marker inside. Walking into this marker will activate the mission Back to School, which is simply a cutscene where Carl Johnson is told by an instructor about the twelve lessons he has to take to improve his driving skills. After this, there will be a red marker right in front of the TV and video tape player.

Mission failure will occur if the player gets wasted, stops or destroys the vehicle during a test.

title: Driving School
text:
The scoring is based on the final heading and position of the player's car. This is the formula of the scoring (goes for all other schools):
 (Final Heading + Final Position) / 2 - Damage Penalty = Final Score
For the Burn and Lap and City Slicking tests, the scoring is simply based on time instead, therefore the formula is:
 ([Gold Medal Time * 2 - Overall Time] / Gold Medal Time) * 100 - Damage Penalty = Final Score

title: Driving School
text:
The Driving School is available at the Turning Tricks Driving School in Doherty, to the south of the Doherty Safehouse upon answering the phone call after Deconstruction.

The recruited Doherty Garage mechanic Jethro will inform Carl via phone call about the Driving School. The Driving School lessons are treated as a tutorial for the maneuvers required to be performed during the car theft mission strand (particularly the ), unlocked with the Wang Cars purchase.

title: Driving School
text:
The first call only occurs if Yay Ka-Boom-Boom is completed first.
Carl Johnson: Hello!
Jethro: Yo, it's Jethro, man. Listen, me an' Cesar have used our contacts to, like, get a wish list of cars, but we'll need to turn them around real quick, dude. Now there's a showroom round the block that's come up for sale and I thought it would be a good idea to make things look as legitimate as possible.
Carl Johnson: Yeah, that's a great idea man, I'm a look in to it. I'm a holla at you.

title: Driving School
text:
The second call only occurs if Verdant Meadows is completed first.
Jethro: Yo, CJ, It's, like, Jethro, dude!
Carl Johnson: Hey Jethro, how is it?
Jethro: Yo, dude, the garage is coming along nicely, man. But I rang about something else. There's an unofficial street racing club in San Fierro.
Carl Johnson: Unofficial, as in 'illegal', right?
Jethro: I don't know what you're talking about, dude. Anyhoo, they meet up around the driving school someplace. Thought you might, y'know, like to know.
Carl Johnson: Thanks, Jethro. I'm a think about it, and I'll holla at you. Later, man.

title: Driving School
text:
By completing the lessons, the player will increase their Driving Skill and unlock the ability to expand the Doherty Garage business to Wang Cars, which will subsequently unlock the Wheel Arch Angels mod garage and the Exports and Imports lists. Additionally, up to three vehicles can be awarded depending on the final results.

The Super GT, Bullet and Hotknife are unlocked by achieving Bronze, Silver and Gold medals respectively in every lesson.

text:

title: The Introduction
text:
The Introduction is a short film, created with Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas video engine, and serves as a prequel to GTA San Andreas that shows the events that happen prior to the events of the game. It was available with the American PlayStation 2 Special Edition of GTA San Andreas and the Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas: Official Soundtrack compilation. It is set in 1992, and ends directly at the beginning of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, with Sweet Johnson informing his brother, Carl Johnson, over telephone that their mother, Beverly, is dead.

The video can be watched and freely downloaded on [http://www.rockstargames.com/videos/video/10491 Rockstar Games' official website] in .wmv or Quicktime format, or on [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=daw8xhaGj2s their official YouTube account].

title: The Introduction
text: This opening scene features LSPD Officers Frank Tenpenny and Eddie Pulaski having just come from a meeting with an unnamed individual who Tenpenny refers to as "that fat fuck" and "that over-sized asshole". Pulaski asks Tenpenny what they are going to do about the new LSPD officer, Hernandez, coming on board with them. Tenpenny states that he is not worried about Hernandez, but says another LSPD officer, Pendelbury, is a bigger concern to their operation. Tenpenny states that if Pendelbury does what he is threatening to do, then they will have a bigger problem with him.

title: The Introduction
text: Almost all the scenes were made in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas locations (including the Liberty City map from the Saint Mark's Bistro mission) despite the fact they are meant to be somewhere else. For example, Kent Paul's studio in England is actually the interior of Madd Dogg's mansion. And despite the fact that Liberty City exteriors were available, as demonstrated earlier in the film, the final scene instead takes place in Downtown Los Santos. One of the possible reasons Tommy Vercetti does not speak in this short film is that Ray Liotta, the voice actor of Tommy, had a dispute with Rockstar North about how much "effort" he put into Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. The appearance of Sex Club 7 in the Liberty City scene is a canonical error. Before 1998, Sex Club 7's unit was actually Paulie's Revue Bar.

Are You Going to San Fierro? is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by pot-growing hippie The Truth from his farm in Leafy Hollow, Flint County, San Andreas.

title: Are You Going to San Fierro?
text:
After the completion of Farewell, My Love..., Catalina gives Carl a deed to an old Xoomer garage in Doherty, San Fierro. The Truth calls, stating that the weed is finally ready, and asks Carl to come see him.

Carl meets the Truth at his farm, pays him for the weed, and prepares to leave in the Truth's Mothership when the two hear a police helicopter outside. The Truth panics, realizing that Tenpenny set them up and that they must destroy the weed; he takes two flamethrowers, gives one to Carl, and the two torch the farm. The player is given five and a half minutes to complete the task. The Truth will stop helping Carl burn the weed after about 70 seconds and will get in his Mothership and wait for Carl.

The Green Sabre is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas. The mission is a major turning point in the game.

title: The Green Sabre
text: The three feuding families of the Grove Street Families have come together due to Carl's efforts and Sweet decides to finally get back at the Ballas. Sweet also makes good with Carl and calls him his "running dog". He then orders everyone to get prepared and meet him under the Mulholland Intersection.

title: The Green Sabre

Carl leaves Sweet's house and receives a call from Cesar, who instructs him to meet up under the freeway north of Verdant Bluffs for some important news. At Cesar's urging, the initially hesitant Carl drives to the meeting point where Cesar is waiting inside a Bravura with tinted windows. There, they witness some Ballas members exiting a garage, followed by Ryder and Big Smoke, and finally Frank Tenpenny. Much to CJ's horror, Eddie Pulaski then reverses a car out of the garage, revealing the same green Sabre that was used in the drive-by in Grove Street that killed Carl's mother. Carl deduces that C.R.A.S.H. ordered the drive-by with the intent of killing Sweet, and have been working with the Ballas, Big Smoke, and Ryder to wipe out the Families and profit off the drug trade.

title: The Green Sabre
text:
The scene where CJ and Sweet are arrested while the other Grove Street members run is inspired by the 1993 movie . In it, Miklo and Paco, two members of the Chicano street gang Vatos Locos (Crazy Guys) get into a shootout with a rival gang and Miklo is wounded. After a police car chase Paco, Miklo and two other members of the Vatos Locos crash the car and while the other two gang members flee the scene, Miklo and Paco are arrested in a similar way to CJ and Sweet and the camera even pans up to an aerial shot. This scene can be seen .
Another striking similarity is that while Sweet and Miklo were sent to prison, Carl and Paco ended up working for law enforcement.
Tenpenny's line "Intimidate those who intimidate others" is a reference to the unofficial motto of the real life unit: "We intimidate those who intimidate others".

Catalyst is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families member Lance "Ryder" Wilson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas.

While Carl and Ryder are talking, Tenpenny and his accomplices walk into the kitchen to inform the pair that there will be an army munitions train passing through East Los Santos shortly, and that enemy gangs such as the Ballas and Vagos will attempt to rob the cargo on board the freight train as well.

If carl fails to throw the required number of boxes by the time they pass Unity Station and enter the tunnel, a short cutscene will play of Carl entering the Picador while Ryder berates him. text: End of the Line is the final storyline mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas.

title: End of the Line

Upon arriving, they see that Smoke's crack palace has heavy security and there's no way to enter the place except for breaking through the wall. Carl convinces Sweet to allow him to go by himself, saying that Smoke and Tenpenny played him, and also wanted to atone for letting their brother, Brian, die five years prior. Carl finds a S.W.A.T. tank nearby and steals it while being attacked by S.W.A.T. officers and Ballas gang members. He successfully smashes the wall and enters the crack palace.

title: End of the Line
text:
Following the closing cutscene and credits, Carl is back on Grove Street. The riots subside, and a final WCTR news report is broadcast detailing the aftermath of the riots. One last phone call from Catalina is received, after which Carl is free to roam about San Andreas as the game enters pure sandbox mode. Any leftover non-storyline missions such as the Zero, Wang Cars, and casino heist strands can still be played out, as can street races, etc.

In sandbox mode, certain aspects of the San Andreas universe continue to play out. Progress with the various girlfriends will still go up and down depending on whether Carl continues to date them or not; Carl's physical condition will still change depending on actions like working out and eating; enemy gang members may still randomly shoot at Carl when he passes.

title: End of the Line
text:
CJ smashing the S.W.A.T. vehicle through the front door of the crack palace is a reference to former police chief , authorizing the LAPD's to use the , an amphibious armored vehicle they referred to as the "battering ram" (which the in-game S.W.A.T. vehicle is based on) to execute search warrants by raiding and smashing into suspected crack dens in during the late 1980s.

text: Robbing Uncle Sam is the final mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families member Lance "Ryder" Wilson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas.

title: Robbing Uncle Sam
text:
Carl goes to see Ryder in his back yard, who is smoking. He asks Carl why he, himself, didn't finish high school. After Carl asks if it was because he dealt drugs since the age of 10, or if it was because he attacked a teacher for wearing Ballas colors, Ryder responds that it's because he is too intelligent. After asking Carl where they can attain guns, Ryder informs him that the National Guard has all of the guns.

Carl and Ryder get inside of a Mule (delivered by LB), and drive to the National Guard Depot at the Ocean Docks. Once they arrive, they notice that the gate is closed. Carl climbs over the wall and shoots the switch to open the gate. Ryder drives the Mule to a weapon's warehouse, where Carl shoots the switch to open the door. Ryder stands guard as Carl collects 6 crates of weaponry inside and around the warehouse using a forklift.

Grove Street Games/Errors 
In the 2014 release of the Mobile version, the outsourced Grove Street Games studio (then known as War Drum Studios) purposely disabled the "Super Sprint" feature introduced by this mission for the touchscreen controls.

In the 2021 release of The Definitive Edition version by Grove Street Games (which is essentially a remastered version of the Mobile version for consoles and PC with Touchscreen UI hidden by default), the "Super Sprint" remains absent from the game. The instruction prompts during the chase will still counterintuitively mention "Super Sprint" despite the player not being able to perform it in this version.

Wrong Side of the Tracks is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families member Melvin "Big Smoke" Harris from his home in Idlewood, Los Santos, San Andreas.

title: Wrong Side of the Tracks
text:
Tenpenny and Pulaski are seen leaving Big Smoke's house from the garage. Carl arrives and Smoke tells him that they have to go to the train station at Unity Station.

When the pair arrive, Smoke explains that the Vagos and San Fierro Rifa are "cutting some kind of deal", and intends to crash the meeting. However, it is actually an ambush and the Vagos attempt to escape by train. Carl and Smoke use a yellow Sanchez parked nearby to chase down the train to kill all four Vagos thugs, whilst avoiding obstacles, such as a car block and incoming trains going the opposite direction. If successful, Carl and Smoke will have eliminated all Vagos before the train reaches the Frederick Bridge, connecting Los Santos and Las Venturas. The two then clear the scene, and CJ takes Big Smoke back to his house.

title: Wrong Side of the Tracks

Due to the difficulty of the mission, leading to many players failing it multiple times, this line became very famous among fans of the , to the point of becoming an internet meme. In the open-world sandbox game , there is a splash which reads "Follow the train, CJ!", which is a reference to this mission. In , the name of the mission is a reference to this mission. There is a scene in Rockstar's Manhunt with the same title, . In , next to the dead body of JC and Little Smoke, the player can find . This mission is referenced in the gold medal objectives for the Grand Theft Auto V mission Derailed, where the player has to follow a train on a dirt bike.

Reuniting the Families is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas.

title: Reuniting the Families
text: Carl goes to Sweet's house and finds him with their close friends Ryder and Big Smoke. All the sets are supposed to meet at the Jefferson Motel.

title: Reuniting the Families
text: The four get into Sweet's Greenwood outside and make their way to the motel. Upon arriving, Sweet goes inside the motel by himself, and after a while a LSPD Police Maverick, callsign "Buzzard 1", appears. They interrupt the meeting and a shootout begins. Big Smoke and Ryder escape in Sweet's car just before the SWAT team arrives in their Enforcers, but Carl enters the motel to rescue Sweet. He makes his way through the hotel and eventually finds Sweet. When they arrive on the roof, Buzzard 1 reappears; Carl shoots down the helicopter, and follows Sweet. The four bail out of the car as it plunges onto the freeway into a Xoomer fuel tanker truck, causing a massive explosion. Believing the quartet have been killed in the explosion, the police call off the search and the mission is completed.

Sweet's Girl is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas.

title: Sweet's Girl
text: Carl Johnson drops by his brother's house. Upon arrival, however, he realises that nobody is home. Carl walks out of the house and receives a phone call from Sweet. Sweet informs Carl that he has been ambushed by Seville Boulevard Families gang members while visiting his girlfriend in Playa del Seville, and that they have surrounded his girlfriend's flat. Carl arrives at Sweet's girlfriend's flat, where he discovers that they are being attacked by five gunmen, two of them are armed with Tec-9s and the other three are carrying 9mm pistols. Sweet is firing back with his own pistol, but his ammunition is depleting quickly, prompting Carl to resolve the situation by killing the gang members. After killing the gang members, Sweet phones Carl again and tells him to acquire a four-door vehicle to drive Sweet and his girlfriend home.

Cleaning the Hood is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas.

The mission introduces the drugs aspect of the storyline, explaining how it has corrupted Los Santos.

title: Cleaning the Hood
text:
Ryder, Big Smoke, and Sweet are inside Sweet's house, talking about the crack cocaine epidemic in the city as CJ arrives. After an argument, Ryder and CJ decide to take care of business and deal with some of the crack dealers that supply the Grove Street gang members. They first go to visit B Dup and Big Bear in Ganton Courts, as CJ wants to recruit some of his old friends for assistance.

Upon arriving, B Dup angrily tells the two to stay away, with Big Bear working as his crack slave. Carl attempts to convince them to return to the Grove Street Families, but unfortunately fails to do so. Ryder and Carl both leave to fend off the dealers themselves, Ryder spots a crack dealer nearby selling drugs to one of the Grove Street gang members. They kill him, and Ryder recognizes the dealer, discovering the whereabouts of the dealer's place in the process.

Big Smoke is the second storyline mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, which protagonist Carl Johnson performs independently at the Johnson House in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas.

There is no gameplay during this mission, as it is simply formed by two cutscenes. The first begins automatically after completion of the first mission and the following mission is automatically triggered following the end of the second cutscene.

title: Big Smoke (mission)
text: Carl Johnson, after arriving in Grove Street, enters his childhood home and finds a photograph of his recently deceased mother, Beverly. He takes a chair and sits down, reminiscing on an occasion where his sister, Kendl threatened to tell Beverly about his antics. Big Smoke, an old friend of Carl's, enters the living room from the kitchen with a baseball bat and threatens to attack Carl, mistaking him for a burglar. He explains himself to Big Smoke and the two hug, exploding with love, relief, and pride. Carl and Big Smoke talk briefly about Beverly's death, with Smoke promising to help find her killer. They leave the house and drive to the cemetery in Vinewood in Smoke's Perennial.

title: Ryder (mission)
text: Ryder is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families member Lance "Ryder" Wilson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas.

title: Ryder (mission)
text: Carl drops by Ryder's house in Grove Street. Ryder does not seem that excited to see Carl back. Ryder explains that a local pizza store in Idlewood keeps painting over a Grove Street Families tag on the building, and he wants to "teach the owner a lesson". He asks Carl to come along, to which Carl agrees. The two get into Ryder's Picador and drive over to the barber shop. Carl asks if Old Reece still owns the shop, to which Ryder warns Carl not to get a haircut there, stating that Reece popped his membrane years ago. Despite Ryder's advice, Carl goes inside the barber shop and gets a new haircut. Afterwards, Carl goes back outside and Ryder comments on his new haircut.

Ryder tells Carl to go over to the pizza place across the street by standing from a quick sand and get them some food while he finishes smoking. After Carl orders the food, Ryder walks over to the counter with a gun and attempts to rob the premises. However, the clerk recognizes Ryder, and frightens Ryder and Carl off with a Shotgun. Carl and Ryder flee outside and get into Ryder's Picador. Carl and Ryder drive back to Ryder's house in Grove Street.

After returning to Grove Street, Ryder tells Carl to go over and see Sweet at his house to talk to him about the graffiti all across the hood.

The cutscene prop variant of the Pistol model seen in the cutscene is a , which differs from the in-game -inspired Pistol (a.k.a. the 9mm). title: Vertical Bird
text: This is the only storyline mission that takes place across each of the three major areas in the State of San Andreas. It starts at Madd Dogg's Crib (Los Santos), Carl steals the Hydra from the Easter Basin Naval Station (San Fierro), destroys spy ships in Tierra Robada and lands the jet at Verdant Meadows (near Las Venturas). The only mission that covers more distance is the second Beat the Cock! triathlon. It starts in Palomino Creek, traverses the countryside and requires the player to enter San Fierro, Bayside and Las Venturas properly, the latter two requiring a passage through the desert. The default radio station of the Washington is WCTR, but when Carl and Toreno enter Toreno's car, K-Rose is playing. In the beta, Carl would have to drive all the way to the boat, as depicted by unused mission failure messages (i.e. "Toreno's car is destroyed!").

On the aircraft carrier, three jets can be found initially. A fourth one lands later on, while one of the initial three departs. Destroying one of the remaining jets will lead to two Hydras pursuing CJ after stealing a Hydra, while destroying two will lead to just one Hydra pursuing CJ. The S.A.M. sites on the aircraft carrier are mission-exclusive, and will remain inactive out of the mission, regardless of whether they were deactivated or not by the player during the mission.

Carl goes to the Loco Low Co. garage in Willowfield. Once there, he meets a garage worker who gives him a Savanna equipped with hydraulics. The worker says he owed Sweet from way back. Doberman is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from the Ammu-Nation store in Market, Los Santos, San Andreas.

The mission serves as a tutorial for gang warfare and the assets income.

title: Doberman
text: Carl receives a phone call from Sweet who tells him to go to Ammu-Nation in Market to purchase firearms and kill a former Grove Street Families gang member who betrayed them and defected to the Ballas. The snitch is hiding in Glen Park. Carl purchases some weapons and heads to Glen Park. He then takes over Glen Park by surviving three waves of attacks from the Ballas. Carl then finds the snitch, emerging from his house, who claims that C.R.A.S.H. officer Frank Tenpenny set him up. Carl kills him and Glen Park now belongs to the Families.

The Ballas are holding a funeral for Little Weasel (who Carl and Big Smoke killed), and, according to Sweet, all of the Ballas OG's are going to be there. Just Business is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families member Melvin "Big Smoke" Harris from his home in Idlewood, Los Santos, San Andreas.

title: Just Business
text: Carl drops by Big Smoke's house and finds him in the garage. They agree to take a ride somewhere, as Smoke has business to take care of. They head to Commerce and Big Smoke enters the Atrium. After a brief moment, a shootout is heard inside, and Carl quickly rushes inside, protecting Smoke from attacking Russian Mafia goons. Once all of the Russians are killed, the two hop on a BF-400 and attempt to escape. Carl will use the Micro SMG with unlimited ammo and acts as the shooter, killing as many enemies as possible. On the way, they jump over the ramp of a Packer to escape a roadblock, causing all of the Russians there to be obliterated in a huge explosion, however the bike survives. After a long chase, Big Smoke rides through an alley in East Beach. The two have lost all the Russians, agreeing to split up.

When CJ and Big Smoke get onto the BF-400 to escape, the radio starts playing Radio X. The player's SMG weapon slot is replaced with a Micro SMG when the gunfight begins, and once again when the motorbike chase begins with one providing infinite ammo. Madd Dogg's Rhymes is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families affiliate and aspiring rapper Jeffrey "OG Loc" Cross from the Burger Shot he works at in the Marina, Los Santos, San Andreas.

The mission introduces the player to the ability of stealth kills.

title: Madd Dogg's Rhymes
text:
Carl recently stole a load of music equipment for OG Loc's album release party, but it seems that Loc can't rhyme if he doesn't have them to read off. Loc asks CJ to assist him in "borrowing" rhymes from famous rapper Madd Dogg.

Carl heads for Madd Dogg's Crib in Mulholland. He gains access, discovering that the home is heavily guarded by Madd Dogg's security. Nonetheless, Carl, unable to use his weapons apart from a knife, continues the infiltration and uses his stealth to make his way to the studio room, stealing the rhyme book. He exits the mansion in the safest way possible, and heads back to Burger Shot. Carl then meets OG Loc outside of the restaurant, giving him the rhyme book.

title: Madd Dogg's Rhymes
text:
In order to complete the mission the player must:

Madd Dogg's personal security are patrolling the mansion. 
Do not use any guns on your way to the rhyme book - you will alert them. Use stealth to steal the rhyme book.
Exit the mansion and get the rhyme book back to OG Loc. 
It's safe to use your weapons now, although it may be less risky if you use stealth to get past any guards on patrol.
The guards are using silenced guns. If you manage to obtain one it will allow you to fire a gun without being heard by nearby guards.

House Party is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families affiliate and aspiring rapper Jeffrey "OG Loc" Cross from his house in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas.

The first part of the mission starts at Burger Shot in Marina, and then the actual mission starts afterward. The mission can only be accessed between 20:00 and 6:00.

title: House Party
text: Carl goes to see OG Loc at Burger Shot in Marina and sees Loc angrily quitting his job as a janitor. As this violates the conditions of his parole, Loc tells Carl that he wants to have a big party before he goes back into prison, as it may be his last chance to "get heard". Loc tells Carl to get ready for the party and then to get some girls. Carl can then optionally get some new clothes and a haircut while waiting for the party to start.

Carl arrives at Loc's House to find him rapping his mediocre lyrics on a perfectly functioning mic. Carl sees Ryder there, and the pair go outside, away from the obnoxious sound of Loc's terrible music. Carl and Ryder bump into Sweet and other Grove Street members. title: High Noon
text: High Noon is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by C.R.A.S.H. officer Frank Tenpenny from Las Brujas ghost town in El Castillo del Diablo, Bone County, San Andreas.

title: High Noon
text: Carl is leaning against a post, waiting for Frank Tenpenny and his colleagues to arrive to retrieve the dossier Carl acquired. A Police Car approaches and C.R.A.S.H. emerges. Jimmy Hernandez points a gun at Carl, before Eddie Pulaski tells him to hand over the dossier. Carl hands over the dossier and asks if C.R.A.S.H. will leave him in peace now. Tenpenny asks Pulaski, who says Carl has "done well". Tenpenny then ambushes and knocks Hernandez out with a spade, accusing him of selling them out to Internal Affairs, informing them of the corrupt work Carl has performed for them. Tenpenny then orders Carl to dig the grave for Hernandez, implying that Carl will be digging his own grave as well. Tenpenny then leaves Pulaski alone to supervise Carl while he returns to Los Santos.

title: High Noon
text: As Carl digs the grave under the watchful eye of Pulaski, he tries to convince Pulaski that Tenpenny is using all of them and that Pulaski will be the next to be killed. Pulaski violently silences him, when suddenly Hernandez regains consciousness and tries to attack Pulaski, who turns around and shoots Hernandez, killing him, with his body falling down into the grave. Moments later, Pulaski attempts to flee in a Buffalo, but Carl chases him through the desert in a Bandito. During the chase Pulaski taunts Carl, insulting his sister and mother. At the end of the chase, Carl manages to incapacitate Pulaski, as Pulaski lies bleeding against his car as Carl approaches and asks him if he has any last requests. Pulaski responds that he wants to have sex with Carl's sister, Kendl.

title: Photo Opportunity
text: Carl receives a phone call from Cesar Vialpando. Cesar had been tracking a Ballas car, most likely travelling to San Fierro to acquire cocaine. Cesar wants Carl to come with him, so he makes his way to Cesar's location near Blueberry in Red County. The pair get in Cesar's Savanna and travel towards Angel Pine, where the car was last seen.

title: Photo Opportunity
text:
ear Blueberry in Red County. The pair get in Cesar's Savanna and travel towards Angel Pine, where the car was last seen.

After entering Angel Pine, Carl and Cesar position themselves on a rooftop overlooking a Cluckin' Bell restaurant. Carl whips out a camera and plans to take photographs, believing this to be a secret meeting. Soon afterwards, a brown Picador pulls up. Carl's former ally Ryder, along with a Ballas member step out of the vehicle. Another man arrives in a ZR-350. Cesar identifies him as T-Bone Mendez from the San Fierro Rifa. Shortly followed thereafter, is a mysterious man in a suit, arriving in a Washington. Then finally, a fourth man arrives in a Broadway, joining the others. He is identified as a pimp by Carl, but neither Cesar or Carl recognise him. After taking photos of all four men, Cesar and Carl leave Angel Pine, stopping by a filling station. Cesar drops Carl off, saying he'll meet him back at San Fierro.

text: The reward for this mission is an increase in respect. The mission Jizzy is unlocked. After the mission, the game will inform the player of the availability of Snapshots located around San Fierro.

title: Photo Opportunity
text: During development of the game, this mission had a completely different walkthrough. The player was originally tasked with stealing a helicopter to meet Cesar, and the photos would also have been taken whilst airborne. While watching over the meeting of the Loco Syndicate, Carl and Cesar shout to each other, presumably to make themselves heard over the sound of the helicopter's rotors, before the mission was changed without the dialogue being re-recorded. This is also evident when CJ states the mission "was some heavy shit", contrasting to the somewhat mundane car drive. Unused text strings in the american.gxt file reveal that the Ballas noticed Cesar tailing them and shot up his car, explaining why he had to stop and is seen checking the vehicle.

title: Photo Opportunity
text: e Ballas noticed Cesar tailing them and shot up his car, explaining why he had to stop and is seen checking the vehicle. The dialogue is left unused so the player can continue the trip by riding Cesar's (intact) red Savanna all the way to Angel Pine, instead of using the aforementioned helicopter to pick him up. A few lines were also cut, suggesting that CJ would have discovered Ryder's betrayal here and not in The Green Sabre, which can be seen . The Loco Syndicate's vehicles – Ryder's Picador, Jizzy's Broadway, Mike Toreno's Washington, and T-Bone Mendez's ZR-350 – are all-proof and can be obtained. CJ cannot look backwards while on the rooftop with the camera active. Sometimes, after the mission is passed, the player's camera may be able to take an infinite number of photos. After the camera is lost and reobtained, this no longer occurs.

title: Pimping
text: Pimping is a side mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas that consists of driving prostitutes to meet their clients. The mission can be triggered in any of the main cities in San Andreas while driving a Broadway, but not when in the countryside.

title: Pimping
text:
There are only two prostitutes who need to be driven around, and while there is a time limit similar to the Taxi Driver missions for dropping them off, there is no time limit for picking them up, which allows the player to repair the vehicle at a Pay 'n' Spray if necessary. It should be noted that if the player uses the Pay 'n' Spray during the mission then the first visit is free, though every subsequent visit will cost the normal $100.

After some sessions, the player may be required to either kill a client attacking the prostitute, or chase down a client who tries to escape without paying.

Rival gangs will not attack the player during pimping missions.

Completion of the pimping missions is required for 100% completion.

title: Pimping
text:
Upon collecting a prostitute after a successful session, she will give Carl a $300 cut of her fee. Each subsequent session will increase the multiplier for the player's cut, so after the second session the cut will double to $600, then triple to $900 after the third, with a cut of $3,000 awarded after the tenth session.

Once ten consecutive sessions have been completed, when Carl has sex with a prostitute, she will pay Carl instead.

If the player has to chase down a pimp, the reward table will not appear afterwards, and the reward will not be given to the player after the end of the session.

title: Pimping
text: The Pimping side mission was removed from the Japanese release of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas due to censorship, along with its requirement for attaining 100% completion.

Lure is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his apartment in Chinatown, San Fierro, San Andreas.

title: Lure (GTA San Andreas)
text: Ran Fa Li has gone to Woozie's apartment in Chinatown, but now the Da Nang Boys are after him and he can't get back home. The Triads are planning on how to lure the Da Nang Boys out of the way. Carl, meanwhile, offers himself to be a decoy to lure the Da Nang Boys to the countryside so that Ran Fa Li can get out of Chinatown safely.

Carl gets in a Rancher parked outside the apartment. He drives to the sawmill in Angel Pine, after which he looks out for the Da Nang Boys following him. Several of them eventually arrive on bikes and begin chasing Carl, thinking the car he is driving has Ran Fa Li inside. Carl traverses the heavily forested areas of Flint County and Whetstone. After a long ride, Carl stops at a gas station along the highway. Guppy later calls Carl, telling him that Woozie has taken Ran Fa Li to safety. The Da Nang Boys decide to return to Chinatown, realizing they've been tricked into chasing a decoy.

title: Outrider
text:
Outrider is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Loco Syndicate member Jizzy B. from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas.

This mission is marked as part of the San Fierro Triads mission strand.

title: Outrider
text:
Jizzy B. phones Carl and tells him, in a very suspiciously friendly tone, to get to a car in the Xoomer gas station at Easter Basin. T-Bone Mendez is waiting for Carl there.

He makes his way to the car and sees that nobody is there. As he gets in, T-Bone appears from the backseat and threatens to kill Carl, since he suspects him of working for someone else, and has another true purpose. Carl says he's only working for money, which prompts T-Bone to move the gun away from his face. Mike Toreno suddenly appears and asks if they are done. Since they are, they make their way to a drug shipment nearby.

Carl collects a sniper rifle, as well as a Rocket Launcher, and hops on a Sanchez. He then destroys the road blocks of Greenwoods created by the Da Nang Boys equipped with SMGs and AK47s. After all the four roadblocks are removed, he guards the shipment safely back to the crack factory in Doherty. Once there, Carl tells a San Fierro Rifa gang member to get the van out of sight, as cops will come snooping around real soon.

title: NRG-500 Challenge
text:
The mission is started by entering a parked NRG-500 at a dry dock in Easter Basin, San Fierro. The goal is to collect 18 floating coronas around the dry dock before the countdown timer runs out of time. The countdown timer starts at 10 seconds when the cutscene ends. Each corona will add 10 seconds to the timer. The reward for completing this mission is $1,000 and a step closer to 100%.

If Carl fails the challenge (either by running out of time, staying off the bike for too long after falling off, destroying the bike through damage or jumping into the water) he can try again once another NRG-500 spawns by the dry dock. Alternatively, after the completion or failure of the challenge, the player can keep the motorcycle on their own.

title: NRG-500 Challenge
text: If the player still has the bike after the challenge, they can, instead of leaving Easter Basin in order for the bike to respawn, park it again exactly where it normally spawns, get off, and then get on it again and the challenge will start again. This does not seem to work for the mobile ports of the game, however.

title: NRG-500 Challenge
text: It is possible to disable the timer by simply passing through a corona at the very last moment before the mission failure message appears. After that, the timer will disappear and give the player infinite time to complete this side mission. If the player falls off the bike, the 30-second rule to remount still applies, but the glitch itself will still be active.

title: NRG-500 Challenge
text: On the mobile port of the game, the challenge starts off with 15 seconds and each corona increases the timer by 15 seconds, possibly to make the challenge easier to complete.

title: Saint Mark's Bistro
text: Saint Mark's Bistro is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Leone Family Don Salvatore Leone from the Caligula's Palace, a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas. It is the final mission from the Caligula's casino.

title: Saint Mark's Bistro
text:
Carl comes to visit Salvatore Leone at the office in Caligula's Palace to find him and Maria throwing knives at a tied-up Maccer. Salvatore congratulates Carl on a job well done taking out a Forelli hit squad sent to kill Salvatore. In retaliation, Salvatore decides to send Carl to Marco's Bistro, one of the Forelli Family businesses, and assassinate Marco Forelli. Realizing the opportunity to free Paul, Maccer and Rosenberg, Carl asks Salvatore to let him take the three as back-up, to which Salvatore agrees, due to him thinking that Carl would kill them.

Upon exiting Caligula's Palace, Paul, Maccer and Rosenberg escape from Las Venturas, while Carl drives to the Las Venturas Airport and flies to Liberty City with a Shamal.

After some time, Carl is flying back to Las Venturas in the same Shamal he left in. As Carl lands on the runway in the Las Venturas Airport, the mission ends.

title: Saint Mark's Bistro
text: There never was a plan to include the whole of Liberty City afaik. It would have been a lot of work to get everything to work (trains, ambient peds, cars, weather) as well as adding snow to the whole map. We'd also need npc models for winter weather. Former Rockstar North Technical Director Obbe Vermeij debunking false claims about Liberty City being originally planned as an explorable area. Unused audio and text files remaining in the game files reveal that the high ranking Forelli Family member that Carl assassinates in this mission is Marco Forelli. Liberty City is technically an interior, designed to simulate an exterior look – this is why the sun, moon, and stars cannot be observed even when outside the bistro. It shares its interior world (Int 1) with the Doherty Garage's cutscene interior and is situated high above the end of Easter Bay Airport.

title: Pier 69 (mission)
text: Pier 69 is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triads from a rooftop across Pier 69 in Esplanade North, San Fierro, San Andreas.

title: Pier 69 (mission)
text: After finding out of the next meet between Big Smoke's lieutenant Ryder and the Loco Syndicate through killing Jizzy B., Carl calls Cesar to inform him of this. After Carl and Cesar meet up on a rooftop across from Pier 69, Carl gets there and uses a sniper rifle to gun down the San Fierro Rifa taking the guard over the pier, so that Mountain Cloud Boys acting as the backup can move in. T-Bone shows up with some Rifa in a Pony, as does Ryder with two Tahomas full of Ballas along with one riding shotgun in his Picador. The last to show up is Toreno who arrives by helicopter. Toreno sees the bodies on the rooftops and is red alerted, so Carl and Cesar fight their way through Pier 69 until they confront T-Bone. The two gun him down, then Ryder attempts to escape by a boat, but Carl chases him down and kills him in revenge for betraying the Grove Street Families.

title: Ice Cold Killa

Carl goes to his garage in Doherty looking for material to make a silenced 9mm; shortly, Cesar arrives and gives Carl his own silencer. Woozie has left a message about a Loco Syndicate meeting with the Ballas, and Carl has to kill Jizzy B. and take his phone in order to find out about where this meeting will take place.

Carl drives over to Jizzy's Pleasure Domes club at Battery Point and crashes Jizzy's party. After a brief argument and losing patience, Jizzy attempts to escape with a bodyguard, setting the other guards on Carl; Carl manages to kill them all and makes his way outside the club. Outside, Jizzy attempts to escape, and Carl gives chase, eventually killing him and taking his phone. Carl calls Cesar and tells him to come to Pier 69, the location of the meeting, where they'll take down the Loco Syndicate.

text: Dam and Blast is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Wu Zi Mu as part of plans to pull off a heist of Caligula's Palace from The Four Dragons Casino, a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas.

title: Dam and Blast
text: Carl, having successfully convinced Millie Perkins to date him in order to obtain her keycard, is now positioned to continue preparations for the heist on the main vault of Caligula's Palace. Some online walkthroughs for this mission, such as that posted on this website, indicate that Carl loses his weapons after parachuting out of the plane. title: Toreno's Last Flight
text:
Mike Toreno escaped death when Carl and Cesar Vialpando killed T-Bone Mendez and Ryder, but Wu Zi Mu has tracked Toreno down to a Maverick helicopter at the SFPD headquarters.

Carl drives to Downtown and sees Toreno's men guarding the Maverick. Carl kills Toreno's guards and as he approaches the Maverick, it takes off with Toreno on overboard. title: Key to Her Heart
text: Carl has just returned from the Las Venturas City Planning Department with the blueprints of Caligula's Palace, which he and Woozie intend to burglarize. The next step in his plans involves providing his team access to Caligula's restricted areas by wooing and gaining the trust of one of the casino's croupiers, Millie Perkins. He assures her that she will receive a generous cut of the purloined cash, and takes her security card back to The Four Dragons Casino in preparation for the next steps of the plan.

title: Architectural Espionage

Madd Dogg is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by rapper Madd Dogg from the Royal Casino, a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas.

title: Madd Dogg (mission)
text: Carl walks over to the south side of the casino, encountering two men encouraging someone on the casino roof to jump. One of them tells Carl that the person on the roof is Madd Dogg, a formerly successful rapper. Carl tells Madd Dogg not to jump, but Madd Dogg says his life doesn't mean anything anymore. He has lost everything, from his money to his fame, after his rhyme book was stolen and his manager was killed. Carl once again tries to make him reconsider jumping, but Madd Dogg ignores him. Two croupiers attempt to prevent Madd Dogg from jumping, but he tells them to stay away.

Carl, in an attempt to save Madd Dogg from suicide, steals a nearby Walton and parks near the casino. Madd Dogg jumps from the roof in a drunken state, landing on a pile of boxes. Carl then takes Madd Dogg to a rehabilitation center. On the way, Madd Dogg tells Carl that he is going to get a new manager once he is clean, and might consider Carl. Carl agrees. Carl arrives at the rehabilitation center, where two paramedics check Madd Dogg in. Carl drives off and the mission ends.

The mission is not required for 100% completion.

Fender Ketchup is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his office at The Four Dragons Casino, a casino located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas.

title: Fender Ketchup
text:
Carl pays a visit to Woozie, after inviting him to this new place. Woozie explains to him the problems he's having about the casino business. Apparently, either one of the three Mafia families in the city - the Leone Crime Family, the Forelli Crime Family and the Sindacco Crime Family - are causing the trouble for him, and would do anything to keep them away. Woozie then offers a deal to Carl; in exchange for some help with the casino business, Woozie would offer Carl a share of the casino. Carl gladly agrees.

A little later, a Triad comes in, saying that some Mafia thugs have been interrupting things, and that one of the thugs has been caught. Woozie orders him to get rid of the thug, but Carl has a better idea, namely having the thug tied up to a car, so he would deal with this a little later.

Deconstruction is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, which protagonist Carl Johnson performs independently at the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas.

title: Deconstruction
text:
Carl goes into the garage to check up on his new workforce, who are working on a Remington. Suddenly, an angry Kendl comes in and explains that construction workers from the construction site next to the garage have been harassing her. Cesar attempts to confront them, but Carl tells him he will sort it out, claiming he has been "thinking about getting new land anyway".

Carl goes to the nearby construction site in Doherty to try and deter the building company from getting on the bad side of the Johnson family. He destroys six portable houses while workers are trying to stop him. After the huts have been destroyed, the foreman appears from inside a portable toilet, witnesses the destruction, and heads back into the toilet. Carl uses a bulldozer to push the foreman's toilet into a ditch, then uses a cement mixer to fill the ditch with cement, burying the foreman alive under concrete.

If the player fails to destroy the portables or bury the foreman in time, the mission will fail and a two-star wanted level is attained, with the failure message saying "You took too long. The cops are on to you!"

title: Learning to Fly
text: Learning to Fly is a mission strand in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by government agent Mike Toreno from the Verdant Meadows Airfield in Bone County, San Andreas.

title: Learning to Fly
text: After purchasing the Verdant Meadows Airfield, Toreno informs Carl via a phone call that he will be taking flying lessons. Initially hesitant, Carl agrees to the task when Toreno states that this will help secure his brother's release from prison. Before ending the call, Toreno explains that the ten lessons Carl will be taking are accessible on a television set in the office of the safehouse.

title: Learning to Fly
text: Following this mission, a Rustler will always spawn in one of the hangars at the airfield (along with a Stuntplane if the tests were passed with at least a silver medal and a Hunter for all gold medals). Moreover, a Police Maverick will spawn on the roof of the Los Santos Police Headquarters, while a Raindance will spawn on Santa Maria Beach. The Hunter will also spawn at the Easter Basin Naval Station, but the player will get a five-star wanted level for entering the base. Completing the mission grants Carl his pilot's licence (it can be acquired by increasing the Flying Skill even before this mission), allowing him to enter any of San Andreas' airports via security gates and pilot any of the aircraft at the airports besides the Dodo and the Maverick, which were already accessible beforehand.

All Victim clothing stores in the state will also be unlocked. The six-star wanted level is now obtainable.

Black Project is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by pot-growing hippie The Truth from the Verdant Meadows Airfield in Bone County, San Andreas.

title: Black Project
text: Carl arrives at the airfield and is welcomed by The Truth, exercising on the top of an aircraft wreck. The Truth then berates Carl for having willfully worked for a government agent. He then tells Carl about a secret military research area, where he believes a "black project" is being developed. The Truth drops Carl off at the boundaries of the base before leaving.

Carl must sneak into the underground area, by using the control tower to open the blast doors and get inside. However, he has to do so before sunrise, and the area is heavily guarded with several soldiers patrolling the area, as well as many searchlights. If Carl manages to get into the control tower, he has a limited amount of time to reach the blast doors before they're closed again. If Carl stays in a searchlight for too long or destroys three of the searchlights, the blast doors will be isolated from the main system, forcing him to find another way to get inside, namely through a vent.

Carl steals it and flies towards Arco del Oeste, where The Truth is waiting in his van. text: When inside the Area 69 research area, various announcements tell the employees a variety of things including (but not limited to): "downloading pornography is strictly prohibited", "anyone caught stealing alien technology will not be invited to the next staff night out", and that "running with scissors is dangerous and not permitted". These announcements continue even after security notifies everyone of the breaches. The announcement made about running with scissors not being permitted is a possible reference to the video game company , best known for its Postal games, which are considered by some to be "GTA Clones". title: The Da Nang Thang
text:

The Da Nang Thang is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his apartment in Chinatown, San Fierro, San Andreas.

title: The Da Nang Thang
text:
Carl bumps into Woozie just as he is about to leave his apartment. Suddenly, Little Lion, a Triad gang member, calls Woozie and informs him of the Da Nang Boys having arrived on a freighter ship in the San Fierro Bay and having brought along some Vietnamese refugees who were locked in a container.

Carl rushes to the apartment's roof and meets Little Lion, who is about to fly towards the ship with his Maverick. Carl enters the helicopter and the two fly over to the ship in the middle of the bay. Carl, prepared for the attack, starts killing every Da Nang Boy he spots with a minigun with infinite ammunition and after a brief moment, one of the Da Nang Boys manages to shoot down the helicopter with a rocket launcher. Little Lion is killed while CJ survives the attack, but loses all his weapons, and some of his health, leaving him with only a knife.

title: The Da Nang Thang

Carl boards the ship and kills several Da Nang Boys, continuing his way around until he finds the prisoners and frees them. One of the refugees tells him where The Snakehead, the Da Nang Boys' leader, is located in ship. Carl makes his way to the Snakehead, killing all enemies in the way. During the fight, Carl kills the Snakehead and then meets up with the refugees. They lower some Dinghies into the water and escape after gratefully thanking Carl for everything he did, leaving Carl alone on a Dinghy.

Despite being a C.R.A.S.H. mission, it is labelled as an independent mission from Carl, marked with a "CJ" icon.

title: N.O.E.
text:
We got a problem. I got some guys out in the field need some equipment. If they don't get it, they'll be dead by nightfall. 
N.O.E. is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by government agent Mike Toreno from the Verdant Meadows Airfield in Bone County, San Andreas.

title: N.O.E.
text: Carl arrives at the airstrip, waiting for Toreno. Not long after, Toreno sneaks up behind Carl and grabs him in a chokehold. After Toreno lets Carl go and tells him to "wake up and smell the coffee", he explains that his agents are in trouble and they need some equipment delivered to them; the agents need the package by nightfall otherwise they will all be dead. Carl, after a little reluctance and confusion regarding the situation, proceeds to the task.

title: N.O.E.
text:

Carl gets in a Rustler with the package attached to the fuselage. Carl takes off, with Toreno reminding Carl to stay under the radar, i.e. stay low, close to the surface, so that he will not be detected. Carl flies across the state to Angel Pine, where he releases the contraband at a drop-off point. Carl then makes his way back to Verdant Meadows, again while flying under the radar. Carl arrives at the airstrip, with Toreno congratulating him for a job well done.

title: N.O.E.
text:
In order to complete the mission the player must:
The plane is all loaded up and ready to go. Get in it
Fly to Angel Pine with the package. Stay below the radar, or you'll be chased by Hydras of the U.S. Air Force.
Fly into the corona to trigger the drop
Return to the airfield and land, but get below the radar
Bring the plane to a stop anywhere on the landing strip

title: N.O.E.
text: The reward for completing the mission is $15,000 and the mission Stowaway is unlocked.

title: N.O.E.
text:
N.O.E. stands for "", a type of very low altitude flight course used by military aircraft to avoid enemy detection and attack in a high-threat environment. If Carl flies too high and becomes visible on the radar, Toreno may say, "Nap of the earth, Carl. Nap of the earth."
During the mission, Mike Toreno states "If you did as many amphetamines as [the U.S. Air Force] does, you'd be lucky not to shoot anything that moves." This is a reference to , an amphetamine administered to pilots as "go pills" during the , which was eventually blamed for a February 1991 friendly fire incident.
It could also be a reference to the , for which Dexedrine was also blamed. While anachronistic for the game's setting by a decade, the incident would have been a relevant topic during its development.

title: N.O.E.
text:
If the player flies close to/over Area 69 or too high at any point during the mission, a warning will appear: "DANGER: Restricted air space!". If the player does not change their course, two Hydras will be sent to take them down.
The Hydras in this mission are piloted by civilians, namely by HMORI pedestrians, and not by the military.

Breaking the Bank at Caligula's is the final heist mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by San Fierro Triads leader Wu Zi Mu from The Four Dragons Casino, located along The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas.

Carl arrives at The Four Dragons Casino, dressed as a Caligula's employee, to meet Woozie and the crew in preparation for the heist. The team get into a Securicar and head towards Caligula's Palace, whilst Carl makes his own way there. On the way, Zero asks Carl if he can hear him on his earpiece, with Carl replying that he can.

Carl enters the casino and uses Millie's swipe card to gain access to the lower floors of the casino. Carl heads into the generator room, where he throws a tear gas canister into an air vent, which lands outside the safe and knocks out two security guards.

title: Snail Trail
text: Snail Trail is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by C.R.A.S.H. officers Frank Tenpenny and Eddie Pulaski from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas.

title: Snail Trail
text: Carl enters the garage and is greeted by Jethro. He says that some cops are looking for him in the office. Carl realizes that it is Frank Tenpenny and Eddie Pulaski. He is welcomed by them, and they ask him how things are going, and how his brother is doing. Later on, they order Carl to kill a young journalist, who is apparently investigating Pulaski. Pulaski also tells Carl to kill another journalist who is supposedly going to meet the young journalist at the end of Yacht Harbor in Santa Maria Beach, Los Santos.

title: Exports and Imports
text: Exports and Imports are a series of side missions in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, which becomes available after the Customs Fast Track mission for Cesar Vialpando. Similarly to Grand Theft Auto III s Import/Export feature, Exports and Imports consists of a series of vehicle deliveries for money, as well as the ability to purchase any of the vehicles delivered.

title: Exports and Imports
text: To "export" or sell a vehicle, the player must obtain a "wanted" vehicle (as shown when the player is told via an on-screen message: "You can export this vehicle over at Easter Basin Docks.") and take it to a specific marker on a cargo ship in Easter Basin, San Fierro, where it can be lifted in place via a magnetic dockside crane, or simply driven up a ramp linking the dock to the deck of the ship if the vehicle is compact enough to be driven onto the ship. Once the vehicle is in contact of the marker (and released from the crane magnet, if lifted using the crane), a message will show up that the player has successfully exported that vehicle. The player will then receive money depending on the type and condition of the vehicle.

title: Exports and Imports
text:

To "import" or buy a vehicle, the player simply needs to walk up to the board in Easter Basin and select which vehicle they would like to import. Vehicles are only unlocked for importing after they have been successfully exported. The player can only import certain selections of vehicles depending on the day of the week, the lists being based mainly on the order in which the player had exported them.

Exporting all 30 wanted vehicles is a requirement for 100% completion.

title: Exports and Imports
text:
Each wanted list consists of ten different vehicles needed for export, ranging from motorbikes and regular sedans to off-roaders and sports cars.

Players have the option of either plucking a vehicle that spawns normally in traffic or any parking space, or locating one specifically spawned in one spot when the vehicle is being requested on the list. Note that vehicles will only spawn at certain locations if it is currently on a list; for example, the Euros will only spawn at The Camel's Toe if the player is on the third wanted list and has not exported a Euros already.

Wanted vehicles that are specifically spawned usually have custom license plates.

title: First Date (GTA San Andreas)
text: First Date is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the yet not introduced Cesar Vialpando's mysterious cousin Catalina from The Welcome Pump bar in the town of Dillimore in Red County, San Andreas.

title: First Date (GTA San Andreas)
text: Catalina is inside The Welcome Pump in Dillimore and is threatening two men with a knife. Carl enters the room and explains to her that he is looking for a friend's cousin, who he discovers is Catalina. The two leave The Welcome Pump and Catalina explains to Carl that they are going to rob four locations across the county: a Gasso petrol station, an Inside Track betting shop, a liquor store and a bank.

title: First Date (GTA San Andreas)
text: There is no monetary reward for completing the mission, which is technically a cutscene; the only thing Carl needs to do is arrive with (or obtain afterward) a vehicle. The missions Tanker Commander, Against All Odds, Local Liquor Store and Small Town Bank are unlocked. However, after completing the chosen mission, the other three missions need unlocking once again. Upon completion of the first job, The Truth will also invite Carl by phone to meet him at a motel in Angel Pine.

title: First Date (GTA San Andreas)

Carl tells Catalina that he's a "God fearing man" hinting he believes in God.
There are unique dialogues from Catalina if the player chooses to do any robbery mission for the first date besides Tanker Commander. Because the other robberies all require the player to return to Catalina's Hideout when the job is done, Catalina will tell Carl about her hideout in Fern Ridge and then tell him how to get there. title: Tanker Commander
text: This is one of the several missions in the game that will not work correctly if too many cheats are activated. On rare occasions, a car or truck can crash into the gas pumps as the player approaches them and activates the cutscene, causing the gas station to explode during the cutscene, thus killing Catalina, failing the mission and giving the player a two-star wanted level. It is unknown what causes this situation to happen, but it is most likely a glitch. The bulletproof glass at the gas station is manufactured by Max Pane, an obvious reference to the Max Payne series made by Rockstar. If the player manages to enter the gas station interior and kill both employees, entering the Tanker will cause the game to crash. Near the beginning, when CJ and Catalina run to the truck to steal it, run towards Catalina and she will stay where she is, and start shooting CJ.

title: Don Peyote
text: Don Peyote is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by The Truth via phone call from outside The Four Dragons Casino on The Strip in Las Venturas, San Andreas.

title: Don Peyote
text:
Carl receives an unexpected phone call from The Truth. Apparently, he, a band and their manager went on a " safari" in the desert a few nights earlier. He tells Carl that he has woken up in Los Santos, not knowing how he got there, and he doesn't know what happened to the others. So, he asks Carl to travel to Arco del Oeste and make sure they are still alive.

Carl gets a vehicle and heads out to Bone County. Once atop Arco del Oeste, he starts looking for the band, and finds their frontman, Maccer, and manager Kent Paul. Maccer explains that they passed out from the drugs, while Carl offers them a ride to town. Kent Paul tells Carl to take them to Caligula's Palace in Las Venturas where his friend, Ken Rosenberg, works.

Carl, Maccer and Paul get into Carl's vehicle and begin to drive back to Las Venturas. Carl and Paul ask where the other members of the band are, to which Maccer replies that he remembers "snakes", so Carl drives them to the Snake Farm west of Verdant Meadows. Once there, the snake farmers notice Maccer and Paul, who were involved with the group. Angered by this, the group point guns at the trio. Carl can kill them or simply escape, before driving Paul and Maccer to Caligula's Casino on The Strip.

If the farmers are left alive, they will aggressively pursue the trio all the way to Las Venturas. Once Carl reaches the casino, the farmers will catch up and a fistfight will ensue between both parties. All the farmers must then be killed in order to complete the mission.

Paul asks Carl to give them some space, and that he will call Carl later. Carl leaves the office and the mission is complete.

Outside the casino, Carl calls Wu Zi Mu and explains that he has found a way to survey Caligula's Casino for the heist in a manner which will not cause suspicion. Carl asks Woozie to meet him soon.

text: Retrying this mission after failing it allows skipping to the scene where Carl finds Paul and Maccer. The introduction cutscene for this mission is a reference to 's 1991 biopic about , and particularly its frontman . The Truth's voice on the phone bears a resemblance to Morrison, and he also mentions "communing with 'The Lizard King'", which was one of Morrison's nicknames. title: Mike Toreno (mission)
text: Mike Toreno is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Loco Syndicate member Jizzy B. from his gentlemen's club Jizzy's Pleasure Domes in Battery Point, San Fierro, San Andreas.

title: Mike Toreno (mission)
text: T-Bone is convinced that the Loco Syndicate are being monitored. At that point, Mike Toreno calls T-Bone and explains that he is in danger and needs assistance. T-Bone informs Carl and Jizzy that the van containing the drug shipment has been stolen with Toreno still inside. Toreno informs T-Bone that his phone battery is running low, and he will provide directions until it runs out. Carl drives T-Bone to the locations given by Toreno, and finally locates the van at Easter Bay Airport; there are three possible locations inside the airport for the van to be found.

title: Mike Toreno (mission)

ly locates the van at Easter Bay Airport; there are three possible locations inside the airport for the van to be found.

Guided by Toreno's now-working transponder, Carl and T-Bone locate the van and rescue Toreno from the Da Nang Boys. Toreno exits the van and, not knowing Carl, holds him at gunpoint, though stands down when T-Bone explains who he is. Toreno explains that the police will be searching for the van and they must destroy the van with the shipment inside, despite T-Bone's reluctance to do so. Carl destroys the van and drives Toreno and T-Bone away from the airport. After losing the police, Carl drives Toreno and T-Bone back to Jizzy's club.

title: Wear Flowers in Your Hair
text: Wear Flowers in Your Hair is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, which protagonist Carl Johnson performs with the assistance of The Truth. It is started from the gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas.

title: Wear Flowers in Your Hair
text: Carl, Cesar, Kendl and The Truth enter the garage in San Fierro. Carl is furious that Claude gave him a run-down, long-closed Xoomer gas station instead of a pink slip when he won the race. It clearly isn't a garage, but Kendl is determined to turn it into something profitable. It would take a lot of hard work, but she manages to persuade Carl and they decide to give it a try. She also says if Carl is going to make over the garage, he'll need a few workers. The Truth knows of a few acquaintances who can help convert the garage into a successful chop shop and has Carl drive to specific locations in the city to meet them.

title: Wear Flowers in Your Hair
text: Carl and The Truth first go meet Jethro at a gas station in Easter Basin. After Jethro gets in, The Truth asks Carl to make a few seemingly random stops to monitor the activities of some mysterious vans. One of the stops he asks Carl to make is directly in front of San Fierro Medical Center, where The Truth admonishes the other passengers to "think about a yellow rubber duck" as a van emerges from the hospital's car park. Without explanation, The Truth urges Carl on to the next stop, which is in King's, where Dwaine is found working from his Hotdog van like French fries truck. Then, The Truth asks Carl to go to the San Fierro Police Headquarters to see the van again. Lastly, he asks Carl to pick up Zero in front of his shop. Afterwards, the four return to the Doherty garage together, with Dwaine already there.

title: Wear Flowers in Your Hair
text: In this mission, the game uses unused police and hospital radar blips that were removed from the game's map but are still in the game files. They are only used during this mission. If Zero is killed while sitting on the bench, he will drop a Detonator. This was intentional, as the game developers wanted it to look like he was holding a remote control for the RC Raider. Since no remote control model exists in the game, the only other device to closely resemble a remote control is a detonator. Moreover, Zero is non-solid when he is sitting on the bench, and the player can walk into or through him. The RC Raider is all-proof, and can be obtained by stomping on it with a parachute (one can get up to its position by jumping on top of a car that was driven up the ramp of a Packer).

Excuse me, but I never take drugs. We all know drugs are for losers, and/or sex maniacs. And right now, sex is the last thing on my mind. 
Air Raid is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by electronics expert Zero from his store in Garcia, San Fierro, San Andreas. It is available after purchasing the store for $30,000.

This mission is not mandatory to progress the storyline, but still necessary to achieve 100% game completion.

title: Air Raid
text:
CJ drops by his newly acquired business, Zero RC, and greets a distraught Zero, who's just discovered that his arch-enemy Berkley has returned to town. Whilst telling CJ about his past with Berkley, Zero notices that Berkley has just launched a 'full-scale attack' on Zero RC's rooftop. CJ and Zero head to the roof, where they find Berkley's RC Barons trying to attack the transmitters. Zero instructs Carl to use a mounted minigun (with infinite ammo) to destroy the attacking planes, explaining that he needs the transmitters in one piece so he will be able to launch a counterattack.

Once the attack is successfully thwarted, Zero thanks Carl for the help, telling him that he will prepare for the counterattack soon.

title: Supply Lines...
text:
Berkley has his sycophantic lackeys do all his deliveries. Well, we shall hit him where it hurts the most! Bring his mail order model business to its knees! 
Supply Lines... is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by electronics expert Zero from his store in Garcia, San Fierro, San Andreas.

title: Supply Lines...
text:
CJ enters the shop, looking for Zero and ignoring his plea to leave him alone. CJ enters the back room of the shop, still looking for Zero, and finds him hanging by his underwear in a closet. Zero explains that Berkley humiliated him and that he is in a lot of pain. CJ suggests that he take revenge, so he asks what kind of weapons Zero has. Zero says that he has a miniature plane, and CJ suggests using the plane to humiliate Berkley.

Zero suggests that the two destroy Berkley's delivery service fleet. CJ then takes control of the plane, maneuvering it to different parts of San Fierro in order to kill the couriers before they make their deliveries. He kills five sets of Berkley's delivery personnel, all while watching the fuel of the plane, and flies the plane back to the roof of Zero's shop.

title: Supply Lines...
text:
Zero's quote, "The smell, you know that ozone smell smells like...victory!" is a reference to the movie , specifically to Bill Kilgore's well-known quote "The smell, you know that gasoline smell, the whole hill. Smelled like... victory."
The original version of the mission was so difficult that the actor of Zero (David Cross) hated the mission and said that he "couldn't fucking do it".
Zero and this mission are referenced during a break on the Kult FM radio station in GTA Online, by DJ Zachary, who is also voiced by David Cross.

The plane is everything but bullet-proof, as it is totally unfazed even if there are multiple explosions/flames/crashes. If the plane flips over, it will revert the flip without taking any damage from it. If the plane is destroyed by gunfire or crashes, Zero can be heard shouting "NOOOOOOOOOOOO!" as the mission fails. If the plane runs out of fuel or self-destructs, Zero can be heard saying "My humiliation... is complete." as the mission fails.

New Model Army is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by electronics expert Zero from his store in Garcia, San Fierro, San Andreas.

title: New Model Army
text: Zero and Berkley have planned a showdown, the loser of which must leave San Fierro for good. The battle takes place inside the RC Battle Ground. To win, Zero must navigate across the area and safely get his RC Bandit into Berkley's compound. However, Berkley controls an RC Goblin, using it to drop debris on the path leading to the compound, blocking Zero's route along the way. Carl, also controlling an RC Goblin, must help Zero win by removing any obstructions in his way. He must also destroy any tanks that could be potential hazards to the Bandit. After negotiating the various obstacles planted in his path, Zero drives his Bandit into Berkley's compound, thus defeating Berkley and forcing him to leave San Fierro.

title: New Model Army
text: The player is controlling an RC Goblin, and must remove objects to clear Zero's route within eight minutes. Zero has three RC Goblins in reserve, so if one is destroyed, he will spawn in another at his compound for the player. The Bandit's health level appears on-screen. Begin by removing the first barrel in Zero's way - just drop it in the "river". Zero will drive to a gap in the way and request a bridge. However, if a plank is dropped over the gap, Zero will drive directly into the firing range of one of Berkley's three RC Tigers. Therefore, a better alternative is to leave Zero's Bandit at the gap and destroy the three tanks - one is directly ahead along the path, the second is near the second gap, and the third is directly outside Berkley's base. If time permits, drop a bomb on Berkley's Goblin to stop the influx of barrels.
