title: Amphibious Assault (GTA San Andreas)
text: Amphibious Assault is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his apartment in Chinatown, San Fierro, San Andreas. This mission can only be triggered between 20:00 and 6:00.

title: Amphibious Assault (GTA San Andreas)
text:
Carl meets Wu Zi Mu at his apartment in Chinatown. Woozie explains that he plans to plant a bug on a Da Nang Boys-owned ship in San Fierro Bay. Woozie asks Carl to do this, but Carl is reluctant to do so because of an experience he had (getting a condom stuck to his face) whilst swimming as a child. Woozie later admits to Carl that he cannot do it because he is blind. Carl, sympathizing with Woozie, has a change of heart and agrees to the task.

However, if the player's lung capacity is insufficient before starting the mission, a special cutscene will be triggered. While playing on the CJD 500, Woozie asks Carl if he can swim well, to which Carl replies negatively. The game would then tell the player to improve their lung capacity by diving underwater for the mission to be continued.

title: Amphibious Assault (GTA San Andreas)

Carl makes his way to Esplanade North, near Pier 69. Once there, he dives into the water. He first navigates through a rock formation. Afterward, he sees and avoids the Da Nang Boys patrolling the ship and the sea in Tropics. He also avoids the search lights planted on the tanker. As he arrives at the freighter, he quietly makes his way to the back of the ship, either by avoiding the guards' attention or by killing them. He eventually arrives at the back of the ship, and plants the bug. After planting the bug, Carl leaves the ship quietly and swims back to the dock on Esplanade North.

title: Cut Throat Business
text: Cut Throat Business is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by rapper Madd Dogg from his mansion in Mulholland, Los Santos, San Andreas.

title: Cut Throat Business
text: Carl arrives at the mansion to find Madd Dogg back in the studio and ready to make his comeback. On TV, rival rapper OG Loc is holding a press conference and music video shoot. After listening carefully Madd Dogg realizes that the rhymes by OG Loc are actually from his rhyme book, which was stolen by Carl for OG Loc a long time ago. Carl and Madd Dogg both agree to drop-in unannounced and make a "cameo appearance" in the middle of Loc's video.

title: Cut Throat Business
text: As the two arrive at the shoot, OG Loc is being interviewed. When he sees the two, he attempts to escape in a Vortex. Carl and Madd Dogg take the two other hovercrafts and give chase by Los Santos race. In Verona Beach, Loc gets off his Vortex and switches to a go-kart. Carl and Madd Dogg again take the two other Go-Karts and continue chasing Loc through Los Santos. The chase comes to an end as Loc attempts to escape into the Blastin' Fools Records Building in Market. Madd Dogg and Carl confront Loc, who initially denies the theft but then attempts to buy their silence. Jimmy Silverman, one of the executives of the record company, overhears the conversation and offers to sign Madd Dogg to the record label and sue Loc. Loc is sent to go get them all some lunch; his career is now over. During the physical confrontation between Loc and Madd Dogg, Loc accidentally drops the rhyme book.

Small Town Bank is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Catalina from outside the bank in Palomino Creek, Red County, San Andreas.

title: Small Town Bank
text: Carl and Catalina are planning on robbing the Palomino Creek Bank. They get into a vehicle and head off to their destination. Once they arrive, Catalina gives Carl a Pump Shotgun and tells him to make sure none of the employees lowers their hands, as they will set the alarm off. This triggers a cutscene, showing two deputies leaving the doughnut shop, hopping into their Ranger, and driving to the bank, surrounding it with some other deputies that arrive on HPV1000s.

text:
Listen, out here we like to race for cash or pink slips. Racer's choice. Now get your car started. We're about to go. Good luck, Carl Johnson. 
Wu Zi Mu is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Varrios Los Aztecas leader Cesar Vialpando from an area just south of the town of Montgomery in Red County, San Andreas.

title: Wu Zi Mu (mission)
text:
Carl is waiting for Cesar in the meeting place, who is apparently late for a race. Later on, Cesar arrives, who explains that he is late because he did not know when the race would start. Later, the organizer of the race, Wu Zi Mu (a.k.a. "Woozie"), arrives. He introduces himself to Carl, and tells him that the races here a high stakes, and they may reward the winner with cash or a pink slip. Later on, Carl hops on to his vehicle of choice, and goes to the starting point.

Then, the race begins, with Carl and Woozie participating. They race through different parts of Red County, like in Blueberry and in Blueberry Acres. Then, Carl manages to get to the finish line in The Panopticon first, after Carl wins the race, Woozie congratulates him and makes an offer of partnership if he goes to San Fierro. Both disperse when they hear the police sirens.

title: Wu Zi Mu (mission)
text:
The reward for this mission is $5,000. If Made in Heaven is also completed, the mission Farewell, My Love... is unlocked.

The race may be later replayed under the name Badlands A, as part of the Los Santos Race Tournaments, which can be accessed in Little Mexico after the completion of Verdant Meadows (Back to School in mobile versions and The Definitive Edition) later in the game. Although completion of these races is mandatory for 100% completion (and for the $1 million award), since Carl has already completed the race here, he does not need to do it again, except to improve his time (which has no bearing on completion of the tournament).

title: Wu Zi Mu (mission)
text:
Despite Cesar calling Carl to tell him to meet him and Kendl, the latter does not physically appear in the mission.
Claude, the protagonist of Grand Theft Auto III, can be seen in the background during the opening cutscene.
The song playing during the opening cutscene is "" by . This song can also be heard on the in-game radio station K-DST.
No matter which vehicle the player chooses at the beginning of the mission, Carl is seen with a ZR-350 during the ending cutscene. The ZR-350 is also the car Carl uses in the next mission.
Although Woozie drives a pink bullet-proof, fire-proof, explosion-proof and melee-proof Fortune during the mission, he is seen with a Bravura during the ending cutscene.
Upon reaching The Panopticon, a Walton driven by an Elvis impersonator can be seen going past Carl.

title: Riot (GTA San Andreas)
text: Frank Tenpenny, along with Eddie Pulaski, has finally been charged with racketeering, corruption, narcotics and sexual assault. The whole gang, composed of Carl, Cesar, The Truth, Kendl, Maccer, Sweet and Madd Dogg, are gathered in Dogg's living room, watching the news coverage of the trial. Whilst the reported is being aired, Sweet claims that Tenpenny will get 20 years, but Cesar disagrees, claiming that police officers usually get off lightly in the justice system. In the background, the report mentions retracted witness statements and the disappearance of officer Jimmy Hernandez and Pulaski, who is believed to be on the run.

title: Riot (GTA San Andreas)

acted witness statements and the disappearance of officer Jimmy Hernandez and Pulaski, who is believed to be on the run. A few moments later, the reporters exit the courtroom and Tenpenny's lawyer reads out a statement revealing that the district attorney has cleared Tenpenny of all charges due to a lack of evidence, essentially allowing Tenpenny to walk away a free man and to continue his unlawful actions with the support of the LSPD behind him.

Tenpenny's acquittal causes public outrage and the city erupts into rioting. Sweet is determined that there will be no rioting in Grove Street and asks Carl to take him back. Carl and Sweet drive through Los Santos, avoiding the rioting that has erupted around them. Once back in Grove Street, Sweet plans to "lock down the hood", while Carl says he is going to explore the city and see what is going on.

title: Courier
text:
The mission is a package delivery side-mission, serving as a spiritual successor to the Pizza Boy Mission in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. The side-mission strand offers assets which generate money periodically for the player to collect at each location where the mission is available – one business in each of the three cities.

The mission is activated by getting on a particular two-wheeled vehicle parked outside a specified outlet. A time limit is given to deliver packages in the form of a bag of white powder to designated places all over the city by throwing packages through coronas (by viewing sideways, as with drive-by shooting).

title: Courier
text:
signated places all over the city by throwing packages through coronas (by viewing sideways, as with drive-by shooting).

If a package is thrown incorrectly, it can be retrieved by collecting it on foot or in a vehicle. If a package is thrown while another is on the ground, the previously thrown package will despawn and can no longer be retrieved for the rest of the level. Getting off the vehicle for any reason activates a 20-second timer during which the player has to get back onto the vehicle.

title: Courier

ing off the vehicle for any reason activates a 20-second timer during which the player has to get back onto the vehicle.

Once all the packages have been delivered, the player must return to the outlet to collect a commission, with the amount of money paid based on the number of remaining packages and the amount of time left. At the start of the next level, new destination coronas appear. The number of destinations and the distances between them increases over the four levels. With the exception of the San Fierro Courier Run, the third level of each run consists of delivering packages to locations from the two previous levels in a single run.

Upon completing Level 4, the business becomes an asset that generates income continuously. The player can collect the income by standing in the dollar marker located in front of the business. The vehicles used for these asset missions remain available even after the mission itself is completed, allowing the player to replay the mission for extra cash.

Mountain Cloud Boys is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his apartment in Chinatown, San Fierro, San Andreas.

title: Mountain Cloud Boys (mission)
text: Carl arrives at Woozie's apartment and is led upstairs by a bodyguard, a Triad, who informs Carl that Woozie is actually blind and blessed with unbelievable good fortune. Woozie "reintroduces" himself to Carl and says that he needs to meet a Triad who missed a meeting last time. Carl and Woozie drive over to the storehouse where the missing Triad is found. Upon arriving, Woozie becomes suspicious when he discovers the gate to the courtyard is open, as it is usually locked. They walk further and Woozie bumps into the body of a dead Triad, with several burning vehicles around him. The door to a garage opens and the meeting mediator inside informs Woozie that the Da Nang Boys have wiped out the Blood Feather Triads, just as more of them arrive at the alleyway.

Woozie destroys both the cars and Carl drives him back to his apartment.

text: On the PC version of the game, a glitch may occur in this mission if the player is not using the frame limiter. When Carl and Woozie arrive at the warehouse, both exit the car, but Carl will not move. This can be fixed by reloading a previous save and turning on the frame limiter before starting the mission. Alternatively, the glitch can be avoided if the player stops and exits the car before reaching the red circle and then simply walks into it. In The Definitive Edition of the game, when entering the alley with Woozie, a fleeing pedestrian may say something to Carl. If Carl responds positively, Woozie will stop running forward. title: Up, Up and Away!
text:
Up, Up, and Away! is the second to last mission in the heist strand given to Carl Johnson by Wu Zi Mu in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

This mission can only be attempted between 20:00 and 6:00.

title: Up, Up and Away!
text: Carl recently seized four HPV1000 Police motorcycles to be used as outriders to escort the armored van Carl plans to use to haul the off the cash. His last step would be to somehow obtain an armored van and respray it with the Caligula's Casino logo, but he makes up his mind that he won't raise suspicion to his team by doing a simple carjacking. Zero gives him the idea to hijack a 'sky crane,' called a Leviathan. Carl heads over to K.A.C.C. Military Aviation Fuel Depot, the fuel depot in Spinybed, northeast Las Venturas. CJ penetrates the compound while keeping soldiers armed with M4s at bay. Carl takes down a pair of Hunters using a gun emplacement with unlimited ammo, before lifting off with the Leviathan. He heads to the depot, and using the magnetic winch attached to the helicopter, lifts an armored van and airlifts it to the airstrip in Verdant Meadows.

Land the helicopter in the indicated zone

Both the above solutions will result in Carl getting into a firefight and having to pass through a warehouse to get to the helicopter. A third option is to head to Verdant Meadows, get the jetpack, and fly to the helipad. There will be attacks by RPGs and soldiers on the helipad. however, if one lands in the roof of the warehouse, it's possible to take them out with a Sniper Rifle. This method also has the disadvantage of not indicating where the gun emplacements are located. However, if the player is carrying a minigun, the two enemy helicopters can be destroyed easily and the helicopter taken.

Once the car has been found, security appears. Carl kills three waves of security, and takes Cesar and the car back to the garage.

title: Trucking
text:
The missions become available after completing Catalina's mission, Tanker Commander, which features Mr. Whittaker, an employee at the RS Haul Depot in Flint County, just west of Los Santos and north of Helena Wankstein's Farm. After that, there should be a red marker within the depot compound. To start a trucking mission, simply walk into the marker.

The missions consist of either delivering cargo within a time limit, delivering a fragile cargo without damaging it, or delivering an illegal cargo whilst being pursued by the police with a wanted level of either three or four stars. Throughout the mission, the player cannot repair the truck cab or the trailer in any way. This can especially be observed during the fragile cargo missions, where there is no way to reset the damage meter.

If the player fails the mission, the wanted level will stay with the player, but they can now use police bribes and spray shops, while passing the mission will automatically remove their wanted level.

they can now use police bribes and spray shops, while passing the mission will automatically remove their wanted level.

The successive missions are increasingly difficult, with tighter time limits, more fragile cargo, or stronger police attention, while also covering a larger area of land to reach the destination. Leaving the cab or detaching the trailer for too long, or destroying the truck will result in mission failure. It is noteworthy that the last two missions cannot be started until the player completes Yay Ka-Boom-Boom, which is necessary to unlock access to Las Venturas.

Upon completion of all eight Trucking missions, the RS Haul Depot becomes an asset for Carl Johnson. The business generates a maximum of $2,000 in revenue.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text:
Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas 
 Five years ago Carl Johnson escaped from the pressures of life in Los Santos, San Andreas — a city tearing itself apart with gang trouble, drugs, and corruption. Where film stars and millionaires do their best to avoid the dealers and gangbangers. Now, it's the early '90s. Carl's got to go home. His mother has been murdered, his family has fallen apart and his childhood friends are all heading toward disaster. On his return to the neighborhood, a couple of corrupt cops frame him for homicide. CJ is forced on a journey that takes him across the entire state of San Andreas, to save his family and to take control of the streets.

text:

Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas (also referred to as GTA San Andreas, GTA SA or simply San Andreas) is a Rockstar North-developed video game released on 26th October 2004 by Rockstar Games, and is the seventh title in the and the third game in the of the series. It is the sequel to Grand Theft Auto: Vice City and the prequel to GTA Liberty City Stories and Grand Theft Auto III. It was released on the same date as . GTA San Andreas is set in the fictional state of San Andreas.

On November 11, 2021, the game was re-released on 8th and 9th generation consoles in honor of Grand Theft Auto III s 20-year anniversary under the title Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas - The Definitive Edition, included in The Definitive Edition bundle.

text:
Plot in GTA San Andreas 
 Five years ago Carl Johnson escaped from the pressures of life in Los Santos, San Andreas... a city tearing itself apart with gang trouble, drugs and corruption. Where film stars and millionaires do their best to avoid the dealers and gang-bangers. Now, it's the early 90s. Carl's got to go home. His mother has been murdered, his family has fallen apart and his childhood friends are all heading towards disaster. On his return to the neighborhood, a couple of corrupt cops frame him for homicide. CJ is forced on a journey that takes him across the entire state of San Andreas, to save his family and to take back control of the streets.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text:
San Andreas is 6 by 6 kilometers, or 36 million square meters, in size. "That's just the outside map and doesn't include the interior locations in the game, of which there are many". On top of that, the player is not restricted to the populated area of the map. The player can take a boat or plane and travel in any direction as far as they may want.

Pedestrians in the game were made to be more reactive to the player's actions and even the appearance they choose for CJ. Producer Dan Houser, on the subject of giving CJ "stupid hair", commented that "if you've got a stupid haircut, people will say, 'You look stupid'".

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text: Swimming was a feature that was allegedly added just to quieten the fanbase that had been asking for it since GTA III. On the addition of swimming to the series for the first time, Dan Houser simply commented "swimming we never had before. We just got pissed off with people saying, 'We can't do swimming.' It works well in the game. So if you drive off a bridge you're not going to drown. But that said, it’s not a swimming game." On being able to exit a vehicle which has fallen into the water, Houser added "If you don't choose to exit the car, you will sink with the car, then you'll have a certain amount of stamina under water which you can build up. There'll be a few missions that will have swimming in them, but it's not going to be like a PSone-era action adventure game where everyone was obsessed with swimming periodically. Definitely not. It just gives it playability."

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text: When asked by if a single event could be scripted to occur extremely rarely, such as once a year, like in the case of the viral Bigfoot rumours, programmer John Whyte confirmed that "there isn't any way of the scripts identifying the date and creating events that are scheduled like this."

Senior level designer Chris Rothwell confirmed that the scripting language and engine used in GTA San Andreas hadn't changed much since it was used to make GTA III several years earlier. "Since GTA Vice City, numerous improvements have been made to make scripting more powerful, such as the addition of arrays, switch statements, sequence tasks for character artificial intelligence, and uncountable game-specific commands." A favorite tool that was added during the development was the ability to record cars' positions while driving them around the city in the game, then being able to replay these car recordings in real time during a mission. This enabled the development team to really polish and improve the on-rails missions and scripted cutscenes.

A lot of the new gameplay features in GTA San Andreas were only made possible by these advancements in the scripting language. For example, the 2D-based casino and console games weren't viable in GTA Vice City until a host of heads-up display sprite commands were added during the development of GTA San Andreas. "There were also very few custom animations used during missions in GTA Vice City, but for GTA San Andreas we had a brand-new animation scripting interface." This system allowed the designers to implement animation-heavy gameplay coded entirely within the scripting language, such as in the pool game, the basketball odd job, the parachute, and in numerous other areas.

"We have an overall governing script we call the "main script." Among other things, this main script keeps track of your progress in the game, then loads and launches a mission script when you step on a mission trigger or start one of the odd jobs. Only one mission script is in memory and running at one time. In addition to the missions, we have ambient scripts resident in memory throughout the duration of the game that keep track of a wide variety of in-game systems. Examples of these are the mobile phone, stunt jumps, and shop interface scripts."

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text: When asked if players would be able to reskin characters on the PC version of the game, as they were able to in GTA Vice City, John Whyte noted that "reskinning is a much more complicated task in GTA San Andreas. This is because the model for CJ has three variations (normal, buff, and fat, depending on gameplay), and the clothes for the model have to be put together item by item because you have full control over CJ's wardrobe."

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is similarly structured to the previous two games in the series. The core gameplay consists of elements of third-person shooter and a driving game, affording the player a large, open environment in which to move around. On foot, the player's character is capable of walking, running, swimming (the first Grand Theft Auto game in which diving and swimming without drowning is possible), limited climbing, and jumping, as well as using weapons and various forms of hand-to-hand combat. Players can operate a variety of vehicles, including automobiles, boats, airplanes, helicopters, trains, tanks, motorcycles, and bicycles. Players may also import vehicles rather than steal them.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text: Although it is not explicitly stated when in 1992 the game takes place, it can be inferred to be around early to mid-spring, most likely April. Sunlight lasts around 13 hours, which in real-life corresponds to around mid-April or late August. However, when Carl travels to Liberty City during Saint Mark's Bistro, the city is covered by snow, which in real-life is not possible in August, but can occur occasionally during April. A timeframe of April is also consistent with the pedestrians' clothing they generally do not wear heavy winter clothing, but some can be seen with long-sleeves and trousers, implying that it is neither cold nor hot. It is also not uncommon to see pedestrians at beaches.

According to Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij, for GTA San Andreas, a completely new level of detail system was implemented whereby a number of models (buildings) can share a single low-detail (LOD) model. This way, the low-detail models could be loaded as the player moves around the map as opposed to in one go as the player moves between islands, like in GTA Vice City. The PC version has a further clip distance so that more of the map is always visible, and the map has a lot of the detail that had to be removed from the PlayStation 2 version to get it to fit into the smaller memory footprint. The clip distances for cars and pedestrians are increased, as well. "We have to draw these things further out because the PC will run at a higher resolution. In total, this means that the PC is pushing around a lot more than the PS2."

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text: The game has received widespread acclaim for its technical achievements and free gameplay. However, it also received widespread criticism―initially due to its "gangster" elements, which include drugs, prostitution, and murder; but later due to the discovery of disabled interactive sex scenes, nicknamed Hot Coffee, which could be re-enabled using third-party mods. This led to the re-rating by the ESRB of the game from Mature to Adults-Only until a second version, with the sex scenes fully removed (and removed the ability to mod the PC version), was released.

title: Freight Train Challenge
text:
The mission involves the player transporting freight around the state in a Brown Streak or a Freight under a time limit. The challenge is available after completing Yay Ka-Boom-Boom. Like most side missions, it is activated by pressing the sub-mission button.

Controlling the freight train is very simple: just accelerate and reverse to control the speed of the train. However, the player has to keep an eye for the speed, so as to avoid derailing the train. In addition, upon approaching the destinated station, the player must stop the train exactly within the red marker on the station.

The challenge is completed when both levels have been completed; it is failed when either the train is derailed, the time limit expires, a station is missed, if the vehicle is abandoned, or if the sub-mission button is pressed. Completing the mission is required to achieve 100% completion.

title: Drive-Thru
text: Drive-Thru is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by Grove Street Families leader Sean "Sweet" Johnson from his home in Ganton, Los Santos, San Andreas.

title: Drive-Thru
text: Carl arrives at Sweet's house to find Sweet, Smoke, and Ryder walking out. Smoke suggests getting something to eat. Carl, Sweet, Smoke and Ryder get into Sweet's car and drive to Cluckin' Bell in Willowfield. On the way, Carl asks how his mother was killed, to which Ryder replies that they were trying to kill Sweet and that people say they saw a green Sabre involved in the shooting. They go to the drive-thru and order their food, which sees Smoke order food for everyone else and a much larger order for himself. After collecting the food, Ryder spots some Kilo Tray Ballas in a pink Voodoo, the same one that chased them a few days earlier, heading towards Grove Street.

The Ballas are chased by Carl, Sweet, Smoke and Ryder. Sweet and Ryder shoot at the Ballas car, while Smoke stuffs his face with food. The Ballas car is eventually destroyed, killing the Ballas inside. Afterwards, Carl drives Sweet, Smoke and Ryder back to Grove Street. Carl then drives Smoke back to his house in Idlewood. Along the way, Carl asks Smoke why he moved out of Grove Street. Smoke tells Carl that he received money from his aunt's will, but Grove Street will always be his home. title: Drive-Thru
text: When the second cutscene begins after the quartet arrives at the drive-thru, the four models of Ryder, Sweet, CJ and Smoke can be seen at the bottom left, merged into each other, in T-poses. A video of this can be seen . It is a common practice to store characters or models used later in an in-engine cutscene outside of the visible area, so the game can call them in quickly if needed, without loading them in a second time. In fact, if the original PS2 version is played in 4:3, two black bars cover the bottom and top half of the cutscene, hiding the models. If the game is played in widescreen, however, the bars are omitted, and the models are visible. This can be seen with more ease on the Xbox 360 remastered version because of the higher resolution. This was later removed in The Definitive Edition.

title: The Chiliad Challenge
text:
The mission is started by entering a parked Mountain Bike on top of Mount Chiliad between 7:00 and 18:00 and having a cycling skill above 40%. The goal of the mission is to be the first to reach the base of the mountain while racing with other mountain bikers down the mountain. There are three courses that need to be completed for 100% completion. All three courses share the same final sector and finish zone. Completing the first course unlocks the second one, and completing the second one unlocks the third and final course.

The opponents seem to utilize rubberband AI, a concept which tries to ensure that neither the player nor NPCs can get too far behind or too far ahead without any competition.

title: The Chiliad Challenge
text:
which tries to ensure that neither the player nor NPCs can get too far behind or too far ahead without any competition.

Whereas in any other vehicle race, one can shoot at other contestants and get away with it, in this muscle-based race, if Carl Johnson attempts to shoot opponents, not only will he be disqualified (i.e. fail the mission), but a one-star wanted level will also be obtained. Typically though, trying the race again at the top of the mountain will help lose the cops. The player can, however, get off and use the sniper rifle (no other weapon can be used) to eliminate them without penalty.

There is a safety mechanic that is activated in the event CJ falls off the track with no way to recover. Should this happen, the screen goes black for a second and CJ respawns on the track at the exact spot where he left off, allowing him to resume the race.

title: The Chiliad Challenge
text: Scotch Bonnet Yellow Route: This race's route lays mostly in the southwestern face of the mountain; it is the shortest way down to Angel Pine from the top of the mountain in distance and time, but also the steepest, with very tight corners, most of which are 180º corners. Combined with the reduced grip of the dirt road and the descending factor, cornering here is very tricky. A careful braking and cornering is the key, and it is likewise recommended to sprint sparingly. There are plenty of places where CJ can fall off the track and down the mountain from great heights, but some of them are blocked by fences. This race has 18 checkpoints, and the prize for winning is $500. Birdseye Winder: This race's route goes through the north face road to descend and then turns along the west side and then south down to Angel Pine.

title: The Chiliad Challenge

It is longer and less steep downhill overall than the previous race route, but it also has some long and leveled straight sectors where CJ can sprint for a while and take the lead easily. However, side protections are even fewer than in the previous race and there are still some difficult corners. This race has 31 checkpoints, and the prize for winning is $1,000. Cobra Run: This race starts mid-way down on the south side and follows a narrow trail, which is very tricky in the beginning, with an elevated part; after a jump, the second half allows a higher speed as it is wider. During the race, there are only two opponents, as opposed to five in previous courses. This race has 21 checkpoints, and the prize for winning is $2,000.

This glitch occurs only when said stat is set at the value of 0. The only known workaround to prevent this glitch is by actually performing the two-wheel stunt before attempting The Chiliad Challenge.

title: Valet

The ultimate American dream - get someone else to park your car. 
The Valet mission is a side mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. These mission is triggered when Carl Johnson walks into the red marker in front of the Vank Hoff Hotel in Financial, San Fierro, just north of the Big Pointy Building, but only when wearing the Valet Uniform. The mission, along with the required outfit, becomes available only after completion of the mission 555 We Tip.

title: Valet
text:
The objective is to collect hotel patrons' cars from the front of the hotel (the car will drive into the driveway) and drive them into the underground parking lot.

In each level, the player starts with two minutes on the timer and must park a specified number of cars to complete the level. To collect a car in front of the hotel, simply enter it, then drive it into the parking lot. To park the car, drive it to the red marker inside the parking lot. Upon successfully parking a car, the player will gain a time bonus, which will be added to the timer: up to 45 seconds for keeping the car in one piece and up to 13 seconds for parking straight between the lines and close to the center of the marker, for the maximum time bonus of 58 seconds.

title: Quarry Missions
text: The Quarry Missions are a series of asset missions in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Quarry Missions
text: The Quarry Missions are unlocked after Explosive Situation and involve a series of seven missions in which Carl Johnson works for the Hunter Quarry in Bone County. The missions can be triggered by walking into the red marker at the eastern entrance of the quarry. Each mission involves Carl using quarry machinery to complete jobs around the quarry and beyond. Once a mission is successfully completed, the next one can be triggered by walking into the same red marker (should the player fail a mission, it can be restarted at any time by going back there). Each mission completed rewards the player with money.

Once all seven missions have been completed, the Hunter Quarry will become an asset and generate up to $2,000 in revenue, and the Dozer and Dumper will always spawn in the quarry. The time taken for the player to complete the Quarry Missions is also displayed in the stats. The player can replay the Quarry Missions any time during free roam to beat their best time, and during replays, the player can choose to abort the mission at any point.

Completing all Quarry Missions is required for 100% completion.

title: Roadside Assistance
text:
One dialogue string of a cop mentions a petrol that has been spilled on the road. This would confirm that a removed petrol feature would be present in the mission.
The mission had another segment, which involved a second vehicle to be towed, as ST3_18 indicates that there was another car to be towed at an unknown drive-thru location, and the player needed to go there and hook it up before the real Tow Truck would arrive.
According to the mission strings, it took place on a freeway in San Fierro.
The mission leftovers are from a console port; the string ST3_5 confirms that, as it mentions an "analogue stick to hook up the car". The mission was cut early in developement.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide
text: The Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas Official Strategy Guide is a publication by . It contains strategies, maps and walkthroughs that a player may find useful while playing Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The guide was created before the final release of GTA San Andreas and therefore features some now-cut content.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide
text:
The guide's main authors are Tim Bogenn and Rick Barba, with assistance from Rockstar Games staff such as Devin Winterbottom, Lee Cummings, Jeff Rosa, Ethan Abeles, Scott Peterman, Nick Giovannetti, Gene Overton, Jenefer Gross, Terry Donovan and Sam Houser.

More specifically, special thanks was given to Winterbottom for "proving great support throughout the entire project" and to Abeles and Cummings for helping the BradyGames team map everything in San Andreas.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Basics
text: This page contains transcripts of the Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas Official Strategy Guide Basics section.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Basics
text:
Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas Official Strategy Guide p. 4
 Your Weapon Skill increases with every accurate shot you land. Getting a high Weapon Skill increases your ability with weapons. View weapon skills by pressing the L1 button when holding the weapon in question. The skill level appears in the stat box in the bottom corner of the screen.. You can also check weapon stats through the Stats menu. The Stats menu displays the weapon skill level and a label, such as "Poor," "Gangster," or "Hitman." Gangster level is reached when skill levels fill 20% to 50% of the meter. All "Hitman" levels are reached when skill levels reach the maximum (100%). Your Weapon Skills improve in-between these milestones, as well.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Basics
text:
Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas Official Strategy Guide p. 4-5
 The following weapons are categorized by weapon slots. CJ has 12 different weapon slots, which holds a particular class of weapons and items. You can only carry one weapon per slot, so if that slot is filled you must press the L1 button while standing over the weapon you want to add tp the inventory. The old weapon in that slot is lost.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Basics
text:
Weapons in this slot allow you to attack and block. To block, hold R1 to select a victim and press Square to block. 
Fist - "No weapons, just the good ol' clenched fist."
Brass Knuckles - "More damaging than the bare fist."

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Basics

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Basics
text:
Every weapon in this slot has its own Weapon Skill. All Hitman Skill levels are reached at 100% Weapon Skill. 
Pistol - "Gangster level reached at 10% Pistol Skill."
Silenced 9mm - "The silenced pistol is not only good for keeping quiet, but it's also five times as powerful as the Pistol. Gangster level reached at 20% Silenced Pistol Skill."
Desert Eagle - "This is a very powerful handgun that must be held with two hands to control recoil. Almost twice as powerful as the Silenced Pistol. Gangster Level reached at 20% Desert Eagle Skill."

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Basics
text:
Every weapon in this slot has its own Weapon Skill. All Hitman Skill levels are reached at 100% Weapon Skill. 
Shotgun - "Gangster level at 20% Shotgun Skill."
Sawn-Off Shotgun - "This weapon is more powerful than the Shotgun at close range. Gangster level reached at 20% Sawn-Off Shotgun Skill."
Combat Shotgun - "The spaz shotgun is the most powerful Shotgun of the bunch. Gangster level reached at 20% Combat Shotgun Skill."

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Basics
text:
The first two weapons below are in the "Machine Pistol" Skill category. All Hitman Skill levels are reached at 100% Weapon Skill. 
Tec-9 - "The weakest of the Uzi-type weapons, but allows you to do drive-bys. Gangster level reached at 10% Machine Pistol Skill."
Micro-MP5 - "More powerful than the Tec-9, but can't touch the MP5. Gangster level reached at 10% Machine Pistol Skill."
SMG - "The most powerful weapon in its category, the MP5 is the next big thing to having an AK. Gangster level reached at 30% MP5 Skill."

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Basics
text:
Every weapon in this slot has its own Weapon Skill. All Hitman Skill levels are reached at 100% Weapon Skill.

M4 - "The M4 military weapon is top dog, although it's sometimes difficult to compare it to the AK-47. Gangster level reached at 20% M4 Skill."

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Basics
text:
The weapons in this category have no upgrade ability and no auto targeting feature. 
Country Rifle - "A powerful and popular brand of rifle. With its long barrel comes extreme accuracy. You cannot move while shooting or aiming this weapon. Hold R1 for a targeting reticle."
Sniper Rifle - "Hold R1 to raise the scope to your eye, L2 and R2 to zoom in and out, and L3 to crouch for improved stability. You cannot move while shooting or aiming this weapon.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Basics
text:
The weapons in this category have no upgrade ability and you cannot crouch while wielding them. Rocket Launcher - "You cannot shoot this weapon without first pressing the R1 button to bring up the targeting box. Aim and press Circle to fire. You'll take damage if you shoot close objects."
Heat-Seeking Rocket Launcher - "Press and hold R1 for auto-targeting until targeting reticle turns from green to red. Press Circle to fire a homing missile. The weapon only targets select vehicles and always the nearest vehicle in view. To force a lock on on a different vehicle. To force a lock-on on a different vehicle, aim away from the selected target and scope the desired target."

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Basics
text:
The weapons in this category have no upgrade ability and no auto targeting; they're projectiles. The distance that these projectiles are thrown depends on how long you hold the Circle button - within reason.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Basics
text:
The weapons in this category have no upgrade ability. All have multiple uses.

title: Taxi Driver in GTA San Andreas
text: Taxi Driver is a taxi-based side mission available in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Taxi Driver in GTA San Andreas
text: The player can earn money by delivering pedestrians to their predetermined destination within a time limit. Starting the mission lights up the taxi's roof-mounted sign encouraging nearby pedestrians to flag the player's taxi down. Once a pedestrian enters the vehicle, the destination is displayed on screen and is marked by a blip on the radar and a colored marker at the destination itself. The allotted time given is calculated roughly from the distance to the destination, and an additional 10 seconds is granted upon completing a fare to find another one. If the player runs out of time, exits their vehicle or destroys it, dies or gets arrested, the mission fails.

Although missing rear doors save disembark/embark time, spending the time detouring to a Pay 'n' Spray en-route can be a valuable restoration investment when the cab becomes difficult to control or before it begins to reject new fares.

The taxi side mission in GTA San Andreas also features a "tip meter", which depletes with time elapsed and damage taken. The player must therefore try to reach the destination quickly and safely. The "tip meter" feature was not present in previous games, making the "Speed Bonus" message there ambiguous and confusing.

title: Vigilante in GTA San Andreas
text: Vigilante is a law enforcement vehicle-based side mission available in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Vigilante in GTA San Andreas
text:
In order to start the mission, the player must enter a law enforcement vehicle and press the button shown on the instruction text (platform dependent) to toggle the side mission on or off. Once the mission is started, the player is given the criminal's last known location and a timer. The player must chase down and eliminate the criminal to pass the level and get a time bonus for the next level.

At the start of the mission, a criminal spawns in a random vehicle (clearly marked and shown on the radar) and attempts to evade the player. If the vehicle catches fire or is held in place for more than a couple of seconds, the occupant(s) will bail out and run or attempt to acquire new transport.

title: Vigilante in GTA San Andreas
text:
d in place for more than a couple of seconds, the occupant(s) will bail out and run or attempt to acquire new transport.

The mission fails if the player remains outside of a Law Enforcement vehicle for more than 60 seconds in one go, dies or is arrested, or the time runs out. Each time a Vigilante mission is started, the player always starts at Level 1, as there is no option to continue the mission from the highest level completed.

In order to achieve the 100% Completion requirement, the player must complete 12 levels in a row.

title: Vigilante in GTA San Andreas
text:
Alternatively to land vehicles, the player can start the side mission using the Hunter, using its mounted machine guns and missiles to complete the mission faster. In this case, the side mission will be titled "Brown Thunder" in-game, but the overall gameplay remains the same as the land vehicle counterpart.

Aside from name, the mission progression for Brown Thunder will be normally counted towards the Vigilante mission. If the 100% Completion requirement is achieved through Brown Thunder, it won't be necessary to replay the land vehicle variant of the mission.

text:
In order to start the mission, the player must enter a Fire Truck (standard variant only, not available for the ladder variant) and press the button shown on the instruction text (platform dependent) to toggle the side mission on or off.

After putting out the fire within the time limit, the level is completed and the player will get a time bonus for the following level. For the following levels, the player must extinguish the fires of multiple vehicles and their occupants.

In order to achieve 100% completion, the player must complete 12 levels in a row.

title: Firefighter in GTA San Andreas
text:
An alternative version of the Firefighter side-mission was originally planned, but was scrapped during early development.

This variation of Fire Fighter tasked the player to break into burning buildings and rescue people from inside by guiding them out of the building. It can only be assumed that the interiors used in this side-mission were reused Burglar house interiors due to lack of leftovers of this mission in the game files.

It is suggested that the mission Burning Desire originally served as a tutorial for this side-mission due to the similarity of objectives. However, the "Oxygen" limit is exclusive to the side-mission.

title: Paramedic in GTA San Andreas
text: Paramedic is an emergency vehicle-based side mission available in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Paramedic in GTA San Andreas
text:
In order to start the mission, the player must enter an Ambulance and press the button shown on the instruction text (platform dependent) to toggle the side mission on or off.

Once the mission is started, the player is given the location of a patient in a random neighborhood of the current city or region, and a time limit on screen below the HUD. The player must drive the Ambulance to the patient's location, pick them up and deliver them to the hospital within the time limit to complete the level.

For each new level, an additional patient is added to the radar to be picked up. As the Ambulance has only three seats available for the patients, it will be necessary to make multiple runs to complete a single level after level 3. The number of seats available is displayed below the timer.

title: Paramedic in GTA San Andreas
text:
make multiple runs to complete a single level after level 3. The number of seats available is displayed below the timer.

After picking up any patient, a time bonus is given to the player, increasing the time limit of the current level.

The side mission can be failed by ending the side mission, leaving or destroying the Ambulance, killing one patient, which can occur after numerous bumps (which hurts the patient, costing the player time) or running over patients, and being killed or arrested. Failing the paramedic side mission results in the player having to start from the first level.

In order to achieve the 100% Completion requirement, the player must complete 12 levels in a row. If the mission is cancelled or failed, the player must restart from the first level.

title: Paramedic in GTA San Andreas
text:
The region of Whetstone is considered a separate region from Flint County and San Fierro.

If the player starts the Paramedic mission in this region, all patients will spawn in the small town of Angel Pine, the one and only inhabited zone in Whetstone, and in the same vicinity of the Angel Pine Medical Center (defined as a possible drop-off point for the Paramedic side-mission), allowing the player to complete the side-mission faster.

title: Ammu-Nation Challenge
text: The goal of the challenge is to score more points than the opponents during three consecutive rounds of four different weapons - Pistol, Micro SMG, Shotgun and Assault Rifle, in that order, for a total of twelve rounds. During each round, the player must compete against two opponents. Completing the third round of the AK-47 challenge – only available after unlocking full access to the entire San Andreas map via the mission Yay Ka-Boom-Boom – is a requirement for 100% completion of the game.

title: Ammu-Nation Challenge
text:
All three rounds of each weapon follow the same layout:
Round 1: Three targets are dropped in the first round of each weapon competition. After destroying one, the next one drops at a greater distance. To destroy a target, the player must shoot the center of the seven different red circles on it. A hit anywhere outside the circles doesn't count. To pass this round, the player must destroy their three targets before the competitors destroy theirs. Round 2: A target drops and moves steadily from the back of the range toward the player, then stops until all seven sections on the target are shot. Once the target is destroyed, another drops at the back of the range and follows the same route. To pass this round, the player must destroy their three targets before the competitors destroy theirs.

title: Ammu-Nation Challenge
text: s the same route. To pass this round, the player must destroy their three targets before the competitors destroy theirs. Round 3: In the final round, there's only one target that moves across the targeting range, from left to right or vice versa. All competitors shoot the target simultaneously, racing against each other to get to the target score of 20 points. Points are indicated on the right side of the screen. A point is earned for each section of the target removed. Targets continuously drop at varying distances and strafe across the range until someone reaches the target score. To pass this round, the player must score 20 points before the competitors do so.

title: Ammu-Nation Challenge
text:
If the player enters the shooting range while having certain weapons in their inventory and leaves without finishing the course, the ammunition for that weapon doubles. The trick can be repeated infinitely, potentially serving as a way to get infinite ammunition before reaching 100% completion. The affected weapons are:
Handguns: Silenced 9mm, Desert Eagle (the frequency of doubling the ammo count for handguns is slightly lowered compared to the other weapon classes)
Shotguns: Sawed-off Shotgun, Combat Shotgun

It is important to note that other weapon classes are not affected. Also, if the player enters the range with the standard Shotgun, they will lose the weapon.

title: Blood Ring (GTA San Andreas)
text:
Using a Bloodring Banger, the player is required to collect small fractions of time for a constantly decreasing timer via a randomly placed checkpoint around the arena until they have collected enough time to complete the side-mission. The player is challenged by 20 other competitors whose primary goal is to ram the player's car and hinder the player's progress, while snatching up the checkpoints themselves. Spinning pickups marked with a wrench are also available only to the player to repair their car.

The player begins with 30 seconds on the timer, with each checkpoint being worth 15 seconds. If the player is wasted or runs out of time, the player fails the mission. If the vehicle is flipped over, it will be automatically turned back up. The player is able to repair their Bloodring Banger by collecting repair pickups, appearing as a blue "wrench" pickup.

The player is not given any reward for destroying competing cars, though the number of cars destroyed will still show after winning the competition.

If the player is wasted during the mission, they will spawn outside of the stadium without losing the weapons, instead of a nearby hospital or Katie Zhan's House.

title: Weapons in GTA San Andreas
text: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas features 38 different weapons and three special items, where they follow the same mechanics as in previous titles, however, the arsenal has been expanded with the introduction of "consumable items", as well as "gifts", which are primarily used for girlfriends and optionally used as melee weapons.

title: Weapons in GTA San Andreas
text:
A notable improvement over previous games is the auto-aiming system on every weapon (except the Rifle, the Sniper Rifle, projectiles, or any of the heavy weapons), which occurs when the target is within the weapon's range (determined by the type of weapon and the player's proficiency with that weapon based on the skill) and takes the priority on the closest target when facing multiple NPCs. Another feature of this improvement is the targeting lock that changes color as the target's health decreases. Green progresses to orange, which progresses to red, and finally black upon the target's death.

The Auto-aim also seems to bear a strong resemblance to the execution system in Rockstar North's Manhunt, where the darker the color or the target, the more gruesome the execution; in GTA San Andreas, the darker the color of the target, the less health of the target.

title: Weapons in GTA San Andreas
text:
Another notable feature is a weapon skill system; where it determines the general proficiency of the player with the weapons. This increases when the player shoots accurately. Getting a high Weapon Skill increases the ability with weapons and grants more versatility when used. There are three levels of skill: "Poor", "Gangster", and "Hitman".

One can view the weapon skills two ways:

Wielding the weapon, then press L1, LT, or TAB. The skill level appears in the stat box in the bottom corner of the screen.
In the menu, select Stats, then Weapons. Each weapon type displays one of three labels: "Poor", "Gangster", or "Hitman". If one is wielding a weapon, one will also see their current skill level for that weapon.

title: Weapons in GTA San Andreas
text:
Gangster level is reached when the meter is 20% to 50% filled.

When Gangster is reached with certain weapons, the player is able to move while aiming, and their lock-on range, accuracy, rate of fire, and strafe speed increase:

All type of Shotguns (note: Carl can already move while aiming/firing the sawn-off shotgun)

title: Weapons in GTA San Andreas
text:
Hitman level is reached when the meter is 100% filled.

When Hitman is reached with certain weapons, the player's lock-on range, accuracy, rate of fire, and strafe speed increase further, and they're able to fire these weapons while moving:

AK47
Combat Shotgun
Desert Eagle
M4
SMG

Shotgun

title: Weapons in GTA San Andreas
text:
One new feature is the ability to duel-wield certain weapons after reaching Hitman weapon skill level. These weapons are light enough and feature reloading that is compatible with holding one in each hand. This allows the player to inflict twice the amount of damage per reload cycle. For weapons that have Double Weapon Hitman, it takes longer to reach 100% weapon skill opposed to other weapons that can only be wielded with both hands.

When the player reaches Double Weapon Hitman, they can wield two of the below weapons simultaneously, and their lock-on range increases:

Micro SMG
Pistol (9mm)
Sawn-Off Shotgun
Tec-9

title: Weapons in GTA San Andreas
text: The TEC-9, Flamethrower, and Minigun are the only weapons which, when fired, do not move CJ's body. Oddly enough, melee weapons such as the Chainsaw can be used to amass large sums of money in short periods of time, if the player correctly utilizes the weapon with no law enforcement in their vicinity. Much like the Baseball Bat in Grand Theft Auto III, where the player can kill literally thousands of citizens with no wanted level if planned correctly. There are two different ways to get infinite ammo for guns. Acquiring 100% game completion or the infinite ammo cheat. The Tec-9 and Micro SMG are the only weapons that share the same weapon skill (that is shown in stats as machine pistol). Weapons that can be dual wielded at Hitman level take significantly longer time to level up.

title: Weapons in GTA San Andreas
text: It is possible to get infinite ammo by going to a shooting range in some Ammu-Nation shops. Select a firearm of choice (excluding heavy and throwable weapons) and enter the shooting range, right after the screen turns black, press the escape button a few times and wait for CJ to teleport back in the shop; the player will notice (sometimes, rarely or never) the ammo of the firearm they're holding have doubled, keep doing this (with the help of luck) and when the ammo reaches until a point that the amount disappears, then it will become unlimited. Players who are looking for an alternative way to make the ammo amount on the HUD icon disappear can simply buy ammo till it reaches 9999-?? and then pick up any weapon via police that they've dropped.

title: Horseshoes
text:
There are 50 Horseshoes located all around Las Venturas, which the player must find and collect while on foot.

Each Horseshoe collected rewards the player with $100 and 20 points of "Luck" in the Stats menu (which does not affect the gameplay in any way), totaling $5,000 and 1000 "Luck" points for collecting all Horseshoes.

Collecting all 50 Horseshoes is a requirement for the 100% completion.

title: Horseshoes
text: The Horseshoes are available upon gaining control of Carl Johnson during In the Beginning (collecting them before Las Venturas is unlocked is risky due to a 4-star wanted level obtained).

title: Horseshoes
text:
Collecting all 50 Horseshoes will reward the player with an additional $100,000 bonus (totaling $105,000), and spawn points for the SMG, M4, Combat Shotgun and Satchel Charges in front of The Four Dragons Casino.
 The Four Dragons Casino items, after collecting all Horseshoes.

title: Horseshoes
text:
The "Luck" stats tied to the Horseshoes is a leftover of an unfinished gameplay feature, originally intended to affect the casino games (available at The Four Dragons Casino, Caligula's Palace and Casino Floor), as confirmed on June 2024 by former Rockstar North Technical Director Obbe Vermeij, who also implemented the Luck stats code. In the final release, Luck is simply a meaningless value shown on the "Player" section of the Stats menu.

Respect encompasses two different gang-based systems in and Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Respect
text:
In GTA San Andreas, respect is an element indicating how inclined the gang is to help Carl. The more respect he has, the more gang members he can recruit to tend to his personal interests.

Raising the respect bar is straight-forward: doing missions, taking over gang turf, and murdering rival gang members and law enforcement officers are the most common ways. Respect also affects CJ's sex appeal.

Up to seven gang members can be recruited. This will not happen until Carl has roughly 80% of the respect meter full.

title: Girlfriends in GTA San Andreas
text: In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, there are six possible girlfriends Carl Johnson can date, with two of them becoming girlfriends through the storyline.

title: Girlfriends in GTA San Andreas
text:
Dating any of the six girlfriends is not required for 100% completion, with the exception of Millie, though she can simply be killed during her first date instead.

CJ meets Denise Robinson during the mission Burning Desire, whilst Millie Perkins is introduced in Key to Her Heart. The other girlfriends are encountered during free roam, rather than being attached to missions. Helena Wankstein, Michelle Cannes, and Katie Zhan become available to date after completing The Green Sabre. Although Helena is encountered in Red County (which is accessible from the start of the game), she does not appear until Flint County and Whetstone are unlocked. Barbara Schternvart becomes available after Yay Ka-Boom-Boom.

On PlayStation 2 and Xbox, players can initiate two-player free roam with any of CJ's girlfriends, as long as she is dating CJ and at home.

title: Girlfriends in GTA San Andreas
text: Three different activities are available during dates. These include a visit to a restaurant (including fast-food chains, diners, formal restaurants, and bars, alongside the bar in dance clubs), dancing at a dance club, and driving around. Each girlfriend has their own different tastes in the three activities, as well as Carl's physical appearance. After a certain number of successful dates, Carl may be invited back to her place for "coffee" (sex). Reaching a 35%-50% relationship status will give Carl access to the girlfriend's car as the game will mention that the girlfriend has shared her car keys to CJ, and once the relationship status is maxed, Carl will receive a unique outfit from the girlfriend.

title: Girlfriends in GTA San Andreas
text:
Denise, Michelle and Millie have unique dating activities the other girls do not have:

For Denise, if she is driven through areas occupied by enemy gangs, she will perform a drive-by. After about five successful kills, she'll be pleased enough to take her home.

For Michelle, instead of driving her around, she might ask to be the one who will drive, and as long as Carl does not bail out of the car, the date will be successful.

For Millie, by simply appearing in a gimp suit (which will be in Carl's wardrobe after their first encounter) to pick her up, regardless of Carl's progress with Millie, she will offer to have sex with him and the progress will increase.

title: Girlfriends in GTA San Andreas
text: Note: The Amity Seafood Restaurant in Blueberry is erroneously marked as a bar in-game, instead of being marked as a diner. If visited during a date, it will count as a dining date.

title: Girlfriends in GTA San Andreas
text:
There are ways for a date to either turn out right or wrong. If Carl takes a girlfriend to a restaurant they like, romantic music will play and it will show the two having a good time with each other. However, if Carl takes the girlfriend to a restaurant they do not like, the girl will show displeasure with Carl, who is gobbling his food.

When dancing in a nightclub, if Carl does not score a high enough dancing score, the girlfriend will be disappointed. When driving around, if Carl insists on consistently driving in areas the girlfriend doesn't like or drives at an undesirable speed to the point that her fun meter hits zero, she will just ask to be taken home.

If certain criteria are met, there is a 50% chance that another jealous girlfriend will appear 7 seconds after CJ and his date set off to return to her house following a good date. A brief cutscene will play, alerting the player of the jealous girlfriend. After the cutscene, CJ can proceed through the date as normal, however the jealous girlfriend will pursue CJ and his date.

If CJ gets too close to the jealous girlfriend, another cutscene will play in which the two girlfriends insult each other briefly. The date will then be over, and CJ is instructed to take his date back home, and CJ will lose progress with the jealous girlfriend. Alternatively, CJ can evade the jealous girlfriend.

The criteria for having a jealous girlfriend appear are as follows:
CJ must not go on a date with any girlfriends until he has more than one.

title: Girlfriends in GTA San Andreas
text:
Unlike the mission unlocking-related phone calls received throughout the game, which are forced to retry if ignored, the game will not check if the player is available to receive a girlfriend phone call due to a fault on the dating system script.

As a result, whenever the player is not available to receive the date phone call prompt (while in a mission, minigame, vehicle, swimming, falling, Jetpack, Parachute, etc.), the game will force the script to initiate the phone call regardless. The phone call will be immediately terminated after being triggered by the script and the game will count that as the player ignoring the phone call, resulting in the "random" relationship status decrease notification.

Break-up calls are also ignored due to this oversight.

title: Tags
text:
There are 100 Tags located all around Los Santos, which the player must find and paint a Grove Street Families tag over it using a Spray Can while on foot. A tag needs at least 29 units of Spray Can "ammo" to be completely sprayed over. 

A Tag is not considered sprayed until the on-screen message appears and confirmation sound is played, which can be triggered without the Tag being completely covered and so can still be locked on. Using the Spray Can may attract a wanted level.

The Spray Can item is available in three different locations in Los Santos (interior and rooftop of Johnson House, and a house in Las Colinas) and at the Sobell Rail Yards in Las Venturas.

Spraying over all 100 Tags is a requirement for the 100% completion.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Gameplay Features
text:
Many new features have been included in the game. New vehicles include bicycles (which feature a new control scheme), trucks with detachable trailers, police motorcycles, operable tow trucks, combine harvesters, quad bikes, aircrafts, military jet fighters and trains.

New to the players character is the ability to swim and climb up and over short walls and fences. For greater firepower, players can also wield dual firearms or perform a drive-by shooting with several gang members. The camera, fighting, and targeting controls were reworked with concepts from another Rockstar game, Manhunt, including improved target cross-hairs that change colors from green to red to black, depending on the target's health.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Gameplay Features
text: Rockstar has emphasized the personalization of the main character. Clothing and accessories (which players can buy at some of the game's many clothing stores), haircuts and tattoos are now available for purchase by CJ, and have more effect on NPCs' reactions than the clothing in Vice City. Players must also ensure CJ eats to stay healthy, obtaining food from fast food restaurants such as Cluckin' Bell, street vendors, diners, bars, and nightclubs. The balance of food and exercise has an effect on his muscularity and appearance. If CJ eats too much in a short period, he will get sick and throw up; if he overeats periodically, he'll get fat and move more slowly while on foot; if he fails to eat, he will become less muscular and, eventually, will lose health.

San Andreas also features skills, in areas such as driving, firearms handling, stamina, and lung capacity, which improve through use in the game. CJ may also learn three different styles of unarmed combat at the gyms in each of the game's three cities.

A new activity that continues the Grand Theft Auto series' tradition of controversy is home invasion

Numerous minigames are also available for play in San Andreas, including basketball, pool, rhythm-based challenges involving dancing and hydraulic vehicles, and video game machines that pay homage to classic arcade games such as Gyruss, Defender and Gradius, in addition to the aforementioned methods of gambling.

Another improvement to the game is the AI. No longer can the player beat a pedestrian to death on a busy street in broad daylight and have bystanders not do anything: while most pedestrians will flee or duck for cover, some armed civilians and enemy gang members will attack CJ, and friendly gang members will shoot at and pursue his opponents. This would make the previously mentioned home invasions more difficult than one would expect because the occupants will resist, and in some cases, draw weapons. There is also road rage, if the player hits a driver's car (commonly a taxi) they will come out and attack you, or they may try to total the player's vehicle.

A two-player cooperative mode has also been added for the PlayStation 2 and Xbox. Two-player icons are found in several key locations in the San Andreas world. Setting foot on one of these icons and pressing any button on a second controller starts up a series of special objectives similar to a "Rampage" in previous Grand Theft Auto games. Two human players will be able to go in a car or on foot. Both the players are required to remain on the same screen and within a reasonable proximity of one another.

title: Snapshots
text:
There are 50 Snapshots located all around San Fierro and city limits, which the player must find and photograph using a Camera. The Camera has several spawn points in San Fierro, all located near Snapshot locations.

The Snapshot location indicators appear as a rotating circular camera icon, only visible when viewed in first-person through the Camera's viewfinder. Between 00:00 and 05:00, a pinkish glow can be seen without the Camera, which marks where the snapshot icons are. Outside of these hours the glow can be seen using Night Vision Goggles.

Each Snapshot taken rewards the player with $100, totaling $5,000 for photographing all Snapshots. Photographing all 50 Snapshots is a requirement for the 100% completion.

title: Snapshots
text:
The player is allowed to capture Snapshots through structures and buildings from a long range by zooming in with the Camera, regardless whether the Snapshot pickup is visible onscreen or centered.

It is also possible to catch a glimpse of a Snapshot icon without the need of a camera if the player speeds towards one, it will be visible for a second before disappearing.

title: Snapshots

text: This page contains transcripts of the Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas Official Strategy Guide Chapter 1: Los Santos section.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Chapter 1: Los Santos
text: Five years ago Carl Johnson escaped the city, his past, and a life that was spiraling out of control. He abandoned Los Santos for Liberty City when his brother, Brian, met an early end. Unfortunately, recent gang violence also claimed his mother's life, forcing CJ's return to the city to attend the funeral... and to avenge her death. En route front the Los Santos International Airport, CJ is welcomed by a couple of old acquaintances from his gangbanging past — corrupt police officers, Frank Tenpenny and Eddie Pulaski. They escort CJ into the squad car and drive him to the heart of Ballas territory (the unforgiving Ballas are gang rivals of CJ's gong, the Grove Street Families). Tenpenny and Pulaski dishonestly draw CJ back into their crooked game by linking him to a weapon used in a fresh cop killing.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Chapter 1: Los Santos
text: As its name suggests, this strand of missions introduces you to the story, some basic game elements, your 'hood, and a few of your homies.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Chapter 1: Los Santos

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Chapter 1: Los Santos
text: You begin the adventure on foot, in a Jefferson alley, with $350 in your pocket and no weapons - not a good combination when in hostile territory. For the moment, you are safe. You have time to check out the Pause Menu options and the San Andreas map. The Player Position in Jefferson and the "CJ" icon in Ganton are the most significant things to notice on the map at this time. Approach the BMX bike (with the large, attention-getting blue marker cone above it) in the alley just ahead. Press the Triangle button to get on the bike and follow the roads leading to the "CJ" icon on the map. Several bike-riding tips appear onscreen as you pedal toward your destination. Do your best to read and ride at the same time. For more information on bikes, check out the Wang's Auto Trader section of this guide. When you reach your destination, you find yourself in your old neighborhood.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Chapter 1: Los Santos
text: e Wang's Auto Trader section of this guide. When you reach your destination, you find yourself in your old neighborhood. This is where the Grove Street Families reside - in a low-income housing cul-de-sac. Hop off the bike and walk into the red marker in front of your house to begin the first mission.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Chapter 1: Los Santos
text: After you grab the BMX bike, exit the alley and go left around the corner to the red Jefferson Motel building. Climb the motel stairs to the roof and find a nice, gleaming MP5. Later, you can also find some Body Armor and a Micro-SMG beneath the overpass bridge near Carl's Mom's House on Grove Street, plus a 9mm Pistol in a nearby backyard. Always check our Security Services maps for free weapon locations!

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Chapter 1: Los Santos
text: Just as you can now sprint faster by continuously tapping the X button (note that this is limited by Stamina), you can also pedal faster by applying the same method while riding a bike. When fast pedaling, CJ lifts off the seat and exerts some real energy onto the pedals for an incredible speed boost!

CJ finds his mom's house plundered and trashed. As he sifts through memories, Big Smoke enters the backdoor, armed with a baseball bat. At first mistaking CJ for a based-up burglar, Big Smoke embraces his old pal and they take off to meet CJ's brother and sister at their mother's gravesite in Vinewood. Big Smoke drives CJ to his mother's cemetery where he reunites with his big brother Sweet; sister, Kendl; and fellow gang member, Ryder. The 5-year reunion is short-lived as family arguments return within seconds. Kendl leaves in a huff to see her boyfriend, Cesar, who Sweet does not approve of - an opinion based solely on prejudice. As the remaining crew leaves the cemetery, the boys are subjected to a Ballas drive-by, forcing them to the ground as Big Smoke's new car explodes into flames.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Chapter 1: Los Santos
text: Follow Sweet Follow the gang across the street to the line of BMX bikes. Your first objective is to stay close to Sweet, who is on the lead BMX. Sweet is indicated on the map as a blue square; a large blue cone marker appears above his head when he's in sight. Try to stay close; the Ballas are still on the hunt. New bike tips appear onscreen as you pedal after Sweet. Pedaling faster and bunny hopping are both introduced. Pedaling faster should be your primary focus. If the Ballas in the Voodoo are giving you trouble, stop suddenly and drive behind their vehicle in another direction. If they drive beside you with guns blazing, try to lead them into hazards that force them to wreck. However, fast pedaling should keep you at a safe distance. Sweet's lead ends under the Mulholland Intersection.

text: o wreck. However, fast pedaling should keep you at a safe distance. Sweet's lead ends under the Mulholland Intersection. After the short cinematic, Sweet draws the Ballas' attention off in one direction while the rest of the gang can make their escape. You are directed to follow Ryder, who now has the blue cone marker overhead and becomes the blue blips on the map. Follow Ryder Ryder leads you through alleys of Downtown Los Santos, across a BMX park, and onto the freeway. You reach a new Cycling Skill level while on this run. Ryder takes the first exit ramp and follows the connecting road to your home in the Ganton cul-de-sac. In most missions, it is no longer necessary to come to a complete stop in the red markers. Drive through the marker to complete the mission. You earn Respect points at the end of the mission, but no monetary reward. Who'd you think would pay you for that?!

Ryder suggests you get some colors and a haircut.

 After the mission is complete, you can park vehicles or bikes in your house's attached garage and enter the house to save your progress. (Establishments with a yellow triangle marker floating in front of the door can be entered.) Walk into the save disc in the kitchen to save your progress. Doing so will advance time by six hours.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Chapter 1: Los Santos
text: Most safehouses have a room with a wardrobe closet. Yours is empty at this time, since you have not yet purchased any apparel items. When you buy a new article of clothing, the old piece is sent to your wardrobe closet. Items you have purchased and that are available in your wardrobe are marked green in clothing stores, so that you know not to buy them. Enter the marker outside the closet to change into any of the apparel items purchased from clothing stores. You can also choose the "remove" option and strip CJ down to his skivvies.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas/Official Strategy Guide/Chapter 1: Los Santos
text: Drive to the Barbers Follow Ryder into his Picador and drive to the yellow blip on the map just a few blocks away. Stop in the red marker outside of Old Reece's Hair & Facial Studio. Walk through the door with the yellow marker to enter. Reece's Barbershop Enter the red marker and have a seat in the barber's chair. Select from Old Reece's cuts using the D-pad or Left Analog Stick. When you find one you like, press the X button to purchase the cut for the indicated price. To exit the barber's chair, press the Triangle button. Refer to the Barber Shops section in our Odd Jobs chapter for a list of available hairstyles by location. Once outside, Ryder will comment on your choice of cut. You can safely assume that the more you pay for a cut, the higher your Respect and Sex Appeal stats will rise.

Enter Pizza Shop and Buy Some Food When you receive your next objective (to eat), more tips appear onscreen. The Well Stacked Pizza Co. is directly across the street from Old Reece's shop. Cross the street and enter the restaurant. Approach the counter, enter the red marker, and order some food. There are four different meals to choose from, each with a different price and varying amounts of food. These meals replenish lost health in proportion to the price of the meal. After gobbling down the coronary delight, Ryder leaves his seat and holds the cashier at gunpoint. However, the pizza boy pulls a Shotgun from under the counter and returns the favor! CJ and Ryder run out of the joint with a new objective: Escape! Get Back in Ryder's Car!

Once out of Shotgun range, you can take your time plotting your course back to Ryder's house. Follow the yellow blip on the map. Enter the red marker in Ryder's driveway to complete the mission. Before you take the next mission, enter your house and save your progress. This is a good habit to get into. Also note that this refills your Health and feeds you.
