One of the few ways to kill an invincible pedestrian is running them over with a combine harvester.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: In Downtown Los Santos, there is a building with floors on the outside that the player can stand on. On the floor in the middle of two other higher floors, they can see very little of the interior of it in some places, while others, when they look at just the right angles, make CJ invisible, but only in that spot looking in that angle. If the player has a jetpack on and do this, the flames will show. The building is straight across the highway from an Ammu-Nation.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: When a car with an aggressive NPC driver is damaged, the driver may get out of the car to deal with whoever caused the damage, and then return to the vehicle as scripted. If the car has an NPC passenger in the front seat, however, the passenger will take the driver's seat if the driver does not return after some time. When the driver is done with his job and returns to the car, he will throw the passenger out and retake the driver seat, because the driver is never scripted to take any seat other than the driver's when he enters the car. The kicked out passenger may also become aggressive and attempt to jack the driver again, or just pull him out and challenge to fight him. This can lead to endless car jackings or gun/fist fights if the NPCs are members of the same gang.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If the player runs over a lamp post with a vehicle, then parks the car where the lamp post originally was and proceeds to save, when they come back, the car will be inside the lamp post. While the car is in the lamp post, it has no collision, but as soon as they drive it out of the lamp post, it regains collision. This glitch can also be seen if the player skips a cutscene in Sweet's Girl. One of the Seville Boulevard cars will be stuck inside of a lamp post.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: There is a bug with the TransFender in Las Venturas in the PlayStation 2 version, where driving a Moonbeam into the TransFender will allow the player to modify the vehicle as normal, but once the player exits the TransFender modification screen and attempt to leave, the vehicle will spawn on top of the garage but underneath the actual roof, making it impossible to drive the vehicle out and also trapping the player inside the TransFender. The only way to escape is for the player to kill themselves by damaging the Moonbeam enough to blow it up and kill the player, or re-loading the game's save file, or the game itself. The bug is not present in subsequent versions of the game.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If the player loads a game save and exits the safe house (if the game was saved in a safe house) or waits for the game screen to display if saved at a save point, the game may rarely fail to load the texture of San Andreas and will become stuck soon after exiting. This only happens on the PC version.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: When the player loads a save file and plays about 1–2 minutes after loading the save file, an LSPD officer usually appears walking on the street. This even happens if the player has saved the game outside Los Santos. This happens much more in the mobile version due to an unexplained error, where an LSPD officer spawns at the player's current location when the game is played for some time.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If the player kills a main character (e.g. Sweet, Ryder) during a certain mission progress, the mission will fail and the in-game message says the character has died. In some occasions, the killed character will drop a random amount of money as an NPC does.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: In the PC version, while CJ is hanging with one of the main characters during a mission, such as Sweet, Smoke, or Ryder; if the player press F1 key to view the replay, their models will be replaced with the default generic male pedestrian model (known as "MALE01"), but it will revert to normal when gameplay resumes. This glitch always works with the mentioned three but won't work on some other main characters (such as Cesar or Woozie).

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If players manage to pick up a lightly harmful melee weapon such as the nightstick while they have a heavy melee weapon like a chainsaw in their melee weapon slot, the nightstick will be automatically obtained with the chainsaw being removed from the current inventory, even if they have not tapped the changing weapons button. It is unknown if this was an oversight from the game developers or a simple glitch. This does not occur if the opposite situation happens, as players have to tap the changing weapons button instead. This does not always happen, though.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If the player uses the cheat code, NIGHTPROWLER, the in-game clock display will freeze at 0:00 but the actual time passed will still advance. This cheat code affects the time cycle of the game (as defined in the timecyc.dat file), making the sky color always dark and cause a glitch in which the weather changes suddenly and one eerie phenomenon: after some time with this cheat activated, a very bright object in orange color will appear to rise in the sky (commonly mistaken as UFO by players). The object is in fact the sun but glitched, this can be seen if the cheat is deactivated and the displayed time is adjusted to the actual time which is daytime by then; or just activate the midnight cheat during daytime. Because the sun sprite still follow the actual time, it may appear at the time supposed to be midnight, even though the sky is dark.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: sun sprite still follow the actual time, it may appear at the time supposed to be midnight, even though the sky is dark. (Note that if originally the cheat code is activated after sunset but before midnight, it can set the actual time to 0:00, but not stop it). Another effect that can be easily observed is that the brightness of map textures (streets, buildings, etc.) still obey the actual time, so textures can appear daylight bright in a nighttime sky setting.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: The player must obtain a Monster and park one wheel onto a random car's hood or trunk. The wheel must glitch by pressing against the Monster's body. Next, they must get out of the Monster, get in the car CJ parked on, and the player may find themselves spinning high in the air, crashing back down to earth, or respawning somewhere else. Also, if the player manages to glitch the tire of the vehicle while it is moving onto the hood of the car, the car may fly into the air, merge into the ground and potentially stretch out, or catapult the Monster into the air. This glitch is also present in The Definitive Edition.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If, while sprinting, Carl takes a picture with a camera by quickly pressing the right mouse button (to aim) and right after, the left mouse button (to take a picture, almost at the same time), CJ should be running with the slow running animation, but with the sprinting speed, making him look like he's sliding on the ground. The higher the FPS, the easier it is to do (Tested on PC).

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: Obtain a Mountain Bike and, while Carl is riding it, the player must hold down Square and tap X very quickly. If done correctly, CJ's body will shimmer and distort out of proportion. This glitch appears to be possible only on the PS2 version of the game.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: The ninja jack glitch allows the player to kill the driver of a vehicle while hijacking it from the passenger side. This can be done by entering a car from the passenger side and holding the 'sprint' or 'jump'-button and 'move forward' just before the player sits down on the passenger seat. When done correctly, CJ will skip closing the passenger door and push the driver out, who instantly falls to their death. This also eliminates the possibility of the driver retaliating. Its term was popularized by multi-player communities where it is sometimes used to grief other players. This glitch is not present in The Definitive Edition.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: Sometimes, if Carl is driving or flying really fast over San Andreas and abruptly stops or lands, no cars will spawn on the road, although stationary vehicles and pedestrians do spawn. This glitch can be fixed by simply activating a sub-mission or entering an interior. This glitch also sometimes occurs if CJ dies inside an interior. Then, when CJ spawns at the hospital, there will be no traffic.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: A strange glitch may occur when the player drives a Packer truck with its top ramp lifted up, then stops on a pedestrian path and waits for any nearby pedestrian to step on the lower ramp. As the pedestrian continues walking inside, the Packer truck will suddenly float up in the air for a few seconds before falling down with the pedestrian. It's most likely next that the Packer will flip on its side when it reaches the ground, and the pedestrian will be dropped dead.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: The Broken Wooden Bridge to the west of Palomino Creek can be used to trigger a seemingly-considered glitch. If the player attacks a vehicle roaming in the town from the east side of the bridge with a carbine rifle or a sniper rifle while vehicles are visible, the vehicle will speed on and sometimes rush towards the bridge. Once upon reaching the bridge, the driver may crash the vehicle onto the fence of the bridge, and after that, the driver will simply drive ahead and end up falling into the water below, killing the occupant(s). Sometimes, the driver will successfully perform a stunt jump and continue driving.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If the player falls down from a low height with a parachute, the result of the fall is the same as falling from great heights without maximum health or with a not-in-use parachute. This is more than likely a glitch. It is likely because the game thinks that Carl is falling from a great height when wearing a parachute, as the parachute is intended to be used at a great height.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If the player has a parachute but doesn't deploy it yet or is still doing the opening parachute animation when CJ hits the ground, the health bar will deplete instantly and CJ will be killed. Cheats, hacks, mods or trainers couldn't prevent it from happening. This is probably because the game consider the player are still 'falling' when the opening parachute animation is triggered thus making this glitch. This glitch is also present in mobile versions.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: The parachute can be used as a weapon to attack and even kill some invincible enemies during some missions. An example of this is Big Poppa in A Home in the Hills. Despite the player can attack him in the mansion, he is considered to be invicible. However, if reacting fast enough, the player can attack him with a parachute inside. He will receive damage and can be killed, but the mission will be stuck if this happens, since he is not programmed to die in the mansion.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If the player switches to a parachute and presses F1 to toggle replay mode, the replay will have CJ hold the parachute rather than having it in his back. This is more than likely a glitch. As the parachute counts as a weapon rather than a vehicle.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: Rarely, the player can spot a paramedic running towards a disappearing NPC corpse. The paramedic will still lie down and the animation used for paramedics rescuing a collapsed pedestrian will still be played. When the paramedic finishes his "job", nothing will happen, since the corpse has been already cleared out by the game factor before the paramedic could react. This happens more commonly during the events of the Los Santos Riots between the missions Riot and End of the Line.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: There are a few locations on the map without a predetermined pedestrian path, so any NPC pedestrian in that region will walk away randomly or walk to the nearest pedestrian path. Sometimes, this can be fatal for the pedestrian if they randomly walk into water and drown or fall from a great height. The most infamous example of this is known as the "Suicidal Photographers" at the Flint Intersection. Pedestrian paths can also happen to cut structures such as high buildings, poles, or trees, so some pedestrians may unusually spawn on the top and fall down to the ground. An example is at The Emerald Isle in Las Venturas. The pedestrian path around this area cuts a corner of the building, thus pedestrians have a chance to spawn on the edge and fall down to the sidewalk below, although the fall is not lethal as that edge of the building is not high enough.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: ge and fall down to the sidewalk below, although the fall is not lethal as that edge of the building is not high enough. Some other locations include near the Cluckin' Bell in East Los Santos north of Ganton Bridge, where a pedestrian may spawn on one of the telephone poles, and the sidewalk near the road leading to Easter Bay Airport where the pedestrian path is very close to the water and without a barrier causing some pedestrians to fall into the water and drown.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text:
If the player provokes a pedestrian to make him retaliate via melee attacks, having the latter lured into attacking another pedestrian will either result in that NPC running away or fighting back, even leading to another fight if the former is attacked by the lately-provoked NPC and Carl will be ignored if this happens.

This can also apply to a police officer, however occasionally the lured NPC will be automatically given a pistol or a melee weapon to fight against the officer, who will always perform an attack with his pistol. If the NPC is shot while having nothing in his hand, he/she will immediately flee no matter what.

When the player has no wanted level, if a provoked pedestrian armed with a gun shoots at a police vehicle, the officers will get off and try to kill the NPC.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: Sometimes, if a pedestrian somehow gets killed while commenting on Carl's appearance, Carl will still be looking at that pedestrian. And if the player presses the answering button before Carl moves his head out of that pedestrian's sight, CJ will sometimes still reply that NPC by positive or negative words. This is known as a continuity error.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: In the mobile version, sometimes a dialogue box will pop up when CJ encounters killed NPCs, and the player can still choose to respond positively or negatively.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: Sometimes after completing End of the Line, some pedestrians across the state won't react to the player attacking them. Instead of fighting back or running away, they continue walking as if nothing happened.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If the player flips their car over during the last task of Yay Ka-Boom-Boom, they will have a permanent location blip at the Doherty Garage, and cannot get rid of it unless they start a new game.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: Whenever the player is answering a call and fall from a short gap (doesn't make CJ fall flat to the ground), and then tries to enter a vehicle (but don't enter it, just make CJ open the door) and then walk away. If this done correctly, CJ will hold his phone and not putting it away. This glitch is more likely to happen at the end of the conversation, just before CJ put his phone away. However, changing weapons would revert the glitch.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If CJ is on a boat and the phone rings after he gets off, he can answer before hitting the water, which will not only cause him to talk while swimming, but will also render him unable to pick up items such as oysters until he enters another vehicle. This is especially noticeable if CJ automatically answers the call about Big Smoke's Cash when exiting the boat.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If the player has a one-star wanted level and is being chased by a police officer, having the latter lured into attacking an NPC who will sometimes retaliate and fight back will not affect the officer's behavior. If the NPC attacks the officer while the wanted level remains, the officer will ignore the pedestrian and still try to arrest the player, unlike preceding 3D Universe game titles, where an NPC provoked via attacks from a police officer who is chasing the protagonist while having a low wanted level will fight back and the officer will flee and ignore the player if hit. However, if the officer is hit by an NPC while the player has no wanted level at all, the officer will try to kill the pedestrian regardless.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: This glitch may occur if the player attains a high wanted level, triggers a gang war, or defends a territory from an enemy gang attack. In these situations, the density of traffic (pedestrians and cars) is significantly reduced. However, in some occasion, when the player successfully evades the wanted levels or ends the gang war (by winning the territory or leaving the war zone), the traffic density will not be properly reset to the usual values (as defined in popcycle.dat game file). As a result, there may be either no cars will spawn at all but a few pedestrians still rarely spawn, or a few cars will spawn but lacking pedestrians, making the city seemingly abandoned. This glitch persists even after the player saves or reloads a save file, unless the player quits the game and restarts in another session (which refreshes the game memory).

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: reloads a save file, unless the player quits the game and restarts in another session (which refreshes the game memory). It occurs more often on a PC with low performance or if the game memory is full.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If the player drives a vehicle into a car mod shop, after quitting, pressing the button to emit the horn of the vehicle for a period of time before the door of the garage fully opens will instantly change the in-game radio station. This can also happen to a Pay 'n' Spray.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: In San Fierro, the two railroad crossings in Doherty have glitches on the signals; the barriers appear too high up and too far to the right. They are functional, but do not spawn correctly.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: Technically this glitch may occur if the CJ starts to date with any girlfriends (e.g. Denise Robinson, Katie Zhan) and takes them to a place (e.g. restaurants, clubs) then after it, the player must go the Gym, then get out of it and the progress made to your girlfriend will gradually increase and the date will be repeated all-over-the-time instead of waiting just go back to their house. Make sure you select the right place which your girlfriend wants, otherwise the progress made with your girlfriend will be decreased.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If the player reaches Santa Maria Beach, Mulholland and some places, they may have a chance to find a sheriff's deputy wandering there, although the sheriff's department have no property to control the city area. Rangers may also spawn driven. Also, in the mission Wrong Side of Tracks, if the player and Big Smoke kill the targets in a short time, after returning to the city, a sheriff's deputy may spawn, despite them being in the city. This is likely a spawning glitch.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: Many characters in the game the player does missions with have scripted reactions to Carl running over pedestrians. However, due to errors in the code they don't trigger as intended. The reactions will only trigger if the player runs over pedestrians with a Quad or when gently pushing them against the wall without making them fall.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: In The Definitive Edition, when an emergency vehicle has its sirens on near CJ, if the horn button ( by default on PC) is held down, the sirens will behave as if CJ were in the vehicle, playing a higher-pitched and faster siren (works on foot and while in any vehicle).

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: This glitch is occurred when CJ aims and shoot using a sniper rifle at the mirror on the safehouse wardrobe in a several times, can get kill himself.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: A game crash can occur if the player stands in place and drinks enough Sprunk. This occurs because the game's buffer only clears out items on the ground when the player gets far enough away from it, and by standing in place for a long time drinking Sprunk after Sprunk, the cans continue to accumulate, causing visual glitches such as CJ's hand disappearing, and the eventual crashing of the game. While this has been noticed recently in The Definitive Edition, specifically the Switch port, the glitch exists in all versions of the game. In The Definitive Edition of GTA San Andreas, if the crash lines up with an autosave, it will cause save file corruption.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: During a stormy weather at around the sunset time, most notably in the countryside areas, the sky unusually appears bloody red near the horizon (this is also known as the blood red fog), and greenish blue higher up. This glitch only occurs on the PC version of the game, because the PC version has an error in the timecyc.dat file which causes the game to set incorrect sky colors and ambient lighting at 20:00 during rainy weather in the countryside. The strange weather phenomenon can be observed after the first cutscene of the Vertical Bird mission where the weather is scripted to be always stormy.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If the player drives a vehicle and speeds near a pedestrian, they will sometimes jump directly in front of the vehicle instead of away from it; this may cause the player unintentionally running over the pedestrian, killing or injuring them. In such cases, the pedestrian AI tries to jump away from the player vehicle's path, but if the player changes their direction or turns slightly at the last second, the pedestrian may end up jumping in the wrong direction. This sometimes results in a one-star wanted level if the suicidal pedestrian happens to be a police officer or if the police sees the player committing the unintended roadkill. While this is quite common in GTA San Andreas, it has been rectified in later GTA games, and the glitch is almost nonexistent in the HD era games.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: If the player performs a bunny hop with any bike, and then presses the fire button immediately after letting go off the bunny hop button, the bike will go even higher.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: A glitch can occur when the player begins the Taxi Driver mission, but no fares are available. It happens when the player has crossed over the map boundaries (e.g. flying too far away from San Andreas). It is advised to complete the Taxi missions very early on in the game to avoid this glitch.

title: Glitches in GTA San Andreas
text: There is a common random factor of the game where airplanes crash to the ground or into buildings near CJ (with sometimes fatal or mission-failing consequences). Most crashes occur if the player is roaming around an area with many tall structures around them. The airplane may crash into one of these structures, making an audible explosion sound. However, there are also some instances where the player is on relatively flat ground and an airplane may just crash straight into the ground near them, or into the vehicle the player is in. Other crashes occur after CJ exits an interior after being inside for a few minutes and an aircraft spawns too low. Random crashes occur all around the state, most notably around Downtown Los Santos and San Fierro, or also in heavily forested areas like Whetstone. There are also frequent crashes on top of Mount Chiliad.

text: Some central or main characters have quotes when Carl bumps into them or attacks them to make them retaliate, but they are not displayed on-screen. If they are in a flipped or incinerating vehicle, or the vehicle CJ is driving gets crashed or is controlled with a high speed, especially during a certain mission, they will shout out something. title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas: Official Soundtrack
text:
Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas: Official Soundtrack is a three-disc compilation CD/DVD set containing a selection of music from the video game Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. It includes songs from each of the game's ten music radio stations, plus the "Theme from San Andreas". It was released internationally on November 23, 2004.

In addition to music, the CD also includes a bonus DVD containing the short film prequel The Introduction.

A more comprehensive soundtrack box set was also released in Europe on December 7, 2004, containing the majority of the music heard in the game.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas: Official Soundtrack Box Set
text:
Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas: Official Soundtrack Box Set is an eight-disc compilation CD box set containing music from the video game Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, featuring music from nine of the game's ten music radio stations. It was released in Europe on December 7, 2004. Unlike the previous soundtrack box set from Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, the eight CDs were not released for purchase individually.

Although the majority of the music from the game is included on the soundtracks, the CDs do not feature every song heard on the relevant radio station. In addition to music, each CD also includes station idents, plus two radio commercials heard in the game.

title: Mafia Boss Music

title: Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition
text:
O Mio Babbino Caro (Hudson Mohawke Remix) - Rockstar Games 
 Three iconic cities, three epic stories. Play the genre-defining classics of the original Grand Theft Auto Trilogy: Grand Theft Auto III, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City and Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas updated for a new generation, now with across-the-board enhancements including brilliant new lighting and environmental upgrades, with high-resolution textures, increased draw distances, Grand Theft Auto V-style controls and targeting, and much more, bringing these beloved worlds to life with all new levels of detail. Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition is a compilation of three remastered Grand Theft Auto games from the . It includes Grand Theft Auto III, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, and Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, originally released on the PlayStation 2 in 2001, 2002 and 2004 respectively.

The three games have been marketed as a trilogy since 2005 and on online PC gaming platforms such as Steam since at least January 2011. The Definitive Edition was officially announced by Rockstar Games on October 8th, 2021.

text:

The games were released digitally on November 11, 2021, and physically on December 17, 2021, and they are available on PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, Xbox Series X S, Xbox One, Nintendo Switch, and PC. Mobile versions for Apple iOS and Android were released on December 14, 2023, via Netflix subscription. The PC release was initially exclusive to the Rockstar Games Launcher, with a Steam release coming later on January 19, 2023, and an Epic Games Store release coming on February 15, 2023. title: Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition
text:
In August 2021, a report published by detailed that Rockstar Games was developing a remastered trilogy of Grand Theft Auto titles: Grand Theft Auto III, Vice City, and San Andreas, originally developed by Rockstar North. According to the report, its development was led by Rockstar Dundee and uses the Unreal Engine. In September, the in South Korea gave the trilogy a game rating. Media speculation about the game continued in early October after an update to the Rockstar Games Launcher included related data to the game in addition to logos, art, and game achievements.

Several days later, on October 8, 2021, Rockstar officially announced the remastered trilogy on its website and social media pages.

title: Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition
text:
s later, on October 8, 2021, Rockstar officially announced the remastered trilogy on its website and social media pages.

Existing versions of the three games were removed from digital retailers on October 11, 2021. Audiences and journalists criticized the move, citing concerns with video game preservation, a lack of choice between versions, and the potential removal of music due to expired licenses, which had occurred with previous re-releases.

After release, numerous graphical bugs and glitches, physics glitches from the GTA San Andreas mobile port, and a number of other issues plagued the titles. Switch users found The Definitive Edition unplayable due to framerate issues.

In the intervening time, many customers began flooding Take Two Interactive's and Rockstar's Twitter pages with demands for refunds.

title: Ballas (3D Universe)
text:
The Ballas have been around since the 1970s. Specific information regarding where or how they formed is unknown. However, it is likely that the Ballas evolved either from Glen Park or Jefferson, since Idlewood and possibly Willowfield were controlled by the Grove Street Families prior to 1987 and since East Los Santos was split between the Grove Street Families and the Vagos prior to 1992.

The Ballas have a long-running, intense and bloody rivalry with the Grove Street Families. The start date of the rivalry is unknown, but was in full swing by 1987.

Prior to 1992, the Ballas used to control the area of Temple which is under control of the Temple Drive Families in 1992. This is evidenced by the fact that the game references a fourth Ballas set known as the Temple Drive Ballas. Graffiti referring to the Temple Drive Ballas can also be found in Temple. However, the Temple Drive Ballas become active again after the Grove Street Families are weakened, allowing them to take back their former Temple territory from the Temple Drive Families.

The Ballas also establish ties with the Russian Mafia for weapons. Despite their business relationship with the Vagos, they will still react with hostilities on the streets it is possible only the higher-ranking OGs of the Vagos and the Ballas are involved in the business relationship.

Sweet is released from prison on the orders of Mike Toreno, and he and Carl rebuild the depleted Families by reclaiming Ganton, Glen Park and Idlewood from the Ballas while killing many of the drug dealers in the area, weakening the Ballas' stronghold in the drug dealing business. Carl later infiltrates Big Smoke's crack palace in East Los Santos where he confronts and kills Smoke. This weakens the Ballas further and causes them to lose more of their influence on the streets. If the player chooses, they can take over all Ballas territory in Los Santos, wiping the gang out for good.

title: Ballas (3D Universe)
text: The Ballas are an African-American street gang based in Los Santos. Most of their territory can be found in the poorer/run-down neighborhoods to the far east of the city. They are involved in gangbanging, gang warfare, street violence, prostitution, gang-related homicide, murder, drug trafficking/manufacturing (especially the crack cocaine trade), gun-running/arms trafficking, vandalism, and degeneracy. They are easily identifiable by wearing purple clothing as their gang color.

title: Ballas (3D Universe)
text:

They are the Grove Street Families' sworn enemy. They are enemies with all sets of the Families and the rivalry has been going on for several years as part of the Ballas-Grove Street war. The Ballas are also enemies with the two Los Santos Mexican/Latino gangs – the Los Santos Vagos and the Varrios Los Aztecas, though the rivalry is not as intense as it is with the Grove Street Families. It is unknown why their feud with the Mexican gangs exist, though it is likely that the Aztecas and Ballas (especially the Front Yard Ballas) developed a rivalry due to the close proximity of their territories (Willowfield/Idlewood and El Corona/Unity Station).

Despite their rivalry with the Los Santos Vagos on the streets, influential members from the Ballas and the Vagos maintain a business partnership for the interest of money and drugs. Both gangs provide protection for Big Smoke's crack empire.

The Ballas have ties with the San Fierro Rifa, Big Smoke, and the Loco Syndicate for narcotics (mainly crack cocaine), and the Russian Mafia for weapons. The Ballas also collaborate with C.R.A.S.H. Unlike the GSF, the Ballas have no reservations about making money by selling drugs; the spread of crack cocaine into the Grove Street community is part of their strategy to wipe the GSF out.

Like all gangs in GTA San Andreas, the Ballas have three skins that walk and drive around their territories.

title: Ballas (3D Universe)
text:
Their rivalry with the Grove Street Families is based on the rivalry of gangs and . Violence hit a peak in Los Angeles in the early-nineties due in part to the crack cocaine epidemic. Moreover, the Ballas are based on The Bloods, but their gang colors are based on those used by the Crips.

The Ballas and Grove Street Families are based on (who are actually maroon) and (who are green) respectively. Hearts and Hibs are both soccer teams based in , Scotland who have a great rivalry. Edinburgh is also the location of Rockstar North, which is why they chose these two teams.

title: Ballas (3D Universe)
text:
There are four sets of Ballas:
The Front Yard Ballas (FYB) territory is located in Idlewood and a part of East Los Santos.
The Rollin' Heights Ballas (RHB) territory is located in Jefferson, a part of East Los Santos, and a part of Willowfield.
The Kilo Tray Ballas (KTB) territory is located in most of Willowfield and in Glen Park.
The Temple Drive Ballas (TDB) territory is located in Verona Beach. After the completion of The Green Sabre, they take over Temple, Vinewood and Santa Maria Beach from the Temple Drive Families.

the completion of The Green Sabre, they take over Temple, Vinewood and Santa Maria Beach from the Temple Drive Families.

Each set is differentiated into different territories and neighorhoods. Apart from this, they are all the same and are all represented under the "Ballas" banner, all wear purple attire, are all enemies of all Grove sets, and are all heavily involved in the drugs trade. All sets are also strongly allied throughout the events of San Andreas unlike the Grove sets at the beginning of the game.

The Front Yard Ballas are the largest and most active set. The Front Yard Ballas are also Los Santos' most notorious drug dealers, the primary enemy of the Grove Families. The FYB are also the primary source of spreading drugs into Grove Street territory from their crack houses in Idlewood.

title: Ballas (3D Universe)
text:
The FYB are also the primary source of spreading drugs into Grove Street territory from their crack houses in Idlewood.

The Ballas employ a drug/hit strategy to wipe out their main enemy the Grove Family sets (especially the Grove Street set). This strategy involves the Front Yard Ballas supplying their territory with large amounts of drugs (mainly crack cocaine) to weaken them, while the other sets perform hit and run tactics such as drive-by shootings.

title: Ballas (3D Universe)
text:
rugs (mainly crack cocaine) to weaken them, while the other sets perform hit and run tactics such as drive-by shootings.

The Ballas primarily make money by selling drugs (especially crack cocaine) which they primarily get from the San Fierro Rifa, the Loco Syndicate, and Big Smoke. They then use this money to acquire various weapons; primarily from the Russian Mafia. Any remaining drug supply is then sold to other dealers who have no gang affiliation in the Grove territory in an attempt to weaken them (as it would be too dangerous for a Balla to sell in enemy territory).

In addition to being a regular street gang, the Ballas are also hired by Big Smoke to provide protection for his drug empire in exchange for money and crack cocaine. This protection duty is one exception in the game where the Ballas and Vagos cooperate with each other despite being enemies on the streets.

title: Ballas (3D Universe)
text: Although they are seen with Voodoos in some missions (i.e. Sweet & Kendl and Drive-Thru), the Ballas only have two gang cars, the Tahoma and the Majestic. The Tahoma is a lowrider and sometimes appears with hydraulics. The Ballas prefer to use the Tahoma for drive-by shootings due to its four-door capability, as opposed to the Majestic which is only a two-door vehicle. In the mission Catalyst, they use also a Greenwood, which is primarily a Grove Street Families car. In the mission Los Sepulcros, they use a unique black and blue Greenwood for backup. On one very important occasion, the Ballas use a green Sabre to murder Beverly Johnson in a drive-by shooting. In the Sabre and Voodoo's cases, it is implied they use these vehicles to avoid suspicion. The Ballas' favorite radio station is Bounce FM.

title: Dolphins
text: Dolphins are an animal species featured in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, Grand Theft Auto V, GTA Online and . In all of their appearances, the species of dolphin that is featured seems to be the , scientifically known as Tursiops truncatus.

title: Dolphins
text: Dolphins are marine mammals found in large water bodies in both GTA Vice City and GTA San Andreas, alongside other marine animals such as sharks, sea turtles and jellyfish. Being background models in both games, dolphins take no damage when they are shot at by the player, and the player cannot interact with them in any way. However, in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, the player can kill a dolphin (and any sea creature present in the game, like sea turtles and sharks) by throwing grenades at it. The dolphin model also lacks moving animation, therefore it stays still while swimming.

title: Dolphins
text:
Dolphins return in the enhanced version of Grand Theft Auto V. Unlike sharks, they never attack the player when swimming in the water. They may however approach the player if they are wearing Scuba gear or controlling a submersible.

Dolphins are one of the animal species the player may experience when consuming a Peyote Plant in GTA V. As part of the continuation of The Diamond Casino & Resort update, Peyote Plants were also added to Grand Theft Auto Online.

A pod of dolphins can be spotted during the first few moments of GTA VI s first trailer.

title: Flash
text: The Flash appears to be primarily based on the , most evident in its front and rear fascia, with possible secondary influence from the . It is rendered lower and wider than both, making it one of the smallest and lowest cars in the game. Its front bumper and fog lights are derived from those of the .

title: Flash
text:
Like most tuners in the game, the body is weak, making the Flash susceptible to intense damage from high-speed impacts and heavy gunfire. The Flash has excellent handling due to its front wheel drive, which minimizes spinouts and burnouts, as well as excellent acceleration and speed due to its light weight and powerful engine. The car is considered as one of the best handling cars in the game. Traction and grip are amazing. Its supreme handling makes the car almost impossible to oversteer. These traits make the Flash an ideal car for street racing, especially with a nitro upgrade. It is also useful for evading the police.

The Flash has the same engine sound as the Blista Compact, Club, Esperanto, Feltzer, Jester, Majestic and Tahoma.

title: Basejump Challenge
text: Basejump Challenge is a removed vehicle side-mission cut during the development of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Basejump Challenge
text:
At some point in early development, a side-mission involving Parachute jumps was planned. The mission consisted of basejumping from two unspecified peaks around San Andreas.

The first variation of the side-mission involved landing on a target, a similar task included in the Pilot School. The second variation of the side-mission involved using a bike to launch the player across the cliff at full speed and landing on the water within a 20-second limit.

Leftovers of this side-mission can be found in the notusedtext.txt file, a text file containing early american.gxt entries scrapped by the original Rockstar North developers, and accidentally left in the files of the original release of Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition by Grove Street Games.

title: Ammu-Nation (3D Universe)
text:
is the Ammu-Nation Film Festival, with free screenings of the documentary Red Dawn! Ammu-Nation: Protecting your rights! The name Ammu-Nation is a portmanteau of ammunition and nation, which implies that the store is patriotic. The store is run with a right-wing paranoia philosophy, describing itself as the "store leading the fight against communism". The store also seems to promote the purchase of its products for illegal purposes, even suggesting they be used to kill one's mother-in-law if she is "being a bitch".

It is implied that Ammu-Nation existed in the 1950s as a gun association with Derek the Dodo as a mascot to teach kids about gun safety, before Ammu-Nation has been rebranded as a firearms emporium in 1978.

Ammu-Nation's first chronological appearance in 1984. Derek the Dodo is still a mascot for the company, used to entice children into using guns at Saturday Safety Fun and to shift blame to "anti-gun zealots". Vice City Mambas football player José Pimsoll is also a supporter for Ammu-Nation.

In 1986, the store is giving away an anti-aircraft gun used by American army during the Australian-American War, and opened a shooting range featuring images of famous communists as targets. The Vice City Bureau of Investigation is currently investigating Ammu-Nation and other Hardware Stores around Vice City, with posters labelling them as "suspicious businesses" in their office.

Many of the ammunition boxes found inside Ammu-Nation stores around San Andreas are static versions of Category:Ammunition items used in Rockstar North's Manhunt.

In the late 1990s, Ammu-Nation opened an online service at AmmuNation.net. Following the mass hysteria, Ammu-Nation began selling the "Strongest Will Survive" Y2K Kit exclusively on their website, which consisted of a tractor trailer full of Logger Beer, Redwood Cigarettes and enough fire power and ammunition to level a small country.

text:
The Downtown Vice City store originally used an image of Ronald Reagan (President of the United States in the 1980s, mentioned multiple times in-game) shooting at an image of ( in the 1980s) using a Desert Eagle. The sign alludes to the description of the Ammu-Nation shooting ranges in the radio commercial, featuring faces of "famous Commie pinkos".

The level designers decided not to use the shooting range sign in the final version and, instead of removing it, they simply changed the X coordinate until it was moved behind the interior wall. The LOD texture for the Ammu-Nation interior still features the sign in the original location.

The sign can be visible using an exploit through weapons with First Person availability, allowing the player to see through walls.

The mission was designed by Neil Ferguson at Rockstar North and is labelled as " WUZI_3 ", taking place between Amphibious Assault (" WUZI_2 ") and The Da Nang Thang (" WUZI_4 "), after the arrival of the Red Gecko Tong to discuss a way to stop the attacks from the Da Nang Boys on the San Fierro Triads.

While there are no leftovers of the mission in the final version, a notusedtext.txt text file was unintentionally left in the files for the original releases of Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition by Grove Street Games, listing old unused text scrapped from the GXT file by Rockstar North during the game's early development, including mission text for the mission '7'. Prior to that, the only evidence of the cut mission in the original releases was the missing GXT entry between WUZI_2 and WUZI_4 .

hat, the only evidence of the cut mission in the original releases was the missing GXT entry between WUZI_2 and WUZI_4 .

The mission was cut in an early stage of development, as evidenced by the mission text still using the placeholder "Character: Quote" format and Scottish terms used by Rockstar North.

The mission consisted of a stealth mission set during night time at a heavily guarded Triad complex, occupied by an unspecified Triad gang from the San Fierro Triads. Certain objectives suggest this complex is used as a front for a prostitution ring. The mission used certain gameplay mechanics from the mission Home Invasion ("Noise" meter and "Light" countdown), the Manhunt-inspired shadow hiding mechanic introduced in Madd Dogg's Rhymes, and a vague "Stealth" HUD indicator.

The context behind Woozie's order to kill a Triad boss and the location of the complex are not specified in the leftover text. There are no locations in Chinatown and surrounding neighborhoods that can be identified as a Triad complex, other than the storehouse used by the defunct Blood Feather Triad, which does not match with the description of the Triad complex of the mission (building with shadows to hide).

The main objective is to murder the Triad boss by performing the "traditional execution", unspecified in the leftover text. The player has the ability to liberate a gimp inside the complex and obtain the Gimp Suit. The costume appears to have been used for a checkpoint system, giving the player the ability to return to the gimp's cell whenever they are detected by a guard. The mission is failed if the boss escapes the Triad complex alive after being alerted by the guards.

title: Aeroplane
text: The Aeroplane, also known as the Air Train, is an uncontrollable passenger airplane appearing in Grand Theft Auto III, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, GTA Liberty City Stories and GTA Vice City Stories. The uncontrollable vehicle is left unused in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Aeroplane
text:
The vehicle is named after the European aerospace corporation , and certain details of the vehicle such as the windshield are reminiscent of those on older Airbus models. It also appears to take inspiration from the , with adjustments made to its design such as shorter outboard engines and differently designed wing ailerons.

The original design in Grand Theft Auto III is depicted as a DMAir plane, which is itself a reference to DMA Design, Rockstar North's former name. The logo is replaced with the Air Rockstar company logo in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. On the landing gear doors is "T2", which is a reference to Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar Games's parent company.

title: Aeroplane
text:
City. On the landing gear doors is "T2", which is a reference to Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar Games's parent company.

Both the vehicle and static versions have been redesigned in Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories, now having less and bigger windows, a hump and raised cockpit reminiscent of the and a more cartoonish look overall. In Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories, the appearance of the actual vehicle has been reverted to its original design, while its static variant appears as a Plummet Airlines passenger airplane with an extra floor for its cockpit, also similar to a Boeing 747.

title: Aeroplane
text:
iant appears as a Plummet Airlines passenger airplane with an extra floor for its cockpit, also similar to a Boeing 747.

The Aeroplane has been left unused in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas due to the previous path-controlled air traffic system being replaced with a limited AI-controlled air traffic system using normal vehicles with normal vehicle physics. Only its textureless model, handling data and in-game text string are left in the game files, revealing that the vehicle has been renamed to "Air Train" to keep consistency with its data name before being ultimately cut.

In The Definitive Edition, the Airtrains found at Escobar International Airport feature various colored paint jobs, without liveries. The colors include bright red, yellow, cyan and black. The standard 'Rockstar' branded variant remains white.

title: Aeroplane
text:
liveries. The colors include bright red, yellow, cyan and black. The standard 'Rockstar' branded variant remains white.

In , the vehicle is absent; however, static planes intended to represent the stationary planes from Grand Theft Auto III can be found in Francis International Airport.

title: Aeroplane
text:
The vehicle uses colored coronastar effects to simulate the airplane's navigation lights. As the Aeroplane takes off and reaches the game's height limit, it uses a white line effect to simulate far away , only intended to be seen from afar.

Both effects have been kept in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, except for the vehicle model, to depict far away planes intended to be seen from the ground. However, the height limit update for the player-controlled aircrafts unintentionally creates a flaw in which the player is able to reach the invisible airplanes, which are depicted as blinking coronastar lights leaving a contrail line behind them.

Similarly to other coronastar lights in the game (i.e. Snapshot indicators), the airplane nav lights are not visible during daytime, leaving only the contrails visible.

title: Aeroplane
text:
The Aeroplane's performance cannot be observed by the player as, even if the vehicle is obtained via exploits, the vehicle is limited to a scripted path in all of its appearances and its course cannot be changed through normal vehicle controls. If an Aeroplane is generated (only possible through modifications), the game will crash as the vehicle relies on a scripted path.

Unlike other path-controlled aircraft (such as the "dead" Dodo and Helicopter), the vehicle ignores any projectile impact and cannot be destroyed with missiles fired from Rocket Launchers or vehicle-mounted missiles.

title: Aeroplane
text:
res any projectile impact and cannot be destroyed with missiles fired from Rocket Launchers or vehicle-mounted missiles.

Also similarly to the aforementioned vehicles, the Aeroplane is not solid, meaning the player can go through it without taking any damage. Exclusive to the handheld titles (Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories), the vehicle has collision, however in GTA Liberty City Stories, touching the plane will instantly kill the player, and if the player was in a vehicle, the vehicle will instantly explode. In GTA Vice City Stories, touching the plane's wheels will gradually injure the player and cause ordinary damage to their vehicle. The vehicle also allows the player to stand on top of it while it takes off before being automatically ejected upon reaching the game's height limit.

title: Aeroplane
text:
Skins#Oversights 
In both the original PC versions of Grand Theft Auto III and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, when loading a custom skin that has the letter e as the 21st character of its filename, it will trigger a bug that will corrupt the aircraft path data, causing them to fly in or below the ground. This is because the game somehow reads the character as an exponential function, thus causing errors in the CPlane function, which handles the aircraft's flight path.

title: Aeroplane
text: Similarly to any other path-controlled vehicle in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, approaching the Aeroplane as it crosses the map's limit results in a crash (Unhandled exception c0000005 at random addresses). This can only be observed by normal means with the Aeroplane and the uncontrollable VCPD Helicopter.

title: Aeroplane
text:
The flying version of the plane can be accessed in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories through a glitch – if the player gets on the wing while the plane taxis from one runway to the other, and presses the triangle button near the intersection point between the back of the wing and the fuselage, they will be transported inside of the airplane.

The player doesn't have any control of the vehicle itself and can only change the radio stations while it flies on its predefined route. The player can only exit the Aeroplane when its back wheels are touching the ground but not the front one, which is when it takes off and lands.

title: Stratum (3D Universe)
text: The design of the Stratum appears to be mostly taken from the , with the addition of painted D-pillars. This, however, contradicts the 1992 setting of the game. This might suggest that the Stratum could also be loosely inspired, in essence, by the , which features a similarly slanted front end, a comparable name, and a fitting production history.

title: Stratum (3D Universe)
text: The Stratum assumes a more streamlined design compared to the Solair, and it is considered a tuner. The front of the car has a panel between the headlights in place of a regular grille, black details on the doors and around the windows, and small red tail lights on the rear quarters. The gas cap can be seen on the rear right side. The car spawns in a variety of single colors applied on the body.

title: Stratum (3D Universe)
text: Acceleration and speed are surprisingly impressive, considering the Stratum's size. The drivetrain is front-engine, rear-drive, making the Stratum a good selection as a drive-by vehicle. The body is weak, however, making the car susceptible to intense damage from high-speed impacts and heavy gunfire.

title: Elegy
text: The Elegy is based on the , which was only officially sold in Japan as well as Australia. They were never sold in the USA, although several were imported and made "legal" by Motorex, which was only founded in 1999. It actually seems to be an amalgamation of various Skylines, taking its squarish front mostly from the , and its basic shape from the . The vehicle's tail lights and rear fascia bear a close resemblance to those of the R34. The Elegy is rear-wheel drive, unlike the well known , which is all-wheel drive, but the Elegy's understated styling, closed grille, and lack of any large rear wing means it's likely to be more closely related to RWD Skylines such as the , or the R34 GTT, as well as the US legal Skyline GT-Rs imported by Motorex which have been converted from AWD to RWD. The stock wheels resemble the R33 GT-R's stock wheels.

title: Elegy
text: Acceleration, speed, and handling are very impressive, but has a huge amount of torque, causing burnouts, fishtailing and oversteer as the engine tends to overpower the drivetrain, threatening to spin it out if attempting to turn in corners. This also makes the Elegy virtually unmanageable at high speeds after a back tire has been shot out, making it extremely difficult to maintain control. Because of the massive power, the Elegy spins out when drifting. The Elegy has a short wheelbase and strong body, so it is capable of withstanding a good deal of damage. With a little practice, the Elegy can be used as a drift car without the use of handling mods. Both the acceleration and top speed are top of the line.

text: In literature, Elegy is a mournful, melancholic or plaintive poem. The Elegy is used by the San Fierro Triads as one of their gang cars, alongside the Sultan and the Stratum, which are also both tuners. Due to the lower height of its driver's seat, CJ will kick the car's occupant when stealing the car. The Skoiloine, a beta vehicle from Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories, is possibly based on the Elegy. The Annis Elegy RH8, a vehicle in Grand Theft Auto V, is the Elegy's successor. It is based on the Nissan GT-R, which is a real-life successor to the GT-R R32, the car which the Elegy is based upon. title: FBI Truck
text: The FBI Truck is an armored law enforcement vehicle that was cut during the development of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: FBI Truck
text: The FBI Truck is depicted as an anti-riot armored truck based on the , albeit with conventional front-hinged doors instead of the Ranger's rear-hinged doors, and no rear doors.

title: FBI Truck
text: The front of the truck features a small painted bumper at the bottom and a large grille in the center, while the sections beside the grille house circular headlights above and small turn signals below. The hood area is slightly slanted in shape and opens to reveal the engine bay, while two circular mirrors can be seen mounted on the front quarters. On the sides, the truck has bulky steps in the middle of the wheelbase area and large access doors with visible hinges, small handles and narrow windows, along with smaller windows and a left-side fuel cap on the rear compartment. The cabin area has a split windshield on the front, while the roof of the rear compartment features a hatch where a member of the FBI can shoot from (unopenable to the player if they were to spawn the vehicle).

title: FBI Truck
text:
features a hatch where a member of the FBI can shoot from (unopenable to the player if they were to spawn the vehicle). The rear end features small windows on the upper area, as well as a gray bumper at the bottom, with a license plate in the center and circular tail lights above the outer edges.

Like the S.W.A.T., the FBI Truck is depicted with a navy blue color and San Andreas Police Department markings (a rather unusual feature for an FBI vehicle, quite possibly due to it being originally intended for use by the SWAT). Like the Barracks and the aforementioned S.W.A.T., the truck also has a siren but no strobe/beacon lights.

title: FBI Truck
text:
The FBI Truck is a rugged, near-indestructible police vehicle. The all-wheel-drive layout handles well on rough terrain and is capable of high speeds, making up for its poor steering and braking at high speed due to its weight.

Although it is a well-armored police vehicle, it has an average damage-proof body, like most vehicles in-game. It cannot take many major hits from larger vehicles and it is not bulletproof either, withstanding bullets better than an average vehicle, but for a limited time only.

The truck uses a diesel engine and a 5-speed gearbox to power all wheels. It shares the sound with the S.W.A.T., the Barracks OL and the Enforcer.

title: FBI Truck

The Las Venturas Police Department (LVPD) is a law enforcement agency in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, servicing the city of Las Venturas and is a branch of the agency responsible for the entire state of San Andreas; the San Andreas Police Department.

title: Las Venturas Police Department
text: The LVPD is modeled after the . LVPD officers mostly travel in pairs inside a police car and many officers walk the streets of Las Venturas. Similarly to the San Andreas Sheriff, its officers seem to have racist views, judging by their busting quotes. Moreover, the officers working at the Roca Escalante precinct are described as "red neck hick bastards".

title: Las Venturas Police Department
text: The LVPD's headquarters is located in the northeast part of the city, in the Roca Escalante district, and it is where the player will respawn after being arrested anywhere within Las Venturas city limits. The police station is accessible and contains three weapons inside: a shotgun, a pistol and a nightstick, as well as body armor. The police parking lot has two floors. Another mechanical garage door on the right-hand side of the station leads to the underground parking lot.

title: Las Venturas Police Department
text: LVPD officers wear a light khaki shirt, light khaki pants with black stripe, black shoes and a silver shield badge.

title: Las Venturas Police Department
text: The primary means of transportation for officers in Las Venturas is the Police car. Interestingly, the police car in Las Venturas is unique, being based on a singular platform not used for any other vehicles in the game. The police cars in Los Santos and San Fierro are based on the Premier, a common civilian vehicle inspired by an early-mid 90s , while the LVPD cruiser has styling cues taken from a late 80's Caprice, with the overall dimensions of the vehicle being closer to those of a . The Predator is also used by LVPD officers to patrol the waters surrounding Las Venturas.

title: Las Venturas Police Department
text: Every patrol officer carries a pistol and a nightstick as their main weapons, although they will also use shotguns when the player has a wanted level of at least three stars.

title: Las Venturas Police Department
text:
The Las Venturas Police Department patch seen on their headquarters is the same as that of the Liberty City Police Department, as is their motto Taking the Law into Our own Hands.
LVPD officers can sometimes be seen in the northern fringes of Red County.

title: Impounded
text:
The mission was designed by level designer Kevin Bolt at Rockstar North and featured one motion captured cutscene at the start. Similarly to Cesar's previous mission (and only remaining mission of his Los Santos mission strand), the mission required the player to drive a vehicle into the mission marker in order to start the mission.

While this second mission for Cesar Vialpando has been cut, High Stakes, Low-Rider is still commented out as part of a "mission strand" in the phone calls script file.

There are several leftovers of the mission in the game files for the final release, including mission text and audio files for scripted dialogue and cutscene. Moreover, with the release of The Definitive Edition, the outsourced Grove Street Games studio developers unintentionally shipped the original release version with all uncompiled mission scripts, a notusedtext.txt file listing old scrapped american.gxt text lines, and other proprietary Rockstar North tools in the game's directory, including the full uncompiled cesar2.sc script file for Impounded.

An early development version which consisted of stealing a "nice car" from the Impound Garage and delivering it to a lock-up.

Both concepts of the mission had the intention of introducing the player to the Impound Garage feature, which is fully functional in-game but never properly introduced due to all instruction notes being cut along with the mission.

text: The police station section of the mission (cops, parking gate, garage door, parked vehicles and pedestrian animations in the underground parking lot) relies entirely on the external script for the Impound Garage environment ( impound.sc ), which is normally loaded outside missions whenever the player approaches the police station.

title: Impounded
text:

In addition, the mission script spawns two cops as enemies on the way out – the only two enemies spawned by the actual mission script.

title: Impounded
text: The mission is completed by losing the wanted level while driving the mission objective vehicle. While the mission suggests the player use the Pay 'n' Spray, the script allows the player the complete the mission by losing the wanted level through alternative ways, such as collecting police bribes.

title: Jefferson Motel (3D Universe)
text:
The Jefferson Motel is a large, accessible two-floor motel building located in northern Jefferson in Los Santos, San Andreas. 

The interior is accessible to the player as soon as they gain control of Carl Johnson during In the Beginning. It is only accessible through the parking lot entrance and cannot be entered from the rooftop. The interior has a total of eight accessible rooms, all sharing a similar layout. A Sprunk vending machine is located in the reception room.

The southern wall of the motel also has one of the 100 Tags that can be sprayed, and a SMG pickup on the roof.

The interior itself is designed for the Los Santos Police Department's SWAT unit raid, thus is always seen with barricades made of tables and missing doors and skylight that are spawned by mission script.

title: Jefferson Motel (3D Universe)
text: The motel is the meeting place for the Grove Street Families and its two split sets, the Seville Boulevard Families and Temple Drive Families during the mission Reuniting the Families. The meeting, aimed at re-uniting the two sets with the original gang, is ambushed by the police. This results in a major shootout between the gangs and the SWAT unit in the interior of the building, and Carl Johnson fighting his way through the heavily armed SWAT officers to find and rescue his brother Sweet Johnson from one of the motel rooms.

title: Jefferson Motel (3D Universe)
text:
The building originally had a pool on its eastern side, and a row of small buildings in its southern side, near the rear staircase. In the final version, the pool is replaced with a small garden and the row of buildings have been removed, leaving an empty lot. The tile of water intended for the removed pool can still be found below the terrain.
 Row of buildings in the backlot of the Jefferson Motel, as seen in a promotional screenshot (scan).

title: Jefferson Motel (3D Universe)
text:
The interior of the Hashbury Safehouse is located high above the skylight in the second lobby, and its save point icon is visible from below while not in a mission.
The safehouse interior itself is invisible as the player currently has the Interior World 15 loaded for the Jefferson Motel, while the Hashbury Safehouse is located by Interior World 10.
The model of the motel rooms were originally intended to repurposed for two acquirable Motel Rooms, which were intended to act as safehouses. The interior of both Motel Rooms are still present, with remnants of the Jefferson Motel hallway visible on their models.

title: Los Santos Police Department (3D Universe)
text: The Los Santos Police Department (LSPD) is a branch of the San Andreas Police Department servicing the city of Los Santos in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Los Santos Police Department (3D Universe)
text:
Modeled after the (LAPD), the LSPD are a prominent part of the storyline in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

The LSPD houses a branch known as C.R.A.S.H. (, based on an anti-gang branch of the LAPD), of which officers Frank Tenpenny, Eddie Pulaski, and Jimmy Hernandez are members. Tenpenny is also represented as the main antagonistic element throughout the game's entire storyline, and he, along with Pulaski, who is also an antagonist, use their authority as LSPD officers to achieve their sinister ends.

The LSPD seems to host the only SWAT team in San Andreas, as the Enforcers that appear when the player has a wanted level of at least four stars have LSPD markings on them, regardless of the player's location.

title: Los Santos Police Department (3D Universe)
text:
The department's headquarters sits adjacent to Los Santos City Hall in the Pershing Square district of Los Santos, San Andreas. This is where the player respawns after being arrested anywhere within Los Santos city limits.

There is another LSPD station in Verona Beach. Unlike the other police stations, it does not serve as a spawn point after the player is arrested within Verona Beach.

While the LSPD does not have any jurisdiction in Red County, there is a police station just outside Los Santos in Dillimore, which has the same interior as the LSPD headquarters, indicating it is a joint police station between the Los Santos Police Department and the San Andreas Sheriff, due to the town's close proximity.

title: Los Santos Police Department (3D Universe)
text: LSPD officers wear a dark blue shirt, dark blue pants, black shoes and a golden shield badge. C.R.A.S.H. members wear the same uniform as above, except with an additional patch on the right arm. LSPD SWAT officers wear a dark blue long-sleeved shirt with a dark blue body armor, dark blue pants with a holster, black boots, dark blue gloves, black balaclava and a dark blue combat helmet with combat googles. In The Definitive Edition, regular patrol officers may now appear with different ethnicities, facial hair, and sunglasses.

title: Los Santos Police Department (3D Universe)
text: The Police car is the main vehicle of the LSPD. It is a modified Premier with a custom paint job and a light bar. The same vehicle is also issued to C.R.A.S.H. members. LSPD SWAT officers respond in the Enforcer when the player reaches a four-star wanted level. LSPD officers may be also seen using the Predator around Los Santos waters. Also, the LSPD uses Police Mavericks, HPV1000s and the S.W.A.T. (the last only during End of the Line).

title: Los Santos Police Department (3D Universe)
text: Every patrol officer carries a pistol and a nightstick as their main weapons, although they will also use shotguns when the player has a wanted level of at least three stars. Additionally, officers are seen using SMGs during Reuniting the Families and Micro SMGs in End of the Line.

text: The Downtown Skyscraper is an unnamed building complex appearing in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Downtown Skyscraper
text:
It is a complex made up of three buildings. The first and tallest building has 43 floors, and is made up of a black facade with white concrete trims. It is also the fourth tallest building in San Fierro. The second building is identical in appearance to the first one, but slightly smaller, and the third building is no less than one floor tall. All buildings in the complex have a small green pyramid-shaped structure on their roof.

The complex features underground parking garage, with a long tunnel entrance that can be explored by the player. The garage door is permanently closed with a warning sign reading "No Entry. Unsafe Building", which implies the parking garage has been deemed unsafe due to San Andreas earthquakes. Despite this fact, NPC drivers can be seen leaving the parking garage when player approaches the building.

text: Gang 9 and Gang 10 are unused gangs appearing in the game's code in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Gang 9 and Gang 10
text:
Originally, the game's developers planned to add 10 unique gangs
, however, " Gang 9 " and " Gang 10 " were never finished or forgotten during the development of the game.
When spawned in GTA San Andreas, they appear as the Varrios Los Aztecas, but will act as San Fierro Rifa members.

The gangs don't appear in the game outside of using cheats or mods. The gangs can be found by entering a cheat.

As noted above, the gang members of the unused gangs use the same character models as the Varrios Los Aztecas, with no changes in their external look. Their behavior, however, is different; they won't attack Carl at first sight, nor will they confront him if he strays too far inside their gang area. The vehicles they drive are Sentinels.

title: Fanny Batters
text:
Fanny Batters is a brothel, containing a bar and several rooms. Sex toys and tapes are sold in the interior, although not purchasable by the player.

Unlike other unused brothel interiors, Fanny Batters appears to be a completely modeled interior. As there are no door markers in the exterior world that lead to Fanny Batters, it is left unused in the game. The building in which the brothel is located is unknown.

text: The Freight Box is a that was cut during the development of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. It was intended for the Freight as an alternative to the flatcar.

title: Freight Box
text:
The Freight Box seems to be based on an American 50ft box car, but given a rounded top rather than a slightly sloped top. 

The Freight Box features a long chassis with twin-axle s, circular lights on both ends and small steps on each quarter, but lacks physical (likely due to it being an unfinished vehicle) and has headlights on both ends. Even though the doors on either side of the car are both open, the player cannot jump in, as there is an invisible wall. The train car is only seen in a rusty/worn light blue color.

title: Freight Box
text:
The Freight Box is shown to have similar properties to the Brown Streak and the Freight, in that it is immune to all forms of damage, including weapon damage, fire, and any physical obstruction.

The train car uses the same handling line as the Freight flatcar.

title: Freight Box
text:
A prop variant can be found parked on the tracks inside the Ocean Docks Freight Depot in Ocean Docks. Unlike the cut vehicle, this variant is based on a typical American boxcar with a flat top and a lack of buffers, although it is substantially shorter than either the cut vehicle or the real thing.

The model is substantially lower quality than the cut vehicle, consisting mostly of flat surfaces with textures applied, as opposed to the cut vehicle's modeled doors, ladders, and brackets. The boxcar comes in a faded yellow livery with black doors reminiscent of the real-life . Unlike the cut vehicle, these boxcars can be entered, but they are all empty except for one, which has a Sawed-off Shotgun pickup.

title: Interiors in GTA San Andreas
text:
Building interiors are first made visible with the series' transition to full 3D graphics with the release of Grand Theft Auto III.

In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, most of the interiors are placed in empty parallel worlds, usually high above the aircraft height limits. The player is teleported to these interiors through the yellow Enter-Exit arrows found in front of certain building entrance doors in the "exterior world". The function of these yellow arrows is to teleport the player from the entrance of the building to the corresponding interior of the building.

These separate "worlds" consists of replicas of the in-game map, where the main map's terrain and objects, except for their collision models, are completely unloaded and invisible, while each individual building interior model is made visible.

title: Interiors in GTA San Andreas
text:
Similarly to the interiors in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, certain interiors have unique ambience sounds.
Fast food restaurants have cutlery and fryer sounds.
Fancy restaurants have unique ambience music (although muted during their only appearance in the dating activity cutscenes).
Tuning garages, wardrobes and other interiors have in-game radio stations playing in the background.

title: Interiors in GTA San Andreas
text: Particle effects used in interiors such as fire, water and smoke are loaded in the exterior world, although not normally visible without using glitches and exploits.

title: Interiors in GTA San Andreas
text: Dynamic objects that can be moved through the player's interactions or mission script are normally visible in the world. This includes physical doors used to load interiors, garage doors and interactive cranes.

title: Interiors in GTA San Andreas
text:
The skybox is present inside interiors, and has two variations.
The colored skybox is used to simulate the exterior world's skybox and its weather presets. However, it does not feature particle effects such as clouds, rainbows or rain. It is mainly used for interiors with visible "fake" exterior, such as Marco's Bistro and World of Coq.
The black skybox is intended for interiors without any visible exterior (windows closed). Despite the visual darkness, the weather presets and dynamic light sources are normally applied to the world itself. It is mainly used by all interiors that are normally loaded by ENEX arrows and mission markers, including all clothing stores, barber shops, restaurants, and it simulates the black ceiling inside stadiums.

title: Interiors in GTA San Andreas
text: In the PlayStation 2 version, two of the existing Ammu-Nation interiors (the Downtown Los Santos and Queens branches) have a large, inaccessible empty room located next to the shooting range, behind the door at the side of the room. This, along with unused targets of characters from GTA III, implies that an extra shooting range challenge, similar to the one featured in The Shootist/Rifle Range in GTA Vice City, was planned at some point in development. This room was cut in all subsequent ports.

title: Interiors in GTA San Andreas
text:
otist/Rifle Range in GTA Vice City, was planned at some point in development. This room was cut in all subsequent ports.

Normally, the room can only be seen from the outside by using a jetpack to navigate all the way to the interior. The ceiling can only be seen from certain angles, becoming fully invisible if it is landed on. The ceiling, the walls and the floor are all solid, indicating that the room was not a last minute addition. Looking from the room towards the shooting range, a space may be seen in a wall from certain angles, instead of the door that can be properly seen if looking from the shooting range towards the empty room.

Another view of the ceiling. Notice how the door that separates the shooting range from the empty room is properly displayed from this angle.

title: Interiors in GTA San Andreas
text:
Due to a glitch involving the Jetpack cheat in the introductory mission In the Beginning, certain interior ENEX arrows available only through mission script can be unlocked.

If the player enables the Jetpack cheat during the Police Car segment, while Carl is inside the vehicle, the mission won't be able to throw him out of the car in the alleyway in order to progress. Instead, the player is Wasted and sent to the nearby hospital.

Afterwards, seven ENEX arrows are unlocked in the map. All of these arrows are intended to be available during missions only, and unavailable before and after completing the mission (except for the Ammu-Nation, which is temporarily disabled until its introduction).
