title: Interiors in GTA San Andreas
text:
Due to a glitch in the PC version, smoke particle generators used in interiors (Millie Perkins's bedroom torches/Cluckin' Bell fryers) may be visible from afar by the player: if the interior is entered, the particles are generated for a few seconds, after which the player can exit the interior and quickly look at the interior's location in the sky.

The Fort Carson Cluckin' Bell is the easiest area to use to spot the smoke particles in the sky, due to its close proximity to the Cluckin' Bell sky interior location.

 The smoke particle generator used in the fryer at Cluckin' Bell (Int 9).

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: This subpage documents removed, unused and changed characters (pedestrians and cutscene models) during the development of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
Bobbi La Queef 
Bobbi La Queef was a cut cheerleader girlfriend, intended to be found at the Verona Beach Gym in Los Santos. The only leftover of this character in the game files is the interior of her bedroom, recycled in-game as the interior of Katie Zhan's House.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
Honey-G 
Honey-G was a cut media personality girlfriend, originally scheduled to be introduced after Cut Throat Business, with Carl Johnson appointing her as the new manager for Madd Dogg. There are no leftovers of this girlfriend in the game files or script.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
An unidentified pedestrian texture and model is used as the base for the chopped body parts produced by the Combine Harvester. The texture image is internally named billyblood (texture container: dead_mantxd.txd ) and depicts an unused mechanic pedestrian texture under the blood overlay.

The official strategy guide section for the Tanker Commander mission (page 67) suggests this is a white skin variant of an early version of one of the pool players/Madd Dogg's security guards. "Billyblood" uses a similar head model as the removed cshelper and cshelper2 (security guards) and pool players seen in the official strategy guide.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: An unidentified motel employee affiliated with officer Frank Tenpenny. He was originally intended to make a minor appearance, providing a shovel to Carl Johnson to dispose of Jimmy Hernandez's body in an unnamed VCRASH2 mission, an early version of High Noon with a completely different story. There are no recorded voice lines or lines of code to identify his (likely generic) character model left in the files.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: An Indian pedetrian model - "Indian Male Young Street" ( IMYST ) - was removed during the game's development. Half of the recorded voice lines were recycled for "Oriental Male Old Street" ( OMOST ) (mostly known for his random farts), explaining his contradictory stereotypical Indian accent. His unused voice lines can still be found in the audio bank files.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: A skater pedestrian - "White Male Young Skater" WMYSKAT - was removed during the game's development. His recorded voice lines can still be found in the audio bank files.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Two Iranian pedetrian models - "Iranian Female Young Street" IRFYST and "Iranian Male Young Street" IRMYST - were removed during the game's development. Their recorded voice lines can still be found in the audio bank files.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
A female pedestrian labelled as "White Female Old Pajamas" ( WFOPJ ) was removed during the game's development. Her cut character model's name indicates she is a female variant of Colonel Fuhrberger's unique character model ( WMOPJ ). She only has 5 voice lines (Furhberger has 7 voice lines), suggesting a minor mission-only role.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
Unused voice lines for the Boat School introduction reveal a removed tutor character for the Boat School. His role is basically the same as the Driving School Tutor. As evidenced by the character's voice, the instructor is intended to be the "Oriental Male Old Boat" omoboat pedestrian model, who is also used to depict a refugee in The Da Nang Thang.

Dialogue lines from american.gxt\BOAT . Audio files from \sfx\SCRIPT\Bank_022 .

~z~To view a demonstration of each test, please use the TV over there.
~z~Passing a test will unlock the next test.
~z~You can come back and check your scores or take new tests at any time.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: An unused fat version of Big Bear, possibly intended for his post-rehab arc after Beat Down on B Dup. Includes a cutscene model ( csbigbear ) and an in-game pedestrian model ( bb ). The cutscene.img file also has a second model of Big Bear ( csbigbear2 ), which is a duplicate of the early version of the generic fat Grove Street Families member wearing a dark blue hoodie.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Early version of the existing pool players, reusing Dope's head model. In the final version, all pool players use the generic private security/bodyguard pedestrian model seen in Madd Dogg's Rhymes, Management Issues and Customs Fast Track.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Early version of the aforementioned bodyguards, internally named "helpers" in the texture files.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
Psycho 
Unused character model reusing some of the textures from the cut 1992 LA Riots' Special Operations Group-inspired SWAT models seen in early screenshots.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
The character model internally named cspunter has a duplicate called cspunter2 . The model is similar to the in-game Italian Mafia pedestrian VMAFF4 . The texture image MAF_B suggests the final version's Italian Mafia pedestrian was originally an early model of the Russian Mafia goon B ( maffb ).

"Punter" is British slang for gambler (Rockstar North is a Scottish game developer) and during his only appearance, he is seen betting inside Wu Zi Mu's betting shop during Mountain Cloud Boys.

"Punter 2" was originally intended to appear at The Welcome Pump during First Date (official strategy guide, page 66) alongside the original "Punter" model. They are both replaced by countryside pedestrians in the final version. This explains why Catalina oddly calls the redneck "fatso", referring to the original fat "punters".

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: A pilot pedestrian internally named bones in the files, unused in-game. Possibly a leftover of an early version of the wmyplt pedestrian.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Unused cab driver pedestrian internally named "White Male Young Cab Driver 2" WMYCD2 . It is likely that Rockstar North left this pedestrian unused by accident, as he has unique lines of dialogue.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Unused Texan pedestrians, left unused in the cutscene.img file as cstexan and cstexan2 . As there are two unused sound banks for male Texan pedestrians (VOICE_GEN_WMYTX1 and VOICE_GEN_WMYTX2), it can be assumed that they were intended to be found in normal gameplay and not simply tied to cutscenes.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
Another security guard pedestrian internally named "Black Male Old Security" ( bmosec ). Also contains unused voice lines and an entry in the peds.ide file. This pedestrian cannot be seen in the streets due to a possibly developer oversight - he is not listed in the pedgrp.dat file.

There is a rare chance of the pedestrian to spawn as a target during Vigilante, as the side mission is scripted to pick any pedestrian listed in the peds.ide file.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Unused Airport Workers pedestrians somyap and vwmyap (both being variants of the existing bmyap for San Fierro and Las Venturas, respectively).

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
section: Su Xi Mu and Claude in-game models
text:
In-game models (not cutscene) of Claude and Su Xi Mu (Ran Fa Li's grunt translator), left unused in the final game.

Unused dialogue suggests Su Xi Mu was intended to appear outside cutscenes during Fish in a Barrel, a casino-related escorting mission turned into a cutscene in the final version. Claude appears as Wu Zi Mu in Farewell, My Love... due to a possible oversight.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Variants of the girlfriend models intended to be used for the cut Hot Coffee minigame, left unused in the files.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
Two unused cutscene models for prostitutes.

The first one is possibly an early version of the existing "San Fierro White Female Old Prostitute" ( swfopro ). The unused model cspro1 is later used for strip club audition posters in both GTA Liberty City Stories and , and served as the base model for the Heidi Hole sex doll used to tie-in both games on the promotional website for Paulie's Revue Bar.

A variant of the pole dancer seen in the mission Jizzy is left unused in the files.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Unused desert sheriff intended to appear in Tierra Robada and Bone County areas. In the final game, the Countryside Sheriff ( csher ) is used instead.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Unused countryside deputy intended to appear in Red County, Flint County and Whetstone areas. Left unused in the files. Reused face textures from Lionel Starkweather from Manhunt.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
Police bikers for the SFPD and LVPD, left unused. In the final game, one single motor officer model is used across the state.

The texture image of an unused second LSPD motor officer LAPDM2 is used for the chopped body parts (texture container: chopcopx.txd ) seen in the end of the mission Reuniting the Families. The number "2" on the texture image suggest there was more than a single motor officer for the LSPD.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Placeholder girlfriend models gfriend and csgfprox used for testing the dating minigame cutscenes, one of which is posed sitting as her default idle animation as a static object. They are both replicas of the existing generic White Female Young Street ( wfyst ) with minor texture oversights.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: A cartoonish version of the Black Female Young Street pedestrian ( bfystr ) from Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, labelled as a cutscene model. A female steward using the same cartoonish art style is seen during the introduction cutscene.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: A recolored version of the existing Hispanic Female Young Street pedestrian ( HFYST ) intended for Las Venturas.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: An unused Las Venturas White Female Young Prostitute pedestrian ( VWFYPR1 ). This is a nearly identical version of the existing " VWFYPRO " with a different face and no high heel stockings.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Various copies of the csblue2 cutscene model ( csblue2_2 , csblue2_3 , csblue2_4 , csblue2_5 and csblue4 ), an old Grove Street Families model with low quality textures appearing as Cesar's Informant in the final game during Customs Fast Track. Official strategy guide screenshots of the Badlands and Return to Los Santos chapters suggest these models were used as placeholders.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: An unused 2D version of Tony the Parrot can be found in the cutscene.img file. This model is simply a flat model using a parrot image, and is never used in any cutscene taking place at the Caligula's Palace office.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Various unused "tramp" pedestrians, the majority being duplicates of existing ones.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Character Customization 
Carl's early face and torso texture is found in the unused player.txd file. The .dff model is corrupted.

In early promotional screenshots, Carl's appearance resembles his final model with minor differences (head, default facial expression, animations).

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Ryder looked vastly different, having no hat and glasses, cornrows and a lot of stubble. He also wore a black hoodie/sweatshirt.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Sweet was originally dressed in black with a grey short-sleeved shirt over a white long-sleeved shirt, and a black skully. This early model is still seen in portraits.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Kendl's facial model and clothing were given to the Black Female Young Street ( bfyst ) pedestrian. She appears once in the game using her beta character due to an oversight in the mission High Stakes, Low-Rider – her only appearance outside of a cutscene. The model and texture can be found in the game files as kendl.txd and kendl.dff . The model can also be seen in the Johnson House in a picture with Sweet's old design, but with her new face.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Big Smoke wore a white Saints jersey and didn't wear a hat, exposing his bald head. Smoke's old cutscene model is reused as an static object in the final version, appearing as a statue of himself found in his crack palace. His cutscene model's eyeballs and mouth interior is still present inside the statue model.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: An old version of Eddie Pulaski's character model ( csplas1 ) is left unused in the cutscene.img file. This model was used as a reference for an unreleased artwork of Eddie Pulaski.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: OG Loc's beanie had a pattern texture. Leftovers of this texture are hidden under his second cutscene model under his Burger Shot hat. An early render of OG Loc appears in the Base 5 poster in-game, with a bandana, different chains and a mustache. The beanie texture and mustache are later used in the Mobile version (cutscenes only) and AI-upscaled in The Definitive Edition by Grove Street Games.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: The appearance of the generic Black Male Young Street pedestrian " BMYST " (also known as the "Orange 12" pedestrian) has been completely changed.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: The appearance of the generic Black Male Young Street Crack Dealer " BMYCR " has been completely changed.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: The generic White Female Young Rich pedestrian " WFYRI " (-inspired pedestrian) originally had a ponytail.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
In pre-release material, the Ballas are commonly listed along with a second gang named "Flats". Developer notes found in the mission script file for Sweet & Kendl and Drive-Thru clarify that "The Flats" was the original name of the Kilo Tray Ballas set.

Line 69 of the pedgrp.dat data file defining the three Ballas ped models as part of the gang contains a commented out note describing the Ballas as "also known as Flats".
 BALLAS1, BALLAS2, BALLAS3 # Gang 1 (BALLAS - Rival Black Gang - AKA FLATS)

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
Two Triad cutscene models are left unused in the files, cstriada3 and cstriboss . The former is a retextured version of the cstriadb with facial hair. The "boss" character is an unused old oriental male character, and an early version of the existing " triboss " pedestrian model featured in Pier 69.

In the BradyGames Strategy Guide, the Triads appear with completely different character models. This model was later rebranded as a generic pedestrian "San Fierro Oriental Male Young Rich" ( SOMYRI ) using a different hair model.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: The " dnb2 " gang member's outfit did not have the ProLaps logo on his outfit, while " dnb3 " used a different character model. Both early models are seen in promotional screenshots of the mission Lure.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: SWAT members originally resembled the real-life U.S. Marshals' "Special Operations Group" tactical unit deployed to combat the 1992 Los Angeles Riots.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: In addition to the aforementioned removed second LSPD motor officer, the first model used different textures, as seen in a promotional screenshot. In the final version, the texture is changed and the LSPD motor officer is used statewide.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: The early version of the generic LSPD officer lapd1 appears to have used a recycled Pulaski model with minor changes at some point. This character model is also seen alongside the aforementioned lapdm2 motor officer in the Feature Clip "Police Bike" on the promotional website.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
An early version of the "Hispanic Female Young Rich" ( hfyri ) pedestrian is featured in one of the early promotional screenshots in Rodeo. The female pedestrian is also featured on the Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories promotional website for Paulie's Revue Bar.

She is identified as hfyri in the Management Issues mission section of official strategy guide, page 48, where the early model is seen depicting Scipio's female associate.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: Related to the aforementioned female pedestrian, an early version of "Black Male Young Rich" ( bmyri ) used by Madd Dogg's manager Scipio, the main target in Management Issues, is seen with a different design in the official strategy guide, page 48.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: An early version of the "Hispanic Male Young Rich" pedestrian appears in the background of the aforementioned promotional screenshot of hfyri in Rodeo, and in the official strategy guide section for the mission Snail Trail, in which he is featured as a target.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: The official strategy guide section for the Tanker Commander mission (page 67) shows a screenshot featuring an early version of the pool player bmypol2 , used as the Gasso Employee in the mission. The generic pedestrian model "White Male Old Street" ( wmost ) used by Derek is also different in the same official guide screenshot.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: An early version of the generic White Male Young Backpack ( wmybp ), left unused in the cutscene.img file with inverted texture image. The pedestrian can be spotted in early promotional screenshots.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: The "Black Male Young Disc Jockey" ( bmydj ) pedestrian was remodeled. The old version of this pedestrian is used as a cutscene model ( csbmydj ) in House Party.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: As its name implies, this model is an early version of the in-game "Oriental Male Old Street" omost pedestrian. A second version of this pedestrian can be spotted in a pre-release screenshot of Market Station, with minor design changes.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text: The "White Male Old Rich" pedestrian was remodeled. The old version of this pedestrian is used as a cutscene model in Mountain Cloud Boys.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
Early versions of the street criminals HMYCR and WMYCR appear in promotional screenshots and in the official strategy guide section for the mission T-Bone Mendez, in which both character models are featured as targets.

 HMYCR can be spotted in a early promotional screenshot purchasing tickets from a machine at Cranberry Station.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
Jeffrey "OG Loc" Cross was originally named Jeff e rey "MC Strap" Martin according to promotional material, unused mission blip and .gxt file entries related to the character. 
Denise Robinson was originally named (or at least nicknamed) Coochie Robinson, according to internal script files.
Katie Zhan was originally named Suzie Nookie.
Helena Wankstein was originally named Kylie Goodpoke. This name is still used the internal file name of her unused barn interior for the Hot Coffee minigame.
The notusedtext.txt file suggests she was originally the mechanic girlfriend instead of Michelle Cannes.
Madd Dogg was originally named Doc G according to the official strategy guide. His stage name was also spelt Dr. G at some point in development.
Kendl Johnson's first name was originally spelt Kendal.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Characters
text:
Certain in-game characters have their names revealed through unused mission dialogue:
Larry and Jordan – LVPD officers in Cop Wheels (LVPD HQ and Hospital, respectively).
Marco Forelli – The Forelli brother in Saint Mark's Bistro.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Items and Weapons
text: This subpage documents removed, unused and changed items and weapons during the development of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Items and Weapons
text:
Adrenaline Pills were intended to make a return from GTA III and GTA Vice City. The pickup model adrenaline.dff can still be found in the game files. It has been "redesigned" (removed circular model from the pills) to match the look of the GTA San Andreas pickup items.

While the item has been removed, the code for the Adrenaline Pills effect is still kept in-game, although only enabled through cheat codes.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Items and Weapons
text:

Adrenaline Pills formerly had spawn points in all three cities, except countryside areas according to the official strategy guide:
2 locations in Los Santos.
At the rooftop of Carson General Hospital in Jefferson.
At the Yacht Harbor's ferris wheel in Santa Maria Beach.
2 locations in San Fierro.
In the doorway of the San Fierro City Hall.
Outside the arena in Foster Valley.

In the corner of Last Dime Motel, slightly hidden in flowers.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Items and Weapons
text:
Similarly to previous titles, Health pickups were meant to be found in normal gameplay. It is highly suggested that Health pickups were scrapped in favor of the various ways to replenish health (restaurants, vending machines and street vendors). In the final version, the Health pickups are only spawned during missions and gang warfares.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Items and Weapons
text:
The Micro SMG model from Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, also known as the /, was intended to make a return in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

The only leftover of this weapon model in the final game lies in the Big Smoke's Crack Palace interior, where it is attached to the hands of Big Smoke's statue as part of a single model.

A second returning SMG class weapon from Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, the Mac 10, was renamed during development as the new "Micro SMG". Developer notes for the weapon pickup locations (on the uncompiled initial.sc file) refer to the existing "Micro SMG" in the final version as the Mac 10, as well as in-game dialogue for Nines and AK's and an unused dialogue for Photo Opportunity, confirming the replacement of the weapon. The HUD icon for the existing "Micro SMG" resembles the Mac 10 rather than its Uzi Pistol-inspired design.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Items and Weapons
text:
Spade 
The Spade was a melee weapon similar to the Shovel, which had a single defined spawn point in the San Andreas map at some point in development. In the final version, the Spade is still present as a cutscene prop used in High Noon. Developer notes indicates that both the Shovel and Spade were separate weapons.

The original spawn point of the Spade is mentioned in the developer notes in the uncompiled initial.sc script file accidentally left in The Definitive Edition:

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Items and Weapons
text:
Aside from the Explosive Barrels, a second "enviromental weapon" consisting of flammable oil puddles (ignited through gunshots) was removed. This feature was later introduced in Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars (during Trail Blazer only) and fully implemented in Grand Theft Auto V.

Hidden in the game's executable, there is a unused " CShadow::GunShotSetsOilOnFire " function. The oil puddle effect itself does not exist in the final version. The following video shows this functionality added to blood puddles through modifications as a test:

In addition, there are two opcodes CREATE_OIL_PUDDLE (no effect) and REMOVE_OIL_PUDDLES_IN_AREA (triggered upon loading the RC Battle Ground interior at the start of New Model Army for unknown reasons).

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Items and Weapons
text:
DDLES_IN_AREA (triggered upon loading the RC Battle Ground interior at the start of New Model Army for unknown reasons).

Three unused dialogue text and audio for the final part of the mission End of the Line suggests the oil puddles were also originally intended to appear during the Fire Truck chase.

According to former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij, the reason for the Oil Puddle's removal was that when trails of oil were rendered, they would spawn in singular splotches (similarly to how blood comes out from NPCs when hit with weapons) opposed to an entire trail.

text:
Flowers 
The Flowers are an example of a gift-type item which can also be selected and used as a weapon in the final release.

The model used for the Flowers is internally named "Flower A" (" flowera "), suggesting that there may have been an alternative flower model. In fact, the HUD icon shows a flower bouquet rather than simply a bunch of flowers.

There are two unused models for Flowers in the game files, listed along the weapon models.
A duplicate of the existing model internally named " stalks " which features no HUD icon.
A duplicate of the existing model without the flower details, internally named "Flower B" (" flowerb ") and reusing the existing HUD icon. This supports the hypothesis that different Flower items were intended for the game.

text:
Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Props 
Six items from Rockstar North's Manhunt were ported by prop artist Campbell-John Dick to be used as props (all using his cj_ prefix in the file names).

The default position of these props, alongside the fact that they are stored in the interior props directory ( gta_int.img ) suggests these are unused display-only weapon models for Ammu-Nation, meant to be placed near the other existing Manhunt ammo boxes found normally inside the store (Morrice Ammunition and Brian's Nails). A painkiller model from Manhunt was originally intended to be held by pedestrians inside interiors (evidenced by the shared pick_up.txd used by fast food interior items).

All of these props are left unused in-game and none of these items uses their original Manhunt textures.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Textures
text: This subpage documents removed, unused and changed textures for objects and UI during the development of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Textures
text:
A real-life license plate was used as a placeholder during the early development, before being replaced by the three in-universe San Andreas plates. Leftovers of this texture can be found in the unused Dashound company's Bus dach.txd texture container and the texture container for the vehicle's generic features vehicle.txd .

California license plates were also used as placeholders during the development of Grand Theft Auto V, some of which have been accidentally left on vehicle wreckages and on one license plate decoration texture.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Textures
text: The same "change me" placeholder texture used for billboard ads in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City can be found in the LODlBd2 LOD model textures in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. It can still be seen, hidden under the second LOD billboard model.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Textures
text: The LOD model for the Xoomer billboard in San Fierro still uses its former name "Xenon". The original billboard texture is no longer found in the game files.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Textures
text:
Various textures for murals found across Los Santos and San Fierro were removed for unknown reasons. They are still left in the LOD models of the buildings in which they were originally placed. The original texture for the mural is no longer found in the game files.

One of the murals, "Save the Whaleland", was one of the original locations for the Snapshots, before being moved to a nearby street banner.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Textures
text: The unused bustopm model intended for bus stops in GTA Vice City has been reworked over to Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas to be used as a dynamic street prop. The advertisement texture for Rubik's Cube found on the GTA Vice City original model can still be found in the texture container file, albeit unused, possibly used as a placeholder for the final version's Burger Shot advertisement.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Textures
text:
Two unused trash can textures, one of them returning from Rockstar North's Manhunt.

The cj_bin2 texture is used for Ryder's "water" bottle cap (cutscene prop: " csbottle ") during Catalyst.

text: Unused " dach.txd " texture container for an unused bus owned by the cut Dashound company. The company would later make its debut in the HD Universe.

text: Unused destination placards found in the texture file for the Tram. In the PlayStation 2 version of the game, all Trams have "Downtown" as their destination, displayed on the sides of the cars, while the trams in the PC version have "Garcia" as their destination.

title: Brothel (Whorehouse)
text: The Brothel is an unused and partially finished brothel interior in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Brothel (Whorehouse)
text:
The brothel is unnamed and is simply referred to using the generic interior transition name "Brothel" on the HUD, shared with another unused brothel.

The interior itself (internally named Whhouse_main ) is partially finished with a hole in the wall intended for the entrance/exit doors. The interior has several unique props.

As its model name suggests, it is located in Interior World 3 at X = 967.5, Y = -53.0, Z = 1001.1, shared with the generic Inside Track and Strip Club interiors, a second unused (and unfinished) Brothel, and the cutscene-only interior for Blastin' Fools Records.

The CSR 103.9 radio station is played inside the interior.

title: Brothel (Unfinished)
text: The Brothel is an unused and unfinished brothel interior in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Brothel (Unfinished)
text:
The brothel is unnamed and is simply referred to using the generic interior transition name "Brothel" on the HUD, shared with another unused brothel.

The interior itself (internally named int3int_brothel ) is unfinished with no entrance/exit doors, with some textures not properly mapped to the model. Some of the bar assets found inside the brothel are shared with other brothels and strip clubs.

It is located in Interior World 3 at X = 940.6, Y = -18.4, Z = 1000.9, shared with the generic Inside Track and Strip Club interiors, the second unused Brothel, and the cutscene-only interior for Blastin' Fools Records.

The CSR 103.9 radio station is played inside the interior.

title: Hidden Packages in GTA San Andreas
text: Hidden Packages are an unused collectible tied to a removed vehicle side-mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Hidden Packages in GTA San Andreas
text:
At some point in early development, a side-mission involving a Newsvan existed in Los Santos, in which the player would have used the vehicle to locate ten hidden packages around the city using a signal sound emitted by the van. The vehicle's antenna appears to have originally meant to point to the nearby package's location, a returning feature from 's save system.

This activity appears to have been more of a concept or a test than a fully developed feature by the time it was scrapped, as some of the hidden packages are placed in plain view rather than hidden.

The original uncompiled script for the mission " collect.sc " has been accidentally left in the files of Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition, containing the exact coordinates of the ten packages and the Newsvan's original location at the car wash in East Los Santos:

title: Doberman (C.R.A.S.H.)
text:
The mission is labelled as CRASH2 in the GXT entries, meaning the mission took place between Burning Desire ( CRASH1 ) and Gray Imports ( CRASH3 ). The mission script file " crash2.sc " no longer exists.

In the final version, the mission is replaced with a mission of the same name – Doberman – given by Sweet Johnson. Despite that, the final mission script is labelled as crash4.sc , although the header in the script file still refers to it as "Crash 2 - Doberman".

The mission starts with a cutscene showing officer Frank Tenpenny having a phone call with Officer Carver, who is threatening to send the DEA after one of Tenpenny's informants, a drug dealer named Poncho.

title: Doberman (C.R.A.S.H.)
text:
with Officer Carver, who is threatening to send the DEA after one of Tenpenny's informants, a drug dealer named Poncho.

Officer Eddie Pulaski suspects Poncho might squeal in prison about his business deals with the C.R.A.S.H., thus Frank Tenpenny sends Carl Johnson to East Los Santos to kill Poncho before he is taken into custody. Pulaski also tells Carl that two bales of weed are being bagged as evidence during the raid and must be collected before they are delivered to the police station.

If the drugs are lost in a vehicle explosion or sunken in the ocean, or if Carver's police unit arrives at the police station with Poncho alive, the mission fails.

Through the cutscene audio, it is assumed the mission cutscene took place outside Jim's Sticky Ring (the starting point for the Los Santos mission strand for C.R.A.S.H.), as the sounds for the trio's Police vehicle's doors are clearly heard.

The mission is labelled as DESERT11 , listed after Green Goo ( DESERT10 ). It was designed by Imran Sarwar at Rockstar North. The mission involved using a Rustler to escort a plane to Easter Bay Airport in San Fierro and using its weapons to protect the plane against enemy vehicles.

Leftovers of this mission can be found in the notusedtext.txt file, a text file containing early american.gxt entries scrapped by the original Rockstar North developers, and accidentally left in the files of the original release of Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition by Grove Street Games.

The mission still used provisional real-life names ("" and "") for in-game text at the time it was scrapped.

title: Fish in a Barrel (cut mission)
text:
The mission was designed by Imran Sarwar at Rockstar North. It was codenamed "Clear & Present Danger" in the leftover debug script and was started at The Four Dragons Casino. The mission was labelled as CASINO7 and consisted of an introduction cutscene, a gameplay segment and a second cutscene at the end.

In the final release, the mission is labelled as CASINO7_CUT with only the second cutscene partially surviving in the final game. All mentions of the Mafia ambush from the early version of the mission have been removed from said cutscene. Leftover text strings for this mission's cutscenes and objectives can be found in the american.gxt file. Only five lines are used in the final release version of the mission.

Moreover, additional lines related to the mission objectives can be found in the notusedtext.txt file, a text file containing early american.gxt entries scrapped by the original Rockstar North developers, and accidentally left in the files of the original release of Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition by Grove Street Games.

These older scrapped text strings reveal that the mission introduced the Float, a carnival float whose only leftover found in the final game is its in-game name and handling data.

title: Fish in a Barrel (cut mission)
text:
The intro cutscenes shows Carl explaining the whole situation regarding Ken Rosenberg, Kent Paul and Maccer at the Mafia-owned Caligula's Palace, saying he feels responsible for them and that they can't begin the heist until they're safe elsewhere.

At the same time, Woozie informs Carl about Ran Fa Li's arrival in Las Venturas. They both suspect the Mafia will try something against him, so Woozie tells Carl to escort the convoy back to the casino. He provides a Golf Club for the job, despite Carl telling him that he should use a weapon of his choice for this job.

title: Fish in a Barrel (cut mission)
text:
The leftover text for the gameplay section shows that, after picking up Ran Fa Li (referred to as the "VIP") in a limousine, Carl was intended to deliver him to the casino in a convoy with his men.

Based on the leftover text, while following the convoy lead, the Mafia soon locates Ran Fa Li and a car chase begins. After following the lead car through an alleyway, they end up in a Mafia ambush with Linerunners blocking the road.

title: Carnival Float
text:
The mission is labelled as CASINO8 , taking place after the cut mission Fish in a Barrel ( CASINO7 )

While there are no leftovers of the mission in the final version, a notusedtext.txt text file was unintentionally left in the files for the original releases of Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition by Grove Street Games, listing old unused text scrapped from the GXT file by Rockstar North during the game's early development.

The cut CASINO8 mission is identified as being "Carnival Float", although there are no leftovers of the mission objectives and dialogue.

As its name suggests, it involved the removed Float vehicle, a carnival float whose only leftover found in the final game is its in-game name and handling data. The Las Venturas carnival is foreshadowed during the mission Snail Trail via the San Andreas Post newspaper.

title: Beta Content in GTA San Andreas/Vehicles
text:
This subpage documents removed, unused and changed vehicles during the development of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

Many vehicles underwent changes through their development, including name and design adjustment or mission appearances, revealed by internal file data, pre-release screenshots or early pre-release builds.

title: Cargobob (3D Universe)
text:
The Cargobob is a transport helicopter appearing in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

The helicopter later returns in the HD Universe where it assumes the design of a tandem-rotor helicopter.

title: Cargobob (3D Universe)
text: The Cargobob's fuselage is mostly reminiscent of a for the bulging fuel tanks, engine, cockpit/nose design and rear loading ramp. However, it has been given a different configuration resembling the smaller , with some design influences from the .

title: Cargobob (3D Universe)
text:
The Cargobob is among the largest and heaviest helicopters in the game (on par with the Leviathan), having a large fuselage with a rounded nose and large cockpit windows on the front, as well as a nose undercarriage with dual wheels. The main section is very large and features a tall compartment where the dual engines and the four-bladed rotor are seen, as well as black frames on the upper area, the main undercarriage on the rear corners of the underside and the cargo hold with a rear ramp door (albeit the ramp door is much shorter than the actual hold entrance). The tail boom has two horizontal stabilizers and a -style tail rotor.

The vehicle will always spawn with a desert camouflaged livery (though files indicate it spawns in a white color); coincidentally, it spawns only in the Bone County area.

title: Cargobob (3D Universe)
text: Although the Cargobob features an open rear loading compartment, it cannot carry other vehicles due to the ramp from the back being inoperable. Its huge weight causes the Cargobob to be incredibly slow, as well as making it very difficult to adjust altitude, turn, or conduct other evasive maneuvers. Although a military helicopter, it does not come equipped with flares. The Cargobob does, however, have very strong armor — it can take over 12 missiles before catching on fire and eventually exploding. This makes the Cargobob almost as resistant as the AT-400. However, on the iOS port, its health has been reduced to Raindance-level.

title: Cargobob (3D Universe)
text:
On the helipad of the K.A.C.C. Military Aviation Fuel Depot, in northeast Las Venturas. The depot can be entered by driving a military vehicle (Patriot, Rhino or Barracks) or flying above the fence.
Inside the Area 69 airfield, on the small airstrip near the Hydras. Area 69 triggers a 5-star wanted level, becomes swarmed by military, police, and FBI agents, and the airspace above it is guarded by S.A.M. sites and enemy Hydras, making acquisition of this Cargobob very dangerous.

The Varrios Los Aztecas (a.k.a. "Aztecas", "Southerners", "Southside Aztecas", or "VLA") are a gang featured in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, as the secondary protagonistic gang.

title: Varrios Los Aztecas (3D Universe)
text: The Varrios Los Aztecas have been around since the early 1980s and are one of the more recently formed gangs in Los Santos. Much of their origins and past history is unknown. Likewise, the origins and past of their rivalry with the other Los Santos gangs - particularly the Los Santos Vagos is also unknown, though it obviously began sometime between 1980 and 1992. It is highly likely that they evolved from the El Corona neighborhood, and their presence grew with the increase of Mexican and other Hispanic/Latino immigration to the area, correlating with the relative deprivation of the area compared to the rest of the city.

title: Varrios Los Aztecas (3D Universe)
section: Events of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text:
The Varrios Los Aztecas are not a major part of the story, but are first mentioned during Sweet & Kendl in which Sweet refers to Kendl's relationship with a high-ranking Azteca member - Cesar Vialpando, stating "you know we beefing". Because of this, the gang acts as a fulcrum point between the relationship of Sweet and his sister due to Cesar being Kendl's boyfriend - much to the dismay of Sweet because to Cesar's involvement with the VLA.

The radio in the early game mentions that the Aztecas were in a war with the Vagos in East Los Santos, despite the area actually being controlled by the Ballas.

title: Varrios Los Aztecas (3D Universe)
section: Events of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text: They are first seen during the mission Cesar Vialpando. Sweet orders CJ to follow his sister to a lowriding club at Unity Station, where a lowriding competition with a high concentration of Azteca gang members is taking place - including Cesar Vialpando himself. Fortunately, the Aztecas do not harass or fight CJ and let him take part in the bouncing competition against an Azteca member. CJ wins the competition without any violence taking place and is then introduced to Cesar Vialpando - Kendl's boyfriend. CJ makes his objection to the relationship clear, and an influential (possibly an OG) Azteca member called Jose approaches CJ and confronts/insults him for his rudeness. Fortunately, Cesar is able to influence Jose to "cool down", thus causing him to leave and possibly saving CJ's life.

This is because the Aztecas never show-up to rob the weapons train during the mission Catalyst, where as the other three gangs were tipped off by CRASH about the train. This is odd since the Aztecas are heavily involved in arms dealing/gun running. Either CRASH are scared of the Aztecas due to them being possibly the most heavily armed gang in Los Santos, or they avoid them because they mistakenly think they are weak due to their small size. Another possibility for this is because CRASH does not want to make the VLA too powerful over the other gangs by equipping them with even more weapons (due to them already being heavily armed).

title: Varrios Los Aztecas (3D Universe)
text: The Varrios Los Aztecas are an extremely proud Mexican/Latino street gang, and they control El Corona, Little Mexico and Unity Station. They are the smallest gang in the city but are likely to be one of the most heavily armed, giving them power over the other gangs. They are a traditionally anti-narcotic gang like the Grove Street families, with heavy involvement in gun running/arms trafficking, gang-banging, gang warfare, street violence, gang-related homicide, murder, vandalism, and illegal street racing. They are easily identifiable by their turquoise colored bandanas and 90's "cholo" style clothing.

The Aztecas have a fierce rivalry with the Los Santos Vagos, and strongly dislike the San Fierro Rifa. They also have many conflicts with the nearby Ballas (especially the Front Yard set) since their territories border near Idlewood. The Aztecas are also enemies with the Grove Street Families and will attack Grove members on sight though the rivalry is not as intense as it is with the Ballas and especially the Vagos since the families are well away from their territory, and since they both share similar views on drug trafficking.

If he drives a car through their turf, they will just stand on the street and won't even chase him or shoot at his car. This indicates that the Aztecas and GSF have a lighter rivalry, as opposed to the Ballas and Vagos, whom the GSF are arch-enemies with.

The San Fierro Triads (Traditional Chinese: 聖費耶洛三合會, Cantonese Yale: Sing Fai Yèh Lok Sāam Hahp Wúi) are a collective of Hong Kong crime syndicates operating in San Fierro, San Andreas, appearing in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: San Fierro Triads
text:
There are two Triad factions in San Fierro; the Blood Feather Triad, which would later be slaughtered by their rivals, the Vietnamese Da Nang Boys; and the Mountain Cloud Boys. The most prominent gang in the group, the Mountain Cloud Boys, is operated by the blind Wu Zi Mu.

All Triad gangs within the San Fierro Triads answer directly to the Red Gecko Tong, led by Ran Fa Li, which acts as a council representing the Triads on the of the United States of America.

The Mountain Cloud Boys are the only Triad gang that can be encountered outside missions, found in Chinatown, the most northern tip of King's and Calton Heights. Triad members don all-black suits or all-grey suits, usually wielding AK47s and pistols. The San Fierro Triads gang members are seen driving Elegys, Stratums and Sultans. They listen to the radio station SF-UR.

In addition to their bases of operations in San Fierro, the Triads also own and operate a casino hotel venture called The Four Dragons Casino on the southern tip of The Strip in Las Venturas; ownership is shared between Wu Zi Mu, Ran Fa Li and Carl Johnson. Because of intense Mafia pressure in the city, the Triads attempted to flex their muscles to show the Mafia that they can hold their own casino on The Strip. While the Triad's primary business is gambling, Wu Zi Mu has shown motivations towards robbery and street racing.

Unlike the Varrios Los Aztecas, the Triads will react with friendliness towards Carl Johnson, unless they are provoked.

title: San Andreas Police Department (3D Universe)
text: The San Andreas Police Department (SAPD), also known as the San Andreas State Patrol (SASP), is the state police and main law enforcement agency servicing the state of San Andreas in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: San Andreas Police Department (3D Universe)
text: The SAPD covers a wide range of law enforcement arms in San Andreas and presides over various jurisdictions in the state. The SAPD is broken up into seven sub-division each with different areas to patrol:

title: San Andreas Police Department (3D Universe)
text:
r various jurisdictions in the state. The SAPD is broken up into seven sub-division each with different areas to patrol:

Los Santos Police Department serving the city of Los Santos.
Community Resources Against Street Hoodlums an LSPD division related to gang crime.
San Fierro Police Department serving the city of San Fierro.
Las Venturas Police Department serving the city of Las Venturas.
San Andreas Sheriff an unnamed sheriff's department serving rural areas of San Andreas, including Red County, Flint County, Whetstone, Bone County and Tierra Robada.
Motorcycle Division a division of the SAPD that patrols the main three cities.
Special Weapons and Tactics a tactical division of the SAPD that respond to serious crimes in the state. The division is apparently based in Los Santos as indicated by the "LSPD" markings on their armored trucks.
San Andreas Coast Guard a water division that patrols the waters of the state. The coast guard officers are regular police officers, depending on the area they spawn.

title: San Andreas Police Department (3D Universe)
text:
The officers can be seen either walking on the street or driving a Police car with one or two occupants. Officers may occasionally chase a street criminal on foot, although harming the criminal will give the player one-star wanted level. They may be also seen in a hot pursuit with a group of criminals in a vehicle.

At a three-star wanted level, police officers will appear on foot in secluded locations. They will continuously appear at higher wanted levels, with the SWAT members, FBI agents, and army soldiers being dispatched to apprehend the player.

title: San Andreas Police Department (3D Universe)
text:
There are three main police stations one in each city. Each of these has an alarmed garage containing police vehicles from that city. The police stations in Las Venturas, Los Santos and Dillimore can be entered, and contain officers, police lockers, cells and some weapons and armor; although be aware that carrying any firearms and explosives inside police stations will trigger a two-star wanted level.

There is also a number of small police stations in rural villages.

title: San Andreas Police Department (3D Universe)
text:
Each of the subdivisions has a dedicated uniform.
LSPD officers wear a black shirt, black pants, black shoes and a golden shield badge.
SFPD officers wear a black shirt, black pants, black shoes and a grey five-star badge.
LVPD officers wear a light khaki shirt, light khaki pants with a black stripe, black shoes and a silver shield badge.
Sheriff's deputies wear a brown shirt, light khaki pants with a black stripe, black shoes, a cowboy hat and a golden five-star badge.
Motorcycle division officers wear a black leather jacket, black leather pants with a yellow stripe, a white helmet, black gloves, black biker boots, a pair of sunglasses, and a golden five-star badge.
SWAT officers wear a dark blue long-sleeved shirt with a dark blue body armor, dark blue pants with a holster, black boots, dark blue gloves, black balaclava and a dark blue combat helmet with combat googles.

title: San Andreas Police Department (3D Universe)
text: Each city has a separate version of the Police car, marked with the individual city's abbreviation (e.g. LSPD, SFPD and LVPD). The LSPD and SFPD use the Premier as their main police vehicle, while the LVPD use a unique vehicle that is not based on any cars. The sheriff's deputies use a Rancher-based police car in rural areas. The motor officers use the HPV1000 to patrol the main three cities in San Andreas. The SWAT officers use the Enforcer, Police Maverick and S.W.A.T. The coast guard officers use the Predator boat to patrol and chase criminals on the waters of the state.

title: San Andreas Police Department (3D Universe)
text: Every patrol officer carries a pistol and a nightstick as their main weapons, although they will also use shotguns when the player has a wanted level of at least three stars. Additionally, officers are seen using SMGs in Reuniting the Families and Micro SMGs in End of the Line.

title: San Fierro Police Department
text: The San Fierro Police Department (SFPD) is the law enforcement agency in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, servicing the city of San Fierro, and is a branch of the police agency servicing the entire state of San Andreas, the San Andreas Police Department.

title: San Fierro Police Department
text:
The San Fierro Police Department is modeled after the . SFPD officers mostly travel on-foot or driving in their police vehicles. Sometimes, an officer may drive a Predator in San Fierro Bay.

Some officers may shout encouraging, nurturing words like "The police are your friends!" or "I'm actually a social worker in this uniform!" to those they pursue owing to the liberal atmosphere of San Fierro, but when required, they use the same attacking and arresting force as any other law enforcement members throughout San Andreas. It is possible that they use these encouraging words to manipulate criminals into giving up. Some of them are also implied to be homosexuals, as indicated by lines such as, "Gotcha honey!" and "Wrestle me, honey!". Other officers will use the same gruff tone and demeanor as police in the rest of the state.

title: San Fierro Police Department
text: San Fierro Police Department's headquarters are located Downtown. The SFPD HQ contains four floors; however, it is not accessible during normal gameplay and can only be entered via the hidden interiors universe.

title: San Fierro Police Department
text: While similar in appearance to Los Santos Police Department officers, SFPD officers are distinguishable by their black undershirt, a seven-point star-shaped badge, a second shield shaped patch (similar to those found on sheriff's deputies), and a mustache. The patch bears a remarkable similarity to the actual San Francisco Police patch, and is most likely a low-poly version scaled down for San Fierro Police officers.

title: San Fierro Police Department
text: The major mode of transportation used by SFPD officers is the Police car, which, despite both being based on the Premier, enjoys superior handling compared to that of the cruiser used by the Los Santos Police Department. The Predator is also widely used by SFPD officers in the San Fierro Bay.

The Farm, also referred to as the Cult Location, is a Survivalist Cult farm in Flint County, San Andreas, appearing in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

text:
The farm is located to the south of Easter Bay Airport and Easter Bay Chemicals and north of the Leafy Hollow marijuana farm. It consists of many greenhouses, a few sheds, a silo, a water tower, and a farmhouse.

It is owned by the Survivalists cult, a group of hillbillies who are preparing to survive an anticipated doomsday scenario. The physical map poster labels The Farm as the "Cult Location", referring to the Survivalist Cult.

title: The Farm
section: Events of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text: The mission Body Harvest involved Carl Johnson stealing a Combine Harvester from the farm for The Truth. The only pedestrians that spawn outside of the mission are a farmer exiting a shed in a Tractor and Combine Harvesters working in the northern field. The Farm is prone to foggy weather at night.

title: The Farm
text:
The farmhouse is one of the many countryside building models in San Andreas to have overly bright textures due to an oversight on the night vertex color of the building model. Due to this bug, the generic dark blue window texture " examwind1_LAe " (reused from East Los Santos) of the farmhouse will appear in a brighter blue tone at night time. A similar night vertex brightness glitch happens with the textures for the Bayside Church.

This night vertex effect (found in several other countryside areas) is erroneously associated with the unrelated Epsilonist cult due to the brightness oversight and misinterpreted "cult location" description on the map referring to the Survivalist Cult, a non-religious cult.

title: Mission Pack
text:
Mission packs are experimental waste of Rockstar Games in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. They are never used in the original game, but they can be used for modding. Mission packs are used to get additional script content into the game. An example usage of this technology is Design Your Own Mission, created by PatrickW and Dutchy3010.

In Grand Theft Auto IV a similar technology is used for the downloadable content The Lost and Damned.

title: Mission Pack
text:
Mission packs must be located in the GTA San Andreas User Files directory. By default, the user files directory is as follows:
Windows Vista and later – C:\Users\Your Username\Documents\GTA San Andreas User Files\ 
Windows XP – C:\Documents and Settings\Your Username\My Documents\GTA San Andreas User Files\

title: Mission Pack
text: For adding a mission pack point to your User Files directory (as described above). Create a new folder and call it MPACK . In this folder, create another folder called MPACK# , where # is the number identifying your pack. This number begins with 1 and increments by one for every mission pack installed. Copy your script and GXT file to this folder and rename the script to scr.scm and the text archive to text.gxt .

title: Mission Pack
text: Create a new file called mpack.dat and open it using any text editor. Insert the following text: n #mission# . Replace n with the number of your mission pack (as described above), and replace mission with the name of your mission pack (e.g. My Mission Pack ). Ensure that the mission pack name is surrounded by two # characters, as shown. The name will be what the player see later on in the game when choosing a mission pack on starting a new game.

title: Mission Pack
text: By default the game skips the external script header in the script file, so it is impossible to use external scripts. However, some members of the [https://www.sannybuilder.com/ SannyBuilder community] created a patch to combat this issue (see below). Using the patch, you can move the script.img file containing your external scripts into the \data\script directory, which is located inside the game's installation directory. Rename script.img to script#.img , where # is the number of the mission pack.

title: Mission Pack
text:
As described on the top of the page mission packs are experimental waste of Rockstar Games. They are not very sophisticated and limited in their functionality. The greatest disadvantages are as follows:

External scripts cannot be used without first patching the game
Only one monolingual text can be used

Despite these caveats, mission packs are not useless. They are a good way to make major changes to the game while still maintaining compatibility and stability. Additionally, they are the only way to use two scripts side-by-side. Another advantage is that the end user of your script does not need to worry about switching save files and scripts by hand, because the game remembers the current mission pack in the save file, so all the end user has to do is load it.

title: Mission Pack
text: [http://sannybuilder.com/files/samp_fix.rar Mission Packs Fix] – Allows to use external scripts in form of a script.img file with mission packs. See [http://www.gtaforums.com/index.php?showtopic=267284 this topic] for detailed information.

title: Motor Officer
text: ', also known as police bikers or motorcycle cops, are police units designated to use police motorcycles in patrols. Motor officers are equipped with different variants of police attire, typically consisting of a helmet and boots, but otherwise behave in roughly the same manner as normal patrol car policemen. Only Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories, Grand Theft Auto V and Grand Theft Auto Online feature motor officers. A fully-functioning police motorcycle model does exist in The Ballad of Gay Tony, but is only available in multiplayer or by using a third-party vehicle spawner, and there are no corresponding motor officers.

title: Motor Officer
text: Motor officers in the game make up the San Andreas Police Department and ride HPV1000 motorcycles, which, like other motorbikes, are far more manoeuvrable, agile and compact than cars. The use of motorcycles also allows police officers to fire their weapons at criminals from any direction while in a chase. While mounted, motor officers will fire upon the player even if they have only acquired a one star wanted level.

title: Motor Officer
text:
chase. While mounted, motor officers will fire upon the player even if they have only acquired a one star wanted level.

Motor officers are equipped with uniforms consisting of a black with white turtle shell helmet, a black leather jacket, biker boots, sunglasses, fingerless gloves, and navy blue pants with a white stripe on the side of the pants legs, They are armed with nightstick and pistol, and are depicted as African American men (with African American accents). Their attire, as well as their choice of motorcycle, mirrors that of Los Angeles motor officer units employed during the early 1990s, as well as the depiction of both a assuming the guise of an LAPD motorcycle officer in the 1991 film and one of the "Death Squad" SFPD motorcycle officers from the 1973 film .

title: Motor Officer
text:
f an LAPD motorcycle officer in the 1991 film and one of the "Death Squad" SFPD motorcycle officers from the 1973 film .

Like SWAT teams, the FBI, and the military, motor officers in GTA San Andreas are one of the only law enforcement units found around the state of San Andreas that are consistent in all areas. (e.g. the character model remains the same in all areas despite the fact that San Andreas Sheriff are found in respective areas and each city has a different police force). For this reason, they sport San Andreas Police Department markings instead of a specific police department designation. Motor officers are most likely the state police, as they appear in each city.

title: Motor Officer
text: Motor officers behave like all other police officers. They will pursue fleeing criminals, make arrests, and use a nightstick and/or pistol when facing resistance. Their only extra behavioural phenomena is that they will shoot at the player from their bikes regardless of their wanted level (this happens when the player has a wanted level and then saves the game, the Motor Officer will still shoot the player). Motor officers usually give chase on wanted levels from one to two stars; however, in the countryside or desert, Rangers chase the player instead. They will often drop pursuit after the player has acquired three-star wanted level, being replaced by larger, more well-equipped units.

title: Motor Officer
text: drop pursuit after the player has acquired three-star wanted level, being replaced by larger, more well-equipped units. During the mission Reuniting the Families, motor officers used risky methods of attempting to stop the car even though there were armed passengers by jumping onto the hood and trunk of the car trying to pacify the passengers.

title: Motor Officer
text: Motor officers in GTA Vice City Stories are similar to those in GTA San Andreas in several regards. They possess similar equipment, including a beige turtle shell helmet, sunglasses, and boots (but otherwise feature the same beige-and-brown Vice City Police Department uniforms worn by other officers), as well as standard issue nightsticks and pistols. However, these officers ride VCPD WinterGreens, a police variant of the WinterGreen motorcycle.

title: Motor Officer
text: Much like the motor officers in GTA San Andreas, in GTA Vice City Stories they will only give chase at a one to two star wanted level. After acquiring a higher wanted level, Police Cars arrive to take over pursuit.

title: Motor Officer
text: Motor officers in GTA V are officers of the San Andreas Highway Patrol and wear uniforms resembling the California Highway Patrol's. They wear beige pants and shirt, with a blue tie and black boots. Officers wear blue helmets and sunglasses, and have a two-way radio clipped to their shirt, along with a standard belt. Motor officers carry Pistols.

title: Motor Officer
text: Officers act identical to all GTA V police; by approaching them they will make warnings to maintain distance, and afterwards could give a one-star wanted level. Officers monitor speeds on the side of the road, and they rarely join police chases. They will only join if the suspect is near them. The officer will shoot at the player during the chase even if they only have a single wanted star.

text: The San Andreas Sheriff is an unnamed rural sheriff's department part of the San Andreas Police Department appearing in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: San Andreas Sheriff
text:
The sheriff's department has jurisdiction over the countryside and desert areas of the State of San Andreas, the deputies may be seen walking in populated rural areas or driving in their police cars. Rarely, a deputy may be also seen driving a Predator in rural waters.

Some of their quotes seem to indicate that they have bigoted undertones, as when they are pursuing Carl, they will say things such as "My daddy told me about fellas like you!", "The judge is going to string you up", "I ain't a racist, boy!", "We got different laws out here for you, boy!", and when pursuing on water, "I thought you couldn't swim!". This is backed by their lax use of the term "boy" when addressing Carl.

It is implied that some of the deputies take bribes in the mission Small Town Bank, along with showing their incompetence, worrying more about donuts than a bank being robbed, portraying a common stereotype of rural law enforcement. This behavior is reminiscent of that of and in .

title: San Andreas Sheriff
text: There are four stations for the sheriff's department. The station in Dillimore is the only one that can be accessed by the player. Barbara Schternvart is stationed at the El Quebrados station.

title: San Andreas Sheriff
text: The sheriff's deputies wear a dark brown shirt, light khaki pants with black stripe, black shoes, a cowboy hat and a golden seven-pointed-star badge. The patch worn by the deputies appears to be a recolored version of those worn by San Fierro Police officers.

title: San Andreas Sheriff
text:
The Ranger is the main vehicle of the sheriff's department. It is a modified Rancher equipped with a new paint job, a light bar and very good off-road handling and speed. This vehicle is primarily used for off-road work so it is typical that it operates in the rural areas. They may also use the Predator in rural rivers and coasts.

And, during the mission Small Town Bank, the deputies use HPV1000s and Enforcers.

title: San Andreas Sheriff
text: Every deputy carries a pistol and a nightstick as their main weapons, although they will also use shotguns when the player has a wanted level of at least three stars.

title: San Andreas Sheriff
text: The countryside deputy is an unused ped in GTA San Andreas. The deputy appears to be a middle-aged man wearing a grey shirt, grey pants with a black stripe and a shield badge. The uniform is similar to that of the . Its face texture is actually a slightly modified face texture of from Manhunt.

title: San Andreas Sheriff
text: The desert deputy is an unused ped in GTA San Andreas that was meant to patrol the desert areas. The deputy wears a tan shirt, green pants, black shoes, a cowboy hat and a golden seven-pointed-star badge.

title: San Andreas Sheriff
text:
The patches worn by the sheriff's deputies are similar, if not identical, to those worn by members of the SFPD.
The deputies may be seen driving police cars from the three main cities when the player approaches any of the cities.
Despite being labeled as , they seem to function more like or , as sheriffs and deputies can only patrol one , not an entire .

title: Utility Trailer
text: The Utility Trailer is a towable trailer that was supposed to appear in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, but was removed for unknown reasons.

title: Utility Trailer
text:
The Utility Trailer is depicted as a small compressor unit intended for street cleaning, mounted on a twin-axle chassis with a functional stand on the front. On the sides, the trailer features a set of hanging cables, small vents on the rear quarters, and "STREET CLEAN" markings, while the top features what seems to be a small exhaust/vent. On the rear end, the trailer features a small panel with gauges.

The vehicle normally spawns in an all-black color on the compressor unit. However, it is revealed to have a secondary color, which is applied on the top exhaust/vent and in the form of a single stripe passing down the whole unit.

When spawned, the only vehicle able to tow this trailer is the Utility Van.

title: Utility Trailer
text:
Being a compact and lightweight trailer, the Utility Trailer is rather acceptable for towing because of its stability, thanks to its four wheels, and it does not cause serious alterations to the performance of the car that it is towed by. However, it cannot withstand serious damage, similar to other small trailers.

Being a trailer, it cannot be driven; however, it does feature its own handling line.

text: 24 Hour Motel is a motel located in Idlewood and Willowfield in Los Santos, San Andreas, that appears in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: 24 Hour Motel
text:
The motel in Willowfield is located next to Ammu-Nation and the one in Idlewood appears behind the The Well Stacked Pizza. The motel has 14 rooms, however, none of them are enterable. The motel in Idlewood has grenades in an alcove, a gang tag on a wall and stationary vehicles on the parking lot. As its name implies, it is open 24 hours.

The motels are inaccessible to the player and play no role in the storyline whatsoever. However, while doing the Taxi Driver side-mission in Los Santos, passengers may ask to be taken to the motel branch in Idlewood.

title: Ocean Docks Freight Depot
text: The Ocean Docks Freight Depot is a railroad depot that appears in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Ocean Docks Freight Depot
text: The depot is used to store railroad cars in Ocean Docks, to the northeast of Los Santos International Airport.

title: Ocean Docks Freight Depot
section: Before the events of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text: Shortly before Carl Johnson's return to Los Santos, LSPD officer Ralph Pendelbury is killed at the back of the depot by Community Resources Against Street Hoodlums (C.R.A.S.H.), after he had uncovered evidence of corruption against police officers Frank Tenpenny and Eddie Pulaski. Pendelbury is killed by C.R.A.S.H. rookie officer Jimmy Hernandez under threat of death by Frank Tenpenny.

title: Ocean Docks Freight Depot
section: Events of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text: Later in the storyline, Tenpenny orders Carl Johnson to raid the freight warehouse in order to intercept an arms deal between the Ballas and the Russian Mafia. The Russian gunrunner Andre is killed during the shootout.

title: Ocean Docks Freight Depot
text:

title: Ocean Docks Freight Depot
text:
An unused version of the warehouse interior can be found in Interior World 8 at X = 1296.6, Y = 0.5, Z = 1001.0.

This may suggest that the warehouse was originally meant to be accessed via the yellow ENEX door arrows, or the interior layout was meant to be reused for something else.

The interior is wider and some of the textures are visibly stretched. The equivalent location of the office where CJ finds Andre is present in this interior (including the rear exit), although it has no collision.

title: Ocean Docks Freight Depot
text: A second unused warehouse interior internally named "Smash TV" uses assets from the Ocean Docks Freight Depot.

text: Psycho was a character cut during the development of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Psycho
text:
He is an unnamed character dubbed as the "Psycho" by the game's internal files.

It is assumed that this pedestrian model was intended to be a mission-exclusive character due to his file being named differently than the generic pedestrians, who generally use five or more random letters referring to their age, gender, ethnicity, occupation, and home region.

His textures, including face, are derived from the early version of the SWAT members, originally inspired by the real-life ' "Special Operations Group" tactical unit deployed to combat the as seen in early promotional screenshots.

title: Psycho

title: Psycho

title: Roadtrain Trailer
text: The Roadtrain Trailer is a cut towable trailer in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Roadtrain Trailer
text:
As its name suggests, the vehicle consists of a trailer intended to be towed by a Roadtrain. The trailer is completely left unused in the game files.

There are no entries for "rdtraint" in the vehicles.ide , carcols.dat or handling.cfg data files, thus it cannot be spawned as a functional trailer by normal means.

title: Roadtrain Trailer
text:
The Roadtrain Trailer is depicted as a traditional full-size container with two doors on the rear end, similar to the standard Articulated Trailer. It features a twin-axle trailer chassis with functional stands on the front and a large bumper with red tail lights on the rear end, along with two yellow warning stickers reading "LONG VEHICLE". The truck wheels are reused from industrial vehicles in Grand Theft Auto III. There are no liveries available for this trailer.

Due to a texture oversight, the trailer only spawns with a green body color, which is also applied to the trailer's chassis, stickers and lights.

title: Richman Tunnel
text: The Richman Tunnel is a highway tunnel that appears in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Richman Tunnel
text:
It serves part of the San Andreas Highway System, connecting Flint Intersection in Flint County to Mulholland Drive in Los Santos. It consists of two tunnels, each one with two lanes passing under the neighborhood of Richman.

Prior to the completion of The Green Sabre, the tunnel is blocked due to a recent earthquake.

title: Richman Tunnel
text:
In the early development, the tunnel was originally intended to be under construction instead of simply blocked by barricades. Leftovers of the original tunnel entrance under construction can still be found in the files.

title: Smash TV Warehouse
text: The Smash TV Warehouse, simply referred to as the Warehouse in-game, is an unused warehouse interior in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Smash TV Warehouse
text:
The "Smash TV" name comes from the file names for the warehouse model and textures (internally named genint3_smashtv.dff and smashtv.txd ). There is an invisible entrance/exit door marker at the textureless garage door, which does not work properly.

It is located in Interior World 1 at X = 1405.3, Y = -8.2, Z = 1000.9, shared with the Doherty Garage and Saint Mark's.

This unused interior is widely known to players due to an exploit inside the Ganton Gym interior which allows the player to explore the interior world through cheat codes. The warehouse's easily accessible door marker can be used as a convenient warp from Interior World 5 to Interior World 1.

title: Sumo Ring Arena
text:
The area is an unused interior intended for a cut 2-player game mode. It was originally started at the Los Santos Forum, according to unused coordinates for its mission marker.

The interior is a simplified replica of the Hyman Memorial Stadium from Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. Both the platform and the oval sand arena have proper collision.

Its usage as a car sumo ring arena is suggested by the file names for the platform (internally named sumoring.dff and ringwalls.dff ).

It is located in Interior World 16 at X = -1400, Y = 1250, Z = 1040. The K-DST radio station is played inside the interior.

This gamemode would later be officially introduced as an Adversary Mode named "Sumo" in Grand Theft Auto Online, as part of the Lowriders: Custom Classics update, in which the player must remain in the designated area for a specific time while trying to shove the competition off the platform.

text: The Spade is a cut melee weapon in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The model is still present as a cutscene prop.

title: Spade
text:
The Spade, like the Shovel, is a tool intended for digging, lifting and moving bulk material. Unlike the Shovel, however, the Spade has a flat blade with straight edges.

The weapon is mentioned as a cut item in the uncompiled initial.sc script file accidentally left in the original release of Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition, removed with later patches, containing original Rockstar North developer notes referring to the Shovel and Spade as separate weapons in the same section.

The Spade had only a single known spawn point in Bone County. It was originally found at the Hunter Quarry, although the item was replaced by a regular Shovel in late development:

CREATE_PICKUP SHOVEL PICKUP_ON_STREET_SLOW 637.0 832.0 -43.0 pickup_weapon[132] // - Spade // in front of the packing crate/mud
