title: San Fierro Bay Island
text: The unnamed San Fierro Bay Island was a location cut during the development of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: San Fierro Bay Island
text: Originally intended to be placed in the San Fierro Bay in San Fierro, the unnamed island can be spotted on an early San Andreas map found inside the Lil' Probe'Inn and Mike Toreno's Ranch. The map itself is in black and white and in low quality. Additionally, there are leftover UI textures for the Race Tournaments left in the PC version of the game in \models\txd\LD_RACE.txd , which used an early render of the San Andreas map with slightly better quality and being colored.

title: San Fierro Bay Island
text:
dels\txd\LD_RACE.txd , which used an early render of the San Andreas map with slightly better quality and being colored.

This colored map reveals that the island was present at an early stage of development and used textures of the nearby Tierra Robada's semi-arid grasslands for its terrain. The island itself appears to be a completely empty area at this point in development, although it appears to have some type of structure (seemingly boat jetties or rocks) on the southeastern coast which cannot be determined due to the poor quality of the image.

On the second earliest known version of the San Andreas map, used in the current Race Tournament UI maps and inside Area 69, the island has been removed from the San Fierro Bay and the town of Bayside was included, which could mean the island was cut in the very early stage of development.

title: San Fierro Bay Island
text:
ro Bay and the town of Bayside was included, which could mean the island was cut in the very early stage of development.

Replacing the island's original location, the in-game zones for Bayside ( SUNNN ), Bayside Marina ( SUNMA ) and the portion of San Fierro Bay in which the island was located ( SUNB2 ) appears to have been defined in a late stage of development, as these three defined zones will never give a 4-star wanted level whenever Tierra Robada is restricted to the player.

title: San Fierro Bay Island
text:
The island appears to have been inspired by , a state park, historical landmark and second largest island in the .

The removed island is commonly speculated to be due to its proximity to the Gant Bridge. However, it appears that this was changed during development, as only two months before the game's release, Rockstar's Director of PR, Jeff Castaneda, was asked in a interview for PlayStation Magazine Issue 53 whether Alcatraz Island would be featured in the game, to which he responded "Not sure yet. We haven't seen it. We're not sure whether we're going to put in the game.".

However, the Rockstar North team appears to have scouted Alcatraz Island a few years prior, during the development of Manhunt, to create textures for the Darkwoods Penitentiary . One of these textures (" mp_brickwall ") was later reused in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas by environment artist Michael Pirso, and is identified as originating from a real-life brick wall on Alcatraz Island.

Moreover, other similar brick wall textures are used for areas in San Fierro, including the Loco Syndicate Crack Factory. They are internally named using the prefix " ws_altz_* " – "altz" may or may not be an abbreviation for "Alcatraz".

title: Motel Rooms
text: Motel Rooms were save point locations cut during the development of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Motel Rooms
text:
During the early development of the game, the player would have been able to acquire motel rooms around San Andreas, but the idea was scrapped by Rockstar North during the development of the game.

Leftovers of this feature are still present in the game. There are two unused motel room interiors, both sharing the same layout and both giving the player access to the Wardrobe. These interiors were not completely finished, as both lack a "false interior box" behind the doors for the interior entering/exiting animation. The first motel room does not have a physical door when its interior is loaded.

The first motel room is located in Interior World 9 at X: 2253.17, Y: -1139.01, Z: 1050.63. The second motel room is located in Interior World 10 at X: 2262.83, Y: -1137.71, Z: 1050.63.

title: Motel Rooms
text:

In addition to the Wardrobe access, both of these interior models use the " _sv " suffix, confirming they were both intended as save points. They both have an interior display name "Motel room", and are both labelled as "Save Generic Motel 1 & 2" (abbreviated) in the american.gxt file.

Replicas of these motel rooms can be found inside the Jefferson Motel, with different floor textures. It is implied that the unused motel room models were reused from Jefferson Motel, as the floor textures for the Jefferson Motel corridor are partially visible at the entrance of the first interior.

title: Police Maverick (3D Universe)
text:
The Police Maverick (also known as the VCPD Maverick) is a police helicopter appearing in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and GTA Vice City Stories. The helicopter also exists in the game files for GTA Liberty City Stories but does not make any appearances (see variants).

The Police Maverick goes on to appear throughout the HD Universe where it again assumes the design of the standard Maverick but with an appropriate police livery. In each GTA game, the Police Maverick (or its chopper twin, see variants) pursues the player when they have a wanted level of at least three stars, a role previously held by the police variant of the Helicopter in Grand Theft Auto III.

title: Police Maverick (3D Universe)
text: In all of its appearances, the Police Maverick is a police adaptation of the civilian Maverick helicopter.

title: Police Maverick (3D Universe)
text:
In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the Maverick is used by the SAPD and is operated in all of the three main cities. In terms of individual parts, apart from the different registration numbers on the tail boom and the black primary color and white secondary color, the Police Maverick remains unchanged from its previous game.

Moreover, in this game, the Police Maverick is slightly scaled up, becoming bigger in contrast to the other 3D Universe depictions. This unique trait is also carried over to all of the helicopter's variants.

title: Police Maverick (3D Universe)
text: The Police Maverick flyable by the player controls similarly to a normal Maverick, differing only by its ability to pitch steeper than a regular Maverick, due to the slightly decreased mass (4,500kg vs 5,000kg of the normal Maverick). The Police Maverick has a slight better top speed and handling, given its usage as a police vehicle. While it does not have weapons or an average resistance, the Police Maverick is still a good choice for flying around the city.

The police Helicopter first appeared in Grand Theft Auto III where it assumed the design of the standard Helicopter (itself internally named "escape" due to its use in the game's final mission). title: Police Maverick (3D Universe)
text: In all of its appearances in the , the rear passengers of the Police Maverick (as well as its civilian counterpart) will sit in the exact same location in the middle of the rear bench seat. This results in both passengers seating "inside one another" if the player manages to get both passengers to seat in the rear. This glitch is actually present because the rear passengers have not been given defined seating coordinates inside the model of the helicopter as a result, they simply seat in its geometric center (centroid), as this is the default position for any vehicle occupants. A similar glitch happens with the Romero's Hearse in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.

title: Police Maverick (3D Universe)
text:
If the player does a replay, then the Police Maverick will fly away after the replay is done or exited.
The AI-controlled Police Maverick may sometimes appear under the ground if using the Jetpack to shake the Maverick off multiple times.
If the player manages to steal the AI-controlled Police Maverick, land, and exit the helicopter, the helicopter will act like it's still controlled by the AI, albeit it can't fly anymore. It will still shoot at the player from the underbelly of the helicopter. It will even deploy SWAT members if the player has a wanted level of more than three stars.
Doing a replay whilst controlling the hijacked Police Maverick will cause the helicopter and CJ to despawn, wasting the player.

title: Police Maverick (3D Universe)
text: Police Mavericks can be seen flying around without a wanted level. They are not solid and do not have any engine noise. They also can not be destroyed, and their rotors are static. On the PC version of the game, this is not the case, and they can be shot down by the player using the minigun or other heavy weapons (which instantly grants a two-star wanted level). Police Mavericks are most commonly seen patrolling areas of Los Santos dominated by gang crime, including Grove Street and Idlewood. They can also be observed flying around airports, presumably to monitor incoming and outgoing flights. The player can activate the Police Maverick's search light, however its direction can only be controlled on the PC version – in console versions, it moves in the opposite direction to the movement of the helicopter.

This feature is unavailable on the mobile version of the game, due to the action button being unavailable. However, if the player connects a gamepad to their device and presses the action/sub-mission button, the searchlight can be turned on. The only leftover of the vehicle present in the game files is an unused cutscene model " cspolicesa " intended for motion capture-based cutscenes (a static prop, not a functional vehicle), whose model name and texture files identify it as a state-wide police car.

When spawned, the SAPD Police vehicle will always appear facing north, and without functional animation rigs for its doors and wheels.

title: Police (SAPD)
text:
Being an exact replica of the LVPD variant of the Police vehicle, the SAPD Police vehicle generally resembles a 1981–1990 , with the sides and back reminiscent of the 1980–1989 , although it lacks any livery with the SAPD initials and seal. As with other cutscene vehicles, the SAPD Police vehicle uses the placeholder "California" license plate for its cutscene model.

The texture image for the vehicle body is vertically inverted by default, meaning that if spawned, the vehicle will have misplaced texture mapping.

The restaurant was originally located on the Rodeo section of Temple Drive in Los Santos, adjacent to Candy Suxxx's billboard. The building is seen on the promotional website for Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas on the "Rodeo" section, visible in the top right corner of the area.

title: Triad Mediator
text: He is a neutral party who tries to end a disagreement between two Triad gangs – Blood Feather Triad and Mountain Cloud Boys and agree on a solution without the necessity of violence.

title: Triad Mediator
section: Events of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text:
On the way to the Blood Feather Triad storehouse, Mountain Cloud Boys leader Wu Zi Mu and personal friend Carl Johnson spot people running away scared of something.

Woozie and Carl arrive at the storehouse only to encounter all of the Blood Feather Triad members killed. They find the meeting mediator hidden in a locked garage, who explains to the duo that the Da Nang Boys ambushed the Blood Feather Triad. As more Da Nang Boys arrive at the scene, the unarmed mediator hides again.

title: 24/7 (3D Universe)
text:
24/7 (also written as 24-7 and 24-Seven) is a chain of convenience stores featured in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City and Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

The store is also featured in Rockstar North's Manhunt series.

title: 24/7 (3D Universe)
text: The 24/7 makes its first appearance in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City due to reused early development assets from Manhunt, where the is derived from. In both games and its subsequent appearance in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the 24/7 franchise also operates other convenience stores and delicatessens, including Calleggi Delicatessen Restaurant, , Top Hat Liquor, 69¢ Only Stores and Roboi's Food Mart.

title: 24/7 (3D Universe)
text:
24/7 stores are widely spread throughout San Andreas. While nearly all 24/7 outlets tend to have distinctive exteriors, some even operating under alternate names (i.e. Roboi's Food Mart, Top Hat Liquor and the 69¢ Only Stores), all branches have closely related interiors, which feature a combination of store shelves that cycle with each visit. Unlike other businesses in the game, 24/7 stores don't have a dedicated map blip.

The 24/7 logo in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas closely resembles 7-Eleven's logo. The main distinctions lie in the wording and the colors used for the numbers; additionally, the real 7-Eleven logo features a slightly darker green background. Texture names for 24-7 outlets also incorporate "7_11" or "711"; The interior logo of 24/7 is different, and is colored white, yellow and blue, perhaps being a beta design of the logo.

title: 24/7 (3D Universe)
text:
The interior logo of 24/7 is different, and is colored white, yellow and blue, perhaps being a beta design of the logo.

Despite their frequent locations and enterable interiors, the stores have limited interactivity. beyond providing the ability to purchase food or drinks from vending machines. The 24/7 stores serve no storyline-related or 100% completion purpose in GTA San Andreas.

title: 24/7 (3D Universe)
text:
In GTA San Andreas, 24/7 stores use a total of three different interiors internally named " X7_11S ", " X711S2 " and " X7_11B ". X7_11S and X7_11B , which are used for all but one 24/7 store, occupy a smaller area and features the aforementioned vending machines and arcade games. However, X711S2 , which is linked to the west Mulholland, Los Santos outlet, features a moderately deep interior but has no vending machine or arcade cabinet, rendering that outlet useless in gameplay.

There are additionally three unused 24/7 interiors, " X711S3 ", " X7_11C " and " X7_11D ", that are only accessible via in the interior realm. X7_11C is designed as a moderately large interior; X711S3 and X7_11D are the two largest 24/7 interiors, with X7_11D bearing a unique L-shaped floorplan.

title: 24/7 (3D Universe)
text:
y large interior; X711S3 and X7_11D are the two largest 24/7 interiors, with X7_11D bearing a unique L-shaped floorplan.

The interiors tend to feature a clerk manning the stores' counter, while two to four pedestrians (or customers) are usually found roaming the aisles, uttering unique shopping-related lines, as well as performing animated sequences where they retrieve items from store shelves and interacting with the player only if provoked. Customers may also interact with the store clerk in a short animation, but the customers never leave the store. The store shelves are also fairly detailed, featuring various branded products like Love Juice, Cherry Popper ice-cream or pizzas from Vice City.

title: 24/7 (3D Universe)
text: The in always appears with one of five liveries applied. The livery is likely inspired by this brand's name and colors.

title: 24/7 (3D Universe)
text:
The stated list of ingredients on the store's own budget "Savings" range is just random gibberish, which could be lampooning the use of artificial ingredients in processed foods.
San Fierro is the only city in San Andreas that does not have any 24/7s.
Pedestrians can be seen picking products from shelves and apparently storing them in their pockets, indicating that they are probably .

title: Shock To The System
text:
The mission is labelled as the sixth and final mission ( STEAL6 ) of the Wang Cars asset mission strand for Cesar Vialpando, taking place after the mission Puncture Wounds ( STEAL5 ). Similarly to the first mission of the same strand, it involved stealing an unidentified vehicle in movement. In order to steal the target vehicle, Zero installed a short range signal device on Carl's vehicle that launches an electromagnetic pulse when in range.

A "pulse" bar is displayed on the HUD to indicate the EMP charge. After using one charge, the player would have to wait for the bar to refill in order to launch another.

As with the other target vehicles in the same mission strand, the player was intended to steal it and deliver it to the Doherty Garage in order to complete the mission.

It is clearly seen in the official strategy guide in a screenshot of the Air Raid cutscene on page 107. The box is also barely visible in a promotional screenshot showing the interior of the Zero RC shop.

As with other vehicle boxes, it depicts an early design of the Cargobob as a , similar to its HD Universe counterpart manufactured by the Western Company.

Rusty Brown's Ring Donuts is a donut and coffee shop appearing in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and GTA Liberty City Stories.

title: Rusty Brown's Ring Donuts (3D Universe)
text:
Rusty Brown's Ring Donuts is advertised on the official manual for Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas as a restaurant chain in the State of San Andreas, despite not having a physical location.

A Rusty Brown's Ring Donuts interior exists in-game, used by Jim's Sticky Ring donut shop in Los Santos, suggesting it is owned by the Rusty Brown's Ring Donuts chain. The interior display name in-game is "Rusty Brown's", and its GXT entry uses the FD* prefix used to categorize all interactive food restaurant interiors in-game.

A generic street criminal pedestrian (Black Male Young Criminal " BMYCR ") can be heard saying "I'm a Rusty Brown doughnut eating gangsta!". Also, the generic food vendor (Black Male Old Chilli " BMOCHIL ") will sometimes comment "Have you been to Rusty Brown's?".

title: Rusty Brown's Ring Donuts (3D Universe)
text:
o, the generic food vendor (Black Male Old Chilli " BMOCHIL ") will sometimes comment "Have you been to Rusty Brown's?".

Additionally, in Colonel Fuhrberger's kitchen, there is a leaflet for Rusty Brown's Ring Donuts on the table, indicating that it could have been featured in the game. This can also be seen in the Johnson House.

title: Rusty Brown's Ring Donuts (3D Universe)
text:
In addition to the interior of Rusty Brown's Ring Donuts, unused models for donuts on trays can be found in the interior-specific IMG file, listed along the other fast food trays for Cluckin' Bell, Burger Shot and Well Stacked Pizza and following the same naming (using low / med / high suffixes), indicating they were intended for a similar food selection menu.

These items are listed in the shopping.dat file, confirming they were intended as purchasable food items in-game and having the same size-based price from other restaurants ($2 for low, $5 for medium and $10 for high). It was the only restaurant not to serve healthy food items. The GXT entries naming each of Rusty Brown's food items ( RUSLOW , RUSMED and RUSHIG ) are missing from the american.gxt file.

title: Rusty Brown's Ring Donuts (3D Universe)

Moreover, other donut shops with detailed exterior (Jim's Sticky Ring, Tuff Nut Donuts and King Ring) contains unused interior entrance boxes behind their doors, intended for the door entering animations while loading interiors. This may suggest that the existing donut shop interior was intended as a generic interior shared between all donut shops.

text: The Turning Tricks Bike School is a state-licensed advanced motoring school appearing in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Turning Tricks Bike School
text:
The school is located in the neighborhood of Blackfield in Las Venturas, San Andreas, to the south of the Blackfield Stadium and to the north of Greenglass College. The bike school is operated by Turning Tricks Advanced Motoring. It consists of a small accessible main building and a very large training ground at the back of the building, surrounded by a wall to prevent the player from leaving the area during a test.

The Bike School tests are available from the building interior upon completing Deconstruction, although only normally accessible with permission from C.R.A.S.H. (without any wanted level penalty) after Yay Ka-Boom-Boom.

title: Turning Tricks Bike School
text:
The Bike School tests were originally planned to be started from a loadable interior, consisting of a less detailed duplicate of the existing Turning Tricks Driving School interior except the hall. The unused Bike School interior is still available in the game, inaccessible by normal means.

It is located in Interior World 3 at X: 1494.3350, Y: 1305.6510, Z: 1093.2890, internally named vgSbikeschl* (Las Venturas [Vegas] South Bike School).

text: The Micro SMG is a weapon appearing in Grand Theft Auto III, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, , GTA Liberty City Stories and GTA Vice City Stories.

title: Micro SMG (3D Universe)
text:
The Micro SMG has appeared in all games in the . The weapon's name on the HUD has changed various times as it recurred through the series:
In GTA III, the submachine gun is named Uzi.
In GTA Vice City, the submachine gun is named Uz-1.
In GTA Advance, the submachine gun is named Uz-I.
In GTA San Andreas, GTA Liberty City Stories and GTA Vice City Stories, the submachine gun is named Micro SMG.

Across the 3D Universe, the Micro SMG is always the cheapest and most traditional submachine gun of every game, as opposed to the more contemporary and expensive SMG, as well as being a common sight in the hands of many gangs in the later missions throughout the games.

The Micro SMG is based on variants of the real-life :

In Grand Theft Auto III and Grand Theft Auto Advance, the Uzi/Uz-I is modeled after a Micro Uzi (with the folding stock removed), an even smaller version that has some resemblance with the .
In Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories, the Uz-1/Micro SMG is modeled after a full-size Uzi, complete with a stock and a large barrel handle on the lower side, in front of the trigger grip.
In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the Micro SMG is modeled after a Micro Uzi, but lacks a stock hinge on its rear. It replaces the Mac 10's role from Grand Theft Auto: Vice City due to the Uz-1 model being cut during development.

The weapon is favored by gang members and law enforcement units, including the SWAT and Vice Squad.

The weapon is favored by gang members and law enforcement units, including the SWAT and Vice Squad.

It is one of the few weapons that used real-life names in the original releases of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, appearing as the Uzi 9mm in the day-one v1.40 release for the PlayStation 2. It was renamed Uz-1 in later releases. Rockstar North remodeled and renamed the weapon in later versions of GTA Vice City, possibly to avoid copyright and trademark infringements.

title: Micro SMG (3D Universe)
text:
The Micro SMG behaves differently depending on the game in which it appears. In Grand Theft Auto III, it takes the form of the compact Uzi, which allows the player to run while firing. This version holds 25 rounds, and has a moderate rate of fire and damage.

The Grand Theft Auto: Vice City rendition is a full-sized model of the real-life Uzi, which means the player can only fire while in a stationary position. It holds 30 rounds, and has a high rate of fire equal to that of the Mac 10. When compared to it, it deals higher damage (the same as in GTA III), at the expense of not allowing Tommy to run while firing (while the Mac 10 does).

title: Micro SMG (3D Universe)
text:
In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the player can run while firing the weapon, since this version is a compact Uzi. It also has a higher magazine capacity of 50 rounds, but has a rather slow rate of fire equal to that of the Tec-9. Its capabilities can be quite lethal at close range, but it will often miss the target at longer ranges due to its heavy recoil, so it is advised to fire short bursts at distances. Depending on the weapon skill, some of the weapon's attributes change:
At 'Poor' (default) weapon skill, the Micro SMG has similar stats to other renditions, albeit with a lower rate of fire and range. After reaching the 'Gangster' weapon skill with the Micro SMG, the weapon slightly improves in accuracy and range (both lock-on and weapon). After reaching the 'Hitman' weapon skill, Carl Johnson will dual-wield them, making them even more effective due to the increased fire rate.

title: Micro SMG (3D Universe)
text:
Hitman' weapon skill, Carl Johnson will dual-wield them, making them even more effective due to the increased fire rate. Lock-on range also improves slightly and matches with the overall range, and magazine size increases from 50 to 100 rounds.

In Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories, the Micro SMG behaves like its counterpart from GTA Vice City. However, in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories, it has a lowered rate of fire (along with the Mac 10), which means it is outclassed by the SMG in nearly every way, since the latter has the same fire rate, but deals much higher damage.

text: Poncho is a drug dealer living in East Los Santos, originally intended to play a role during the cut mission Doberman. His house is located adjacent to the Rodriguez Iron Works recycling center.

text:

In a phone call with Tenpenny, after Poncho's whereabouts are found, Carver threatens to testify to the Drug Enforcement Administration about Tenpenny's deals with Poncho. Carver sends some police officers to apprehend Poncho in his house in East Los Santos.

Convinced that Poncho would squeal about his deals with the C.R.A.S.H., Tenpenny and Pulaski task Carl Johnson with preventing Poncho and the evidence from being delivered to the Los Santos Police Headquarters, by killing Poncho and the police officers bagging his drugs as evidence.

title: Below the Belt Gym
text: The Below the Belt Gym is a gymnasium featured in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Below the Belt Gym
text:
CJ can learn kickboxing moves in this gym, as well as using the other facilities to increase or decrease certain statistics, specifically stamina, muscle and fat. Learning kickboxing is required for 100% completion.

Kickboxing is the strongest style CJ can learn. The kickboxing combo can knockout opponents in just 4 hits unlike other moves due to its final elbow strike being extremely powerful. Another advantage of this style is that CJ can grapple his opponents during the combo, temporarily immobilizing them.

It is located in Redsands East, Las Venturas, the gym becomes accessible after completing the Drive-Thru mission, however, attempting to enter the gym will automatically give the player a 4-star wanted level, as Las Venturas is not unlocked at that point. It can be accessed without any police attention after the mission Yay Ka-Boom-Boom, after which the player is able to explore the entire state without any trouble.

There is a boxer standing next to the gym's lockers who serves as the kickboxing trainer, along with two boxers training with each other inside the boxing ring.

title: Below the Belt Gym
text: It is highly advisable that CJ has maximum health and muscle, and has learned how to fight before attempting to learn kickboxing because the opponent here can easily knock CJ out.

title: Below the Belt Gym
text:
The gym's name is a reference to the phrase "hitting below the belt", an illegal move in boxing, and also a term for an unfair, personal remark.
The last elbow strike of this style's combo is a guaranteed one hit kill.
This can be verified by performing the combo on one pedestrian, turning aside just before the final hit and striking another passing pedestrian with the elbow.
Armored and high health opponents, such as story mission target characters, FBI agents, Military soldiers and gym trainers, can survive this move with either half or little amount of health remaining.
Unlike the Ganton Gym, firing a gun will not anger everyone inside this gym's interior.
If the player kills one of the boxers in the boxing ring, the remaining boxer will cower in fear.
The radio station that plays inside this gym is CSR 103.9.

text: Come see the great state of San Andreas the old fashioned, (slow) way; by rail. Brown Streak Railroad is a railroad company featured in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Brown Streak Railroad
text: The Brown Streak Railroad is a combination of passenger and freight rail operating within the State of San Andreas, operating 24 hours a day through the stations of each city. The company operates a fleet of Brown Streak passenger trains (usually with two to three coaches) and Freight trains (usually with two to four flatcars).

title: Brown Streak Railroad
text:
The Brown Streak Railroad is 18.2 kilometers long, runs a full circuit throughout the entire state of San Andreas, and has two tracks providing service. At two points, the rails combine into a single track and run for a mile or so before parting back into two tracks. Around 80% of the track is constructed on ground level, while the rest is either underground or elevated. In general, all trains use the inner track, with a few exceptions: during the In the Beginning, Wrong Side of the Tracks and Snail Trail. In addition to the main route, there are additional ones:
In Los Santos, a track connects to the main circuit and is a more industrial line. This line cannot be driven on in the game and is merely for show. In San Fierro, a track connects to the main line and leads to the docks in Easter Basin.

title: Brown Streak Railroad
text: There are six stations around the state, which the player can wait for a train to ride on the train cars (with the passenger coach free of charge) or simply hijack the locomotives. Trains will usually depart within thirty seconds of arriving on a station platform. Trains can also be spotted en route between stations.

title: Brown Streak Railroad

Market Station in the Market district, possibly referring to a station on the Metro Red Line. Also has a side platform, but only on Track 2. Ticket Machines are available.

title: Brown Streak Railroad
text: Cranberry Station, in the Doherty district, with two side platforms and one island platform. Features a glass atrium, ticket offices and vending machines. A San Fierro cable car line is located directly in front of the station's entrance. The station is right across the warehouse in San Fierro. Inside the station, in the bottom-right corner, is a camera.

title: Brown Streak Railroad
text:
Yellow Bell Station, in the Prickle Pine district, with side platforms. Ticket offices and vending machines are also available. Free parking is also available for those who wish to use the lots.
Linden Station near the Linden Side district is very similar to Yellow Bell station.
Sobell Rail Yards in eastern Las Venturas near Linden Station. It has a little platform which is not required in sub-missions.

title: Brown Streak Railroad
text:
Railroad Crossings 
There are several railroad crossings all around the state. All crossings have re/white barriers and flashing red lights, with the exception of some in Los Santos. The barriers go down when a train is near the crossing, but many times, the train will be going too fast for the barriers to be fully down. In the desert, at times, the trains will be going at full speed, and there is only a split-second warning before a train crosses. A train strike at this speed may kill the player instantly. Civilian drivers will also attempt to cross after a few seconds anyway, and at times, they will attempt to cross as soon as the barriers go back up, knocking the barriers down. Pedestrians still walk across the crossings regardless if the barrier is down, and if the barrier is down for more than 15 seconds, the cars will drive through the barrier anyway (causing it to fall off).

title: Brown Streak Railroad
text:
f the barrier is down for more than 15 seconds, the cars will drive through the barrier anyway (causing it to fall off).

The trains do not stop for anything nor do they blow a horn, so there will be no warning of a crash. The trains are strong enough to even push aside a Rhino with ease. The barrier-less crossings in Los Santos may be very dangerous; there are no barriers, no lights, and the traffic lights will not signify a train either. Civilians will not stop for a train here, nor do pedestrians, and at times, when the drivers stop at a red light, they will be right on the tracks, making them very prone to being hit by a train. However, vehicles normally do not explode instantly upon impact, but this has been seen in the mission Wrong Side of the Tracks.

The Freight Train Mission is a side mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas that involves the player transporting freight around the state in a Brown Streak or a Freight under a time limit. The challenge is available after all three islands have been unlocked, since it needs delivery to all five stations scattered around the state, namely Unity Station, Market Station, Cranberry Station, Yellow Bell Station and Linden Station. Like most side missions, it is activated by pressing the submission button. The challenge is completed when both levels have been completed; it is failed when either the train is derailed, the time limit expires, a station is missed, if the vehicle is abandoned or if the submission button is pressed.

section: Events of Grand Theft Auto San Andreas
text:
In the process of attempting to become famous, OG Loc ruined Madd Dogg's career by having CJ steal his rhyme book and kill his manager (who called Loc whack). Despite the fact that Loc is a terrible rapper with a squeaky, scratchy voice, he slowly but surely makes a name for himself in the underground by using Madd Dogg's stolen lyrics.

After the downfall of the Grove Street Families, Big Smoke chose to launder his drug money by granting Loc a record contract, making him rich and famous. Using Madd Dogg's rhyme book, he recorded his debut album Str8 From Tha Streetz, immediately paired with a clothing company, Loc-Down (a reference to his prison stint, complete with a handcuff logo) available at Victim. This drives Madd Dogg to a drug-fueled downward spiral, losing his mansion and coming to the brink of suicide.

Bitch 'n' Dog Food is a dog food producing company in the 3D Universe of the .

The company also appears in Rockstar North's Manhunt series.

title: Bitch'n' Dog Food (3D Universe)
text:
The company is known to be active as early as 1984. As of 2001, Bitch 'n' Dog Food is owned by media mogul Donald Love and is treated as part of the Love Media conglomerate.

The company acquired the former Don Kiddick's Sausage Factory building in the neighborhood of Trenton in Portland, Liberty City, rebranded into a dog food factory for the company. The factory is operated by serial killer Marty Chonks.

The official advertisement for Bitch 'n' Dog Food available at LoveMedia.tv claims the company use "tasty bone meal, chicken carcasses, the scrapings off the abattoir floor and lots of other nutritional goodies".

Bitch'n' Dog Food owns a fleet of Benson delivery trucks in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, and the company's dog food cans can be found in Fidl and Verdi Groceries stores in GTA Vice City Stories, and later in 24/7 stores in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Bitch'n' Dog Food (3D Universe)
text:
in Fidl and Verdi Groceries stores in GTA Vice City Stories, and later in 24/7 stores in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

Textures for dog food cans bearing the Bitch'n' Dog Food logo also appear in Manhunt, originally intended for cans. However, in the final version, the texture is only mapped into a rusty watering can in-game. In Manhunt 2, whenever a item is stored in the inventory, it is depicted as a Bitch'n' Dog Food can on the lure item bag, using the aforementioned Manhunt dog food texture. It also reinforces that Sprunk cans replaced dog food cans as lure items during the game's development, as evidenced by the inconsistent HUD icon for the Can in the original title.

title: Bitch'n' Dog Food (3D Universe)
text: The company's name is derived from the terms "bitch", a term for a female dog, and "bitchin", slang for something of a good quality.

title: Binco (3D Universe)
text:
Binco is a place where you get what you pay for... the clothes are cheap and so is the quality. A discount store located in the Ganton district; you can expect to find a large selection of budget priced plaid shirts, khakis, and sneakers. A word of advice for those not familiar with the inner city life of San Andreas please be sure to pick the right colors, because the wrong ones could kill you. 
Binco is a clothing store appearing in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and mentioned in GTA Liberty City Stories.

title: Binco (3D Universe)
text: Access to Binco is unlocked after the mission Nines and AK's. There are four Binco stores located in San Andreas, all sharing the same interior. The stores are primarily based on the concept of a . This could possibly explain the signs in the store which read "Everything 99¢", despite having nothing in the store that sells for 99¢.

title: Binco (3D Universe)
text:
Clothing in GTA San Andreas/Binco 
Binco is the cheapest of the clothing shops in the state of San Andreas, with no item exceeding $100. The clothing on sale is centered around street clothing commonly worn by gang members. Many items are available in green, the gang color of the Grove Street Families.

At the start of the game, the player owns three Binco items as default - White Tank (Torso), Blue Jeans (Legs) and Black Low-Tops (Shoes).

The store also offers various novelty articles of clothing, such as joke glasses, masks, eyepatches, and a cowboy hat and cowboy boots. Binco is the only store to sell briefs (referred to as boxers in game, which can be worn without pants).

title: Binco (3D Universe)
text: The name Binco may refer to (pronounced "Jenco"), a -based urban clothing company that first gained prominence in the early 1990s. The chain itself is possibly based on , an American chain of discount clothing.

title: Binco (3D Universe)
text:
The name “Binco” is similar to “Bin Co.”, implying the stores are like garbage bins. This is reinforced by the company's slogan, "more trash for less cash".
The combination of a Black Tank Top (Torso), Black Boxers (Legs), Sandals and Flip-Flops (Shoes) gives a shout-out to both DC Comics' character, Plastic Man and Monkey D. Luffy from One Piece.
The font used in the logo is .

title: Doherty Garage
text: The Doherty Garage is a derelict Xoomer gas station/garage in Doherty, San Fierro, San Andreas that appears in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The garage is obtained by Carl Johnson after winning a street race against Claude and Catalina. The save point features a vehicle storage garage where the player can store up to four cars.

title: Doherty Garage
text:
The garage was previously a Xoomer gas station, until it was closed c.1987. Following closure, the petrol pumps were removed and the garage stood derelict until it came into the ownership of Claude. After winning a street race against Claude and Catalina, Carl was awarded the deed to the garage in 1992.

The interior of the garage is seen during mission cutscenes. It consists of a large garage area and a small office partition. On the outside, the front windows are broken and a faded "Xoomer" sign can be seen on the front of the garage. It also has its corresponding office.

After collecting all 50 Snapshots, the Shotgun, Micro SMG, Sniper Rifle and Grenades are available here, spawning between the inactive garage and main office building.

title: Doherty Garage
section: Events of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
text: After The Truth is found by the police and he and Carl flee to San Fierro, upon arriving at the garage, Carl finds it derelict and in desperate need of repair. Before Carl sinks into his despair, Kendl convinces him to turn the situation around and make something of the place. With the help of The Truth, Carl employs Dwaine, Jethro, and Zero to work in the garage. With the additional help of Cesar Vialpando, Carl and the rest of the crew are able to turn the garage into a successful chop-shop. The group, along with Wu Zi Mu and the San Fierro Triads, also use the garage as a base of operation to hunt down the Loco Syndicate. Later on, Carl and Cesar work on delivering rare vehicles on the customers wish list to the Wang Cars showroom they have purchased earlier.

title: Doherty Garage

During a later mission titled Highjack for the undercover government agent Mike Toreno, Carl and Cesar attempt to steal a tanker truck on the Garver Bridge, after which they deliver the truck to the garage.

title: Doherty Garage
text:
A glitch on the PS2 and Xbox versions of the game causes the garage not to always open, requiring several approaches before it will open and allow access. An identical glitch occurs with the Portland Safehouse in GTA Liberty City Stories.
Saving custom vehicles with decals in the garage will result in the decals being removed. The same thing also applies to vehicles with unique decals, e.g. The Truth's Camper. This glitch has been confirmed on the Xbox, Android and PC versions of the game.

title: Doherty Garage
text: Although Carl acquires the garage after Farewell, My Love..., the garage is technically available from the beginning of the game, meaning that the player can use the garage even before San Fierro is unlocked. The garage can hold a maximum of four vehicles; although more can be placed inside (i.e. two cars and two motorcycles, or six motorcycles), exceeding four vehicles may result in one or all of the vehicles parked inside disappearing after a period of time. The garage is larger than most available up to this point in the game, capable of holding two Monster trucks. Although there is a second garage immediately adjacent, it is not accessible.

Due to the garage's proximity to a busy pedestrian sidewalk, care must be taken when opening it to make sure street criminals do not get into the garage, as they are known to attempt to drive away in vehicles parked inside (this is a particular concern if the player chooses to back vehicles into the garage or wants to avoid damaging vehicles). An STD calendar inside the garage is open on the month of January, which shows that Thursday is the first day of the year. title: Cobra Marital Arts Gym
text:
Located in the Garcia district, this martial arts dojo is recognized and revered throughout the country. The Cobra Marital Arts Dojo was founded by the Master Sensei over 30 years ago. The master sensei has trained everyone from CIA agents to Vinewood action heroes. His services are greatly sought after and a few have been lucky enough to train with the master. Make your way to the Cobra Marital Arts Dojo and if you make it through the doors, consider it a great honor and privilege. 
The Cobra Marital Arts is a martial arts dojo and a gymnasium featured in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Cobra Marital Arts Gym
text:
The Cobra Marital Arts gymnasium is located in the Garcia neighborhood of San Fierro, just down the road from the driving school. It is available after completing the mission Drive-Thru, although entering the area before the completion of The Green Sabre will trigger a 4-star wanted level due to the city itself not being accessible at this point.

Carl Johnson can work out in the dojo to increase his strength and fitness or receive training from the Master Sensei, who teaches him advanced fighting moves. The sensei, who serves as the dojo's trainer, is seen monitoring his students, while there are two other people training at the back of the interior.

title: Cobra Marital Arts Gym
text: Another one of Rockstar Games' jokes, instead of M-A-R-T-I-A-L, it's spelled M-A-R-I-T-A-L, probably as a reference to "Marital" as in "Marital aids". The dojo's sensei uses the same character model as The Snakehead, as well as some of his dialogue. The gym is probably a reference to the Cobra Kai karate dojo in the movie series The Karate Kid. According to police records the dojo is regularly frequented by police for training purposes. It is said to have great showers which they share and somebody seems to always drop the soap. Unlike the Ganton Gym, firing a gun will not anger everyone inside the interior. The shirtless person wearing a pair of red pants is only seen inside the dojo. He was supposed to be the male lifeguard pedestrian who would appear on the beaches, but he is not listed anywhere in pedgrp.dat. He has the same voice lines as one of the drug dealers.

text: The Casino Floor is a casino located in Redsands West, Las Venturas, San Andreas, that appears in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Casino Floor
text:
It is a casino located to the east of the Las Venturas Bandits Stadium, and is one of the three accessible casinos in Las Venturas. The casino is very small compared to the Four Dragons Casino and Caligula's Palace. The front sign only says "Casino" but when the player enters the casino, it will say "Casino Floor". This casino offers blackjack, wheel of fortune, video poker, and a pool table.

In a similar fashion to the other two accessible casinos, three songs from Master Sounds 98.3 can be heard while inside:
Maceo & The Macks' "Cross The Tracks (We Better Go Back)"
Bobby Byrd's "Hot Pants - I'm Coming, I'm Coming, I'm Coming"
James Brown's "Funky President"

title: Casino Floor
text:
The casino guards that only spawn is a black, bald-headed guard in an executive suit (model id 163 - BMYBOUN) and have a one fixed spawning location which is at the upper-right side of the interior, unlike The Four Dragons Casino where it spawn both BMYBOUN and his whiter counterpart WMYBOUN (164) and have many spawn locations for them to appear. They are programmed to behave like police officers, as the player will obtain a one-star wanted level if they fire a gun or aim a weapon at them, while two stars are obtained by killing the guards with a firearm.
If the player has a wanted level of three stars or more, regular police will start spawning. If the player decides to retaliate against the officers, they stop shooting and put their hands up or cower in fear, and only the casino guards shoot at the player.

Drive-Thru Confessions is a church featured in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas located in Palomino Creek, Red County, San Andreas.

title: Drive-Thru Confessions Church
text:
The church is located behind the Palomino Creek Library. There is a small confessional booth and a driveway going up to it, implying that people can receive services from the confessional by driving up alongside it, however, the player cannot use it. A Romero may sometimes spawn in the driveway of the church in the PS2 version and a Shovel can be found in the graveyard. A pedestrian may be found sitting in front of the entrance doors of the church.

title: Drive-Thru Confessions Church

text: Chuff Security Co. is a security company appearing in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and GTA Vice City Stories.

title: Chuff Security Co.
text:
The security company comes from early assets in Rockstar North's Manhunt, shared during the development of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. While the Chuff Security alarm was left unused in both games, a security card from the company is used across multiple Grand Theft Auto titles as a mission objective pickup.

The only known worker of Chuff Security is P. Rowe, whose image is seen on the security card pickup. A picture of Wonderboy guitarist Peter Rowe is used to represent this character, serving as one of the many Easter eggs towards the Wonderboy band by fellow member Wayland Standing, a Rockstar North environment artist.

DAD-manufactured alarms can be found at the Bunch of Tools hardware store in Vice City Beach and Wang Cars in San Fierro, albeit with compressed textures.

text:
In GTA III, one of company's ships, the Les Cargo, can be found in Portland Harbor and is being used by the Colombian Cartel as a factory for the drug SPANK. The ship is blown up by Claude and 8-Ball in the mission Bomb Da Base: Act II.

In GTA Vice City, two sunken Chartered Libertine Lines shipwrecks can be found underwater. Both wrecks are identical, and their hulls are split in half. Also, there is a Chartered Libertine Lines ship docked at Viceport. The company plays a role in the mission Spilling the Beans where Tommy Vercetti has to interrogate its boss in order to learn about the arrival of counterfeit plates. It is stated to be run either by the Vice City Triads or the Counterfeit Syndicate.

In GTA San Andreas, the company's logo appears on a box that Carl Johnson steals in the mission Green Goo, with a second box appearing in the mission Dam and Blast.

title: Cluckin' Bell (3D Universe)
text: Cluckin' Bell is based on and : the former uses a bell logo, while the latter serves fried chicken. Both companies are owned by the same parent corporation: , Inc. It is possible that Cluckin' Bell could also be based on , because of the color scheme. The name comes from a quote in the episode "" of the British comedy series , which contains the line "I think the phrase rhymes with clucking bell", a censored form of the phrase fucking hell. The franchise is probably inspired by , as both names are s. Elements of the chain seem to be a parody of , including the employee dressed as a chicken (possibly a reference to Chick-fil-A's cows), and some of the slogans used by the company.

title: Cluckin' Bell (3D Universe)
text:
Cluckin' Bell, like other fast food outlets in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, offer the player four meals, each with different quantities of fat, with the Salad Meal being the only fat-free option. title: Cluckin' Bell (3D Universe)
text: Like other fast-food outlets in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, Cluckin' Bell is present in all major cities in San Andreas. Within rural San Andreas, the chain has only one outlet within town limits (Angel Pine), and two outlets at intersections outside Tierra Robada and Fort Carson. Although the mission Drive-Thru has Carl use the drive-thru at the Willowfield branch, most other times it can only be accessed through the front door. All locations feature a cashier who's openly rude to his customers, often berating them in a spiteful way for even buying food there ("If you come back, you're a moron."). There is a Cluckin' Bell outlet in Market, Los Santos, which is unmarked on the map in the original PS2 version. Moreover, the very same branch has a glitched door, which is only properly rendered from certain angles. This occurs on multiple versions of the game.

title: Cluckin' Bell (3D Universe)
text: The Cluckin' Huge Meal features "wing pieces" in a bucket, a clear reference to typical chicken-based fast food restaurants which often serve chicken pieces in buckets, usually for larger, more expensive menus.

title: Cluckin' Bell (3D Universe)
text: In a beta screenshot, the employee is seen to be much fatter and dons a much-too-tight shirt. The back of the employee's shirt has writing that reads: "Taste the cock", a deliberate reference to oral sex. The employee in the store is voiced by Joe Lo Truglio, who later voiced Vincenzo Cilli in GTA Liberty City Stories. Radio X DJ Sage comments about how she "did a guy" behind Cluckin' Bell during the intro to 's "". In the mission Drive-Thru, Carl Johnson, Sweet Johnson, Big Smoke, and Ryder receive Burger Shot boxes instead of Cluckin' Bell boxes. Cluckin' Bell had a website on the real-life internet, designed in HTML 2.0 style, but running on Flash. The site displayed the menu and advertising from Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. After the end of support for Flash, the website was taken offline on 12 December 2020. It now serves as a redirect to the Rockstar Games main page.

text:
Located in the Mulholland and the Marina district in Los Santos, this fast food chain is all about the beef. ”Where’s the beef,” you ask? Burger Shot (formerly The Burger Shot) is a chain of hamburger fast-food restaurants in the of the .

The chain is also featured in Rockstar North's Manhunt series.

title: Burger Shot (3D Universe)
text: Burger Shot first appeared in the form of "The Burger Shot," a small restaurant in GTA Vice City (among many other less known outlets in the Game) where the player can replenish their health if it is below 100 points. The restaurant has risen in prominence in GTA San Andreas, where it is now a large chain based in multiple locations. In addition to replenishing health, Burger Shot in GTA San Andreas allows the player to eat from a range of set meals in order to eliminate their hunger, or accumulate fat by eating fatty food. Burger Shot is absent as a restaurant chain in GTA Liberty City Stories and GTA Vice City Stories (with the location of its western food court and neighboring The Cheesy Crust Pizza Co. being occupied by Flap Lickin' Chickin, while the eastern food court locations were undeveloped spaces).

title: Burger Shot (3D Universe)
text:
It is a parody of American fast food chain . The name and color scheme resembles Burger King, but the style of logo resembles Hardee's. Its notoriously unhealthy and sub-par food, aggressive marketing tactics (especially towards children in particular), and boastful identity (even prizing its status as America's favorite chain restaurant) suggests that it also parodies (though McDonald's is parodied in the HD Universe as Wigwam Burger).

"Burger Shot" is a slang term for a photo of the female genitalia.

title: Didier Sachs (3D Universe)
text:
Access to Didier Sachs is unlocked after the mission Saint Mark's Bistro. Didier Sachs is an upscale clothing store which primarily offers suits of various forms that can be purchased and worn by the player. Befitting its upscale status, Didier Sachs' clothing is the most expensive to purchase, and its only store is located in Rodeo Shopping Mall in the neighborhood of Rodeo, Los Santos (with a Victim outlet right next door). 

If interacting with pedestrians while wearing clothing or jewelry from Didier Sachs, Carl Johnson will comment about how well he is dressed, and swears less, as opposed to when wearing cheaper clothing. Didier Sachs's clothing also gives some of the highest Sex Appeal and Respect boosts available, only rivaled by some of Binco's items that give more respect as they fit better with the Grove Street Families' dress code.

title: Didier Sachs (3D Universe)

Despite being the most luxurious clothing store, Didier Sachs offers the least variety in terms of the types of clothing offered (most of the clothing are merely re-colors of a few types of clothes), as well as being the smallest outlet in comparison to other clothing stores. This is justified as the outlet is expected to be patronized by fewer customers but is able to make up for it with higher prices and larger profits per customer.

While the price of nearly all major articles of clothing as well as accessories (chains and watches) are normally several thousands of dollars each, hats are available at under $1,000 each.

title: Filling Stations
text: Filling stations, also known as gas stations, petrol stations, or service stations, have been featured in every game in the since Grand Theft Auto III.

title: Filling Stations
text:
As limited fuel is not a game mechanic in Grand Theft Auto games, they are not interactive, except for in GTA Chinatown Wars, where they are used to create Molotov Cocktails. They appear as stationary explosive objects, where the fuel dispensers can explode if shot at or run over with a vehicle. The strength of the explosion vary between games, ranging from small, grenade-like explosions to highly violent blasts that can instantly kill the player upon impact. Some service stations in Grand Theft Auto V have accessible interiors. However, the player will receive a two-star wanted level if all the dispensers are blown up.

The prices on price boards generally reflect the prices of the place and era of the game in which they are found. For example, fuel prices in the rendition of San Andreas are $1.34 to $1.49 a gallon, typical for fuel in California circa 1992.

title: Filling Stations
text: Some places exist where filling stations once stood. One notable example is the Doherty Garage in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, which was previously a Xoomer station. The reverse can also be true. For example, the Going filling station in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City is not present in GTA Vice City Stories. In Grand Theft Auto III and GTA Vice City, driving into the fuel pumps will not cause them to blow up. They will simply fall to the ground instead. However, doing so in GTA San Andreas, Grand Theft Auto IV, Grand Theft Auto V, and GTA Online will more than likely cause them to blow up instantly. In GTA III, GTA IV, GTA V, and GTA Online, individual pumps in a housing section can be destroyed if shot at, while others can remain intact.

title: Gasso
text:
Similarly to Tosser and Going, Gasso has a limited presence in the state, operating only a single station throughout the entire region. The company's motto is "We Have Gas!" Gasso utilizes two distinct logos: one features red lettering within a blue ellipse, while the other showcases blue capital letters accompanied by five stripes adjacent to the text within a red ellipse.

The gas station is fitted with Max Pane bulletproof glass. There is a vending machine on the side of the building.

A player may become trapped, as falling through the ground could either respawn them in the solid area of the shop or repeatedly place them in the non-solid section, potentially leading to a softlock situation.

text: The Gaydar Station is a club located in San Fierro, San Andreas, that appears in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Gaydar Station
text:
Found in the Queens district, Gaydar Station's name is an obvious nod to gay culture. "Gaydar" (a portmanteau of the words "gay" and "radar") means to have the ability to "detect" if a person is LGBT+ by either their appearance, personality, or mannerisms.

The club is a medium-sized building with two entrance doors, with the first entrance being accessible. There is a stairway that leads to the second entrance, one of the doors in the first entrance is unique due to it being identical to the ones used in many restaurants as it will always open by anything without going into the interior.

title: Gaydar Station
text:
The interior is identical to the Alhambra in the Idlewood district of Los Santos, as well as the unnamed club near The Camel's Toe in Las Venturas.

The interior is a medium-sized interior with a dancing area with several people dancing, a concert area with several speakers and a bartender behind the bar of the club, two Sprunk vending machines, a snack vending machine and Duality, Let's Get Ready to Bumble and Go Go Space Monkey arcade games. There is a stairway that leads to another part of the interior with several couches and two tables, and a room with a table.

Inside, Carl can partake in a Dancing Minigame with three levels of difficulty. During dancing dates with Katie, the minigame is played, despite she doesn't like the Queens area. The interior will always play music from SF-UR, much like the other clubs.

title: Final Build Construction
text: Final Build Construction is a construction company featured in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories.

title: Final Build Construction
text:
The company is based in Vice City in 1984, with their headquarters being located in Little Havana. However, by 1986, they have left Vice City.

In 1992, the company has expanded into San Andreas. The company has significant construction work across the state, including several sites in Blueberry, Red County and The Clown's Pocket casino in Las Venturas. The company headquarters seem to be at the Las Venturas Airport, north from the LVA Freight Depot. Final Build Construction is a sponsor for the Las Venturas Bandits baseball team, as their advertisements can be seen inside the Las Venturas Bandits Stadium. The Final Build Construction logo is also featured on several Rumpo vans.

title: Final Build Construction
text:
seen inside the Las Venturas Bandits Stadium. The Final Build Construction logo is also featured on several Rumpo vans.

The company has also expanded into Liberty City sometime before 1998, as they are shown to be building the five-pointed apartment complex in Hepburn Heights in Portland. In the mission Snuff, it is shown that the Sindacco Crime Family own the construction site, but they are wiped out by Toni Cipriani on orders from Joseph Daniel O'Toole so that he could leave the Sindaccos in order to join the Leone Crime Family.

By 2000, the company has completed the apartment complex in Hepburn Heights.

title: Final Build Construction
text:
The name "Final Build" is a term used by videogame developers to describe a game that is in its final stage of developing.
In Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories, a miniature crane with the company logo can be seen building the chocolate Easter egg that can be found in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.
In Manhunt 2, the J.E.C. & Sons Construction company logo is a modified version of the Final Build Construction logo seen in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The texture file name of the logo in Manhunt 2 is ws_finalbuild . J.E.C. is a reference to , the protagonist of the first Manhunt title.

title: Kakagawa
text: The company's branding and product range suggest that it could be primarily based on , with possible inspiration from other Japanese electronics manufacturers, such as and .

title: Kakagawa
text:
There are several potential origins for the company's name:
The name might have been derived from either the Japanese city of or the , a large prefecture that includes the city of , located just south of Tokyo in the of Japan.
In the , kakagawa is a word that translates to "just done".
The term "kaka" might have been derived from the crude English word "cack", which refers to feces, while -gawa is a suffix meaning "river" in place names in Japan. As a result, the name could be a play on the phrase "shit creek". The phrase "shit creek" itself originates from the Scottish expression "up shit creek without a paddle", which means to be in a difficult situation with no way out.

title: Juank Air
text:
Juank Air provides air travel between the cities of Los Santos, San Fierro and Las Venturas, via the Los Santos International Airport, the Easter Bay Airport and the Las Venturas Airport, respectively. The airline likely operates out of San Andreas, as when Carl Johnson travels from Liberty City back to Los Santos, he takes a Juank Air flight.

The company continues to operate in 1998, as a sign for the company can be seen in Saint Mark's, Portland, Liberty City. Juank Air's fleet includes the AT-400 and the Nevada.

CJ is able to unlock taking a flight between the three main cities in GTA San Andreas, and will take Juank Air while doing so. All flights between cities are served by the AT-400. Despite bearing the company's decals, the Nevada is never seen servicing, and can be only found parked in the Easter Bay Airport.

title: Inside Track
text: Inside Track is an interactive betting shop for thoroughbred horse races featured as an accessible store in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and as a casino-themed activity in GTA Online.

title: Inside Track
text:
Inside Track's inclusion in GTA San Andreas is part of the game's gambling mechanism, serving as one of the first available means of gambling the player can perform before Las Venturas becomes accessible; in fact, the two Inside Track outlets are located within the Los Santos/Red County landmass of San Andreas that is available for the player to explore from the beginning of the game.

Inside Track also appears in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, GTA Vice City Stories and Grand Theft Auto IV, but in these games, the betting shop is a non-interactive establishment with very spartan frontages.

In GTA Online, the company's logo appears on the Red Racing Suit from the Cunning Stunts update. It also can be found as a minor sponsor on some vehicle liveries, such as the 190z.

title: Inside Track
text:
The interior of each Inside Track features four manned counters, ceiling-mounted television screens that broadcast horse races, and two inside track betting (ITB) machines, the only interactive items in the establishment, that line the walls. The interior also features a backroom which can be entered.

Unlike virtually every other interior space in the game, it is possible to enter Inside Track shops with recruited gang members and other NPCs. This is mostly likely a programming oversight linked to the storyline mission Against All Odds, where Catalina enters an Inside Track shop with Carl Johnson.

title: Inside Track
text: The ITB machine allows the player to bet on any one of the five racehorses for any amount of money divisible to five, from $5 up to $9,999,995. After selecting a racehorse, the player has to add the amount of money that they would like to bet using a calculator; each button adds a specific amount of money into the wager, namely $5, $25, $100, $250, $1,000, $5,000, or $10,000; the $0 is used to clear the amount bet.

There are five racehorses appearing in each race, with each of them numbered and color-coded. Each horse also has its chance of winning given in the form of fractional odds, ranging from 2/1 to 12/1. On the wager screen of the ITB machine, the horses are ordered from top to bottom, based on winning odds:

Once the player places their bet (thereby deducting the bet amount of money from the player), the player is directed to a broadcast of the horse race that lasts between 25 and 30 seconds depending on when the last horse crosses the finish line. The player can then spot a sign saying "SARC24", the channel which is broadcasting the horse races, which is the first TV channel the player can watch in the .

The player wins only when the horse they bet on wins the race by finishing first, in which case the player gets their wagered money back in addition to the payout money based on the horse's odds. For example, a wager of $100 is made on a horse with 2/1 odds, then that horse wins, so the total amount of money won is $300, including the wagered money.

title: Inside Track
text: The Inside Track betting shop appears in one mission in GTA San Andreas, namely Against All Odds. The mission involves Catalina, together with protagonist Carl Johnson, robbing the Montgomery branch of the betting shop for money by blowing open the outlet's safe in its back room, drawing the attention of the police before escaping to Catalina's hideout cabin in Fern Ridge.

title: Helmut Schein
text:
In GTA San Andreas, Helmut Schein markets perfume, advertising "Shine Perfume" in an avant-garde manner on the radio, parodying real-life perfume commercials during the 1990s. The lines in the commercial were voiced by Jodie Shawback, who also does the voice of Sage, the host of Radio X.

In GTA Liberty City Stories, players can find a Helmut Schein outlet in Chinatown, Portland, Liberty City circa 1998. By 2001 (the setting of Grand Theft Auto III), the Liberty City location appears to have closed down and the site is was taken over by the Cut hairdresser. Advertising for the company can also be found near Francis Intl. Airport, showcasing their furniture.

title: Helmut Schein
text:
e Cut hairdresser. Advertising for the company can also be found near Francis Intl. Airport, showcasing their furniture.

Another Helmut Schein in GTA Vice City Stories can be found at the Vice Point Mall in Vice Point, Vice City circa 1984 on the second floor of the northwestern wing of the mall between the Top Bun Hair Salon and Flyingdale's, complete with a detailed interior, although it is inaccessible to Victor Vance. The store is also later sold off by 1986 (the setting of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City), and replaced by two unmarked clothing stores.

While the Helmut Schein storefront in GTA Liberty City Stories is devoid of any interior or details to indicate its type of business, the GTA Vice City Stories Helmut Schein's interior contains sofas, coffee tables, and two counters, hinting that it may also be a furniture store similar to KLÜNT.

title: Helmut Schein
text:
Helmut Schein is a faux-German play on the euphemism for oral sex, Helmet Shine. The slogan for the company is "Polished to Perfection!", another reference. Sales for the company in GTA Liberty City Stories also claim that the sale is "the big one", a further reference.
The billboard for the company in GTA Liberty City Stories shows what appears to be a blue-filtered screenshot of the beta Mulholland Safehouse from GTA San Andreas.
If one listens closely to the commercial, various humorous and strange lines can be heard. These include "Tomorrow, I am the white rabbit", "People on beaches", "Let the children die", "What's your name again?" and "Advertising".

Literally translated from Spanish, Juguetes Regalos means "Toys Gifts".
The writing below the sign says "Calling cards" and "Buy Bus Tokens".
The Definitive Edition changed the writing below the sign, now meaning "bus tickets".
Several characters from ( and ) and (, , and ) appear on the store's signage. This is anachronistic, since the anime didn't debut in America until 1998, yet the game is set in 1992. This is because the shop front textures for the original release of the game were based on photos taken in 2003–04.
In The Definitive Edition, the copyrighted characters are replaced by Impotent Rage, Princess Robot Bubblegum's pets, and Fred's Pictures' mascot.

title: Las Venturas Bank
text:

However, no parked vehicles can be found in both levels of the parking lot. A Minigun can be found in front of the elevator door inside the underground parking lot.

The underground parking lot serves as the final destination for the The Dossier Carrier to ambush Carl Johnson with several FBI agents in the Misappropriation mission. However, if the dossier carrier is killed earlier, the building will not have a role in the storyline.

title: Kronos (3D Universe)
text:
None of Kronos' stores appears in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, but they are one of the sponsors on the Hotring Racer cars and the ProLaps White watch is manufactured by Kronos. This watch appears on a billboard in Shoreside Vale, Liberty City in GTA Liberty City Stories, with the caption "The end of time".

Kronos is more prominent in GTA Vice City Stories, with a store in Downtown Vice City and its logo appearing on vans around the city. Kronos clocks and watches can also be found within the game. Some adverts in Downtown and Escobar International Airport advertise the Kronos "Twatch" (a portmanteau of "twat", a derogatory British term, and "watch"), which appears to be a digital calculator watch, which were popular in the 1980s.

title: Kronos (3D Universe)
text:
Kronos appears to be based on and . The design of the Twatch model seen in Vice City Stories appears to be based on a Casio calculator watch. The Kronos Twatch is advertised as "Time doesn't have to cost money", likely a reference to Swatch being a relatively affordable Swiss watch manufacturer, as well as the low price of typical Casio watches.

The "Kronos" name a derivative of "χρόνος" (chrónos), a Greek term for time.

title: Nightclub
text: Nightclubs, also commonly known as clubs, are clubs used as a place to dance and socialise, as opposed to more sexually orientated strip clubs. Unlike strip clubs, however, interactive nightclubs in the are relatively rare, only appearing in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, Grand Theft Auto IV, and GTA Online. Most other games in the series also feature nightclubs but these are inaccessible and play no part in the storyline.

title: Nightclub
text:
In GTA San Andreas, clubs may be used by the player to dance with a girl, in a minigame similar in fashion to the Lowrider Challenge. The interior of clubs also comes complete with video games, and snack and drink machines. There are three clubs in GTA San Andreas:

The Alhambra in Los Santos. The building is a copy of the real-life in (which is mostly a venue for celebrity awards ceremonies, but has hosted rave parties in its Expo Center in the past).
Gaydar Station, a located in Queens, San Fierro.
An unnamed club in Las Venturas adorned with neo-new-age murals, found east of The Camel's Toe right across the street from the basketball courts. It may or may not be based on Club 662 in , owned by CEO , and 's intended destination the night he was .

title: Nightclub
text:
Nightclubs take center stage in The Ballad of Gay Tony, with three clubs being central to the game's plot:

Maisonette 9, Tony Prince's straight/celebrity club.
Hercules, Tony's gay bar.
Bahama Mamas LC, a competing club only accessible during Boulevard Baby and in multiplayer.

While in Maisonette 9 or Hercules, the player can partake in dancing and taking shots of liquor. Maisonette 9 also allows the player to perform Club Management side activities, as well as engage in champagne drinking contests.

Two of the nightclubs in The Ballad of Gay Tony are only open at night, and are closed during the day. On the contrary, Hercules is open 24 hours a day.

title: Maibatsu Corporation (3D Universe)
text:
It is a Japanese vehicle manufacturer mostly known for manufacturing the Maibatsu Monstrosity SUV circa 2001, referred to as a relatively new vehicle in Grand Theft Auto III and Manhunt. Shortly before, the company also played a major role in the 1998 protests that caused the ban of motorcycles in the streets of Liberty City.

At some point after the 1980s, the Maibatsu Corporation began operating in the United States of America. A landmark named after the company appears in Manhunt 2, located in the neighborhood of Cottonmouth in the Southern U.S., amongst other businesses shared between both Rockstar North franchises.

The company logo was first used in the promotional website for Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories.

Maclains Scottish Whiskey is a Scottish alcoholic drink appearing in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The brand is also featured in Rockstar North's Manhunt series.

title: Maclains Scottish Whiskey
text:
Maclains Scottish Whiskey bottles appear as dynamic objects and decorative props throughout San Andreas and notably used for target practicing at Emmet's during the mission Nines and AK's.

The bottle later returns in Manhunt 2 as decorative props in multiple areas of Cottonmouth.

title: Maclains Scottish Whiskey
text:
During the mission Black Project, an invisible Maclains Scottish Whiskey bottle is placed on the air vents of the Area 69. This is a level design trick by Rockstar North mission designer Imran Sarwar to keep the entrance marked on the radar. The bottle is removed as soon as the player gains access to the Area 69 interior.
Due to a developer oversight by Grove Street Games, the bottle was made visible in the original releases of The Definitive Edition. This was later patched along with the Mobile release of The Definitive Edition.
