title: Nevada
text: The Nevada is a large propeller passenger plane featured in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: Nevada
text: The Nevada is based on the vintage passenger aircraft, and as such is one of the oldest aircraft in the . The Nevada is a large propeller passenger plane with two radial engines. Its access door is at the back and the plane always leans tilted nose up when parked. It possesses Juank Air decals, and can spawn in various color schemes.

title: Nevada
text: The Nevada has a decent top speed, but it has a rather long take off distance and slow acceleration. The Nevada also has good durability; it can withstand one or two homing rockets before being destroyed. Keep in mind, though, that crashing into an obstacle head-on will immediately destroy the plane. Also, it can ram into helicopters such as the Maverick, Sea Sparrow, Police Maverick and News Chopper, but will take damage.

title: Nevada
text: The Nevada is used in the mission Dam and Blast from the "Heist" strand, where Carl Johnson has to plant explosives on the Sherman Dam generators that will be later detonated to disable the power supplying Caligula's Palace. During the mission, CJ must fly one above the dam and jumps in mid-air, which later results in the aircraft crashing into a cliff.

title: Nevada
text: Two can be found parked at Easter Bay Airport. One is near the hangars, across from a Shamal. The other is near the north of the terminals, but occasionally a Baggage or a Utility Van will spawn in place of it, or sometimes nothing at all. The doors are locked unless the player has completed Learning to Fly.

title: Nevada
text: If the player jumps on top of the Nevada and tries to walk up to the nose of the airplane, CJ will suddenly "sink" into the airplane and become stuck in such a position that only his head and shoulders are visible on the top of the nose, in front of the windshield. The only way to get out is to press the action button, where CJ will suddenly appear next to the door and open it.

title: Nevada
text:
The plane's name parodies the nickname given to the military version of the ; the , used by Allied troops during , was nicknamed named after an acronym for Transport Aircraft (DACoTA). The name for the Nevada, however, parodies US state names, and , with .
Like other -style planes (planes that tilt upwards when parked), such as the Rustler, Stuntplane and Cropduster, the plane will roll backwards when the Cars drive on water cheat is enabled.

title: HPV1000
text:
The HPV1000 is a police motorcycle ridden by San Andreas Police Department police bikers, having a siren and flashing emergency lights. The bike is depicted with a white/grey color with black boxes on the sides and the rear, having the San Andreas Police Department markings.

The HPV1000 assumes a unique model that is not shared by another motorcycle, and bears resemblance to a police .

title: HPV1000
text:
Powered by a four-cylinder engine, the HPV1000 has average acceleration, but is considerably faster than most bikes (only below higher end models such as the FCR-900, PCJ-600 and NRG-500), although the player can fall off easily if they have minimal "bike skill".

It is one of the few bikes which have off/on-road tires, which means that its main advantage over other bikes is its versatility; while some bikes (Sanchez, Quadbike) out-perform it off-road, and others (FCR-900, Freeway) surpass it while street racing, it is still considerably good at both. With this characteristic, the HPV1000 is capable of tackling the toughest of hills and roadways and is also very agile, though at higher speeds, one might have to resort to brake-turning.

title: HPV1000
text:
ughest of hills and roadways and is also very agile, though at higher speeds, one might have to resort to brake-turning.

If the Rhino or Hunter is not yet available, this bike is a good choice for completing the Vigilante side mission – mainly because the player can fire a submachine gun straight ahead or on both sides, allowing them to take out the opponent easily. Although its siren is no longer effective in prompting oncoming vehicles to move out of the way, its compact motorcycle design allows it to navigate around traffic far better than full-sized cars.

Overall, the HPV1000 is a well balanced vehicle to use, as well as one of the few bikes available from the start of the game.

The officer will shoot at the player even if they only have one star, and sometimes even after losing the star. Spawning on the road almost every time after saving the game at the Doherty Garage or The Four Dragons Casino. They spawn quite quickly; if the player kills the riders at a red stop light, another one will spawn and one can get around 6 HPVs in a short time. title: HPV1000
text: The HPV might stand for "Highway Patrol Vehicle", though it is also possibly a reference to , which is one of the most common . In a beta version of the game, there was "911" written on the rear, and "SAPD" was replaced with "POLICE". In another beta version, there was a LSPD HPV1000, implying that there would be a city-specific version of each HPV1000, rather than a state-wide version. The HPV1000's emergency lights do not flash from the specified red and blue lights. Instead, they will flash from the front turning lights. The engine sound is actually that of a ; this is also used for the PCJ-600, albeit in a higher pitch. Civilian vehicles will not move aside if the player is driving an HPV1000 with the sirens on, unlike any other emergency vehicles. If a pedestrian pushes an officer off the bike, a police officer on foot will steal the bike while they are fighting.

title: Hermes
text:
The Hermes is more legend than automobile. When all those 1960s classic muscle cars were still in diapers, the Hermes was already crawling down Eclipse Boulevard leaving a trail of unfiltered cigarettes and misogyny in its wake. With that kind of canvas you can paint a seriously offensive painting – and trust us, that eye-watering paint job is just the start. 
The Hermes is a customized late 1940s coupe featured in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, GTA Vice City Stories, and GTA Online. It is manufactured by Albany in the HD Universe.

title: Hermes
text: The Hermes is based on the , with styling cues from the , which is evident with the roof and hood shape, but the car has been evidently modified into a , with a chopped roof and an additional pair of tail lights.

title: Hermes
text: The Hermes returns in Grand Theft Auto Online, this time assuming the design of the , while still featuring influences from 1949-1951 Mercury Eight in the overall shape. The front fascia more closely resembles the . A classic bumper similar to the Hornet's can also be bought from Los Santos Customs. The rear lights and trunk bear mild resemblance to the , while the side window shape and rear, especially with the bumper removed, seems to also loosely resemble the .

title: Hermes
text:
The "Classic Flames" livery resembles the featured in the 1996 movie 
When matched with the corresponding paint color, the vehicle with this livery can also resemble the Cuban Hermes.
The "Ghost Flames" livery is similar to the one found on the by .
The "Amazing Albany" liveries are a reference to the stock car. It is a mix of the livery on ' #92 race car, and the one used by from the movie franchise.
The "Saltflat Drag" livery is loosely inspired by Ron Ernsberger's "" drag car, which appeared at the 2012 World of Speed—an annual racing event held at the on the near , .

title: Hermes
text:
The Hermes is distinguishable by its large body, but seemingly small occupant's visibility. The hood area is relatively long in comparison to the rest of the vehicle, and has a curved trunk. In GTA Vice City, The Hermes does not feature a license plate, while the other renditions adds one on the rear end (directly on the trunk in GTA San Andreas and on the rear bumper in GTA Vice City Stories).

All renditions of the Hermes spawn in a variety of primary colors on the bodywork, with the GTA San Andreas iteration having a secondary color for the interior (always set to white).

title: Hermes
text:
The performance of the Hermes could be described as average; its acceleration is underwhelming, but it has a moderate top speed. It is unusual in that it has front wheel drive (very rare in American cars of the period) and it cannot be blown up with a gas-tank shot like most cars in GTA San Andreas. The car is also prone to understeer, owing to its large size, small tires and front wheel drive.

In GTA San Andreas the brakes are extremely inefficient and are among the worst in the game, but in the hands of an experienced player, the vehicle may be used for drifting. Holding the brake and the handbrake simultaneously is a good way to increase the brake strength of the car. However, this technique is still less effective to put the car into a full stop while sliding down slopes at a high speed.

title: Hotdog
text: The Hotdog appears to be a , with some styling clues from the , converted into a hot dog van. Judging from its silver color, it appears to be made out of aluminum, which is a feature seen on campers.

title: Hotdog
text: The Hotdog is designed as a large, old van, where the front end features a small bumper with a license plate at the bottom, while the upper area has a chevron-shaped grille, a small compartment in the center, and two circular headlights beside it. The area above is occupied by the dual windshield. On the sides, the vehicle has the corresponding access doors and a long compartment on the right that is always open, while a large window and the fuel cap are seen on the left, around the rear half. The roof is distinctively rounded and tall, with an oversized roof-mounted hotdog. The rear of the vehicle is very traditional, featuring a vented unit on the upper area, a large compartment on the lower area, and red circular tail lights beside it, together with another small bumper at the bottom.

title: Hotdog
text:
compartment on the lower area, and red circular tail lights beside it, together with another small bumper at the bottom. The van is also depicted with a fully-rendered interior on the rear compartment, with several details such as compartments and cups.

The van spawns in a white/grayish color with Alex's Dog'z markings, also selling a variety of food and drinks such as tea, coffee, soup and burgers.

The player will receive 40 points of health and have their hunger eliminated when entering a Hotdog van.

title: Hotdog
text:
The Hotdog's poor performance, characterized by its slow acceleration, speed and heavy handling, makes the Hotdog an unpractical vehicle for demanding driving, although its size and weight makes the vehicle more resilient to damage, as most large vehicles do.

The van is powered by a diesel engine, coupled to a five-speed gearbox in a front-engine, rear-wheel-drive layout. It has a noisy engine sound also used on the Yankee, likely to denote its old appearance.

title: Hotring Racer
text:
The Hotring Racers in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City are fast vehicles, almost on par with most sport cars in the game, like the Infernus or the Cheetah. The top speed and the acceleration are impressive and the grip is very good. Its resistance may not be one of the best, but is still a strong vehicle. The vehicle's handling is average, but at higher speeds, it will suffer from understeer, though not as severe.

In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the first variant of the Hotring Racer shares the same performance characteristics with the other variants. It is the second fastest cars in the game in terms of top speed and boast rapid acceleration and good handling, although It is prone to fishtailing at high speeds. The Hotring Racer are rear-wheel drive, and allow drifting.

text: The Huntley is a full-sized luxury SUV that is available in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

text: The Huntley features a design with clear inspiration from a but with slight changes. title: Hustler
text:
Don't worry, the confusion is natural. You see that running board swooping low over the front wheels, that high-set radiator grille, the holder for your cigarette holder, and you're safely back where you belong in the 1920s. But then you see the carbon steel reinforcements to the chassis, the turbo charger and the bullbar, and you're somewhere else altogether. Don't try to make sense of it. Just let it do what it needs to do. 
The Hustler is a classic two-door coupe featured in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and GTA Online. It is manufactured by Vapid in the HD Universe.

title: Hustler
text: The Hustler returns with a very similar design, still based on the in the middle and rear designs. However, the front fascia, front and rear bumpers, fender shape, and gas tank are based on the ones found on the .

title: Hustler
text:
The Hustler is one of the oldest cars available in the game, and is depicted with a mildly-modified bodywork (though not the extent of the Hotknife), featuring a flat front bumper, a tall grille with vertical separations and two circular headlights, as well as a narrow and long hood. The sides have bulky fender arches and black stepsides, while the doors have circular mirrors. The cabin is relatively long and features a single rectangular windshield, dual door windows with the rearmost ones always open, rear-quarter windows and a rounded rear window. The rear has a curved trunk, circular tail lights on the fenders and a bumper that is molded with the rear end and the rear fenders.

The vehicle spawns in a variety of single colors on the body.

title: Hustler
text: The Hustler has decent acceleration, but excellent top speed, owing to its high-output engine. It has remarkably good handling capabilities for a vehicle of its age and weight; It corners sharply, but suffers from some oversteer at high speeds. The Hustler has a pretty good ramming ability in contrast to its size.

title: Journey
text:
A cross-country family vacation in an RV is an American rite of passage. Grab your spouse and the kids, and hit the road today in the Zirconium Journey. It will bring you all closer together, in a really dysfunctional, claustrophobic way. You won't end up despising each other, honest. 
The Journey is a (RV) (also known as a motorhome) in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, Grand Theft Auto V, and GTA Online. It is manufactured by Zirconium in the HD Universe.

title: Journey
text: In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the Journey is based on a motorhome, given the squared-off cabin and simplistic grille shape with turn indicators below, though with stacked circular headlights.

title: Journey
text: In Grand Theft Auto V and GTA Online, the Journey's overall design is inspired by the 1977–1980 motorhomes, such as the and models, with the grille and headlights taking cues from the and the rear being reminiscent of the 1970s–1980s, likely taken from either the or the .

title: Journey
text:
The Journey features a cab-over extension and a somewhat large cabin, similar to a Rancher. The accommodation area of the RV (the back) is well equipped with a furnished interior, which contains a red tiled floor, a sink, a table accompanied by two bench chairs found at most fast food restaurants, and some cabinets; other accessories include a ladder and a continental kit (spare tire) on the rear. The Journey also has a large flat roof, making for a great rampage platform. The only way to access the roof is to jump on the front end and make a second leap onto the top, as the ladder is unusable. Despite the large rear compartment and the access door on the passenger side, it is inaccessible; therefore, the Journey can only fit two people, both in the cab up front.

The vehicle is only available in a white color, with blue/yellow stripes on its sides. It has the same rims as the Elegant.

title: Journey
text:
The Journey, living up to its bulky size, is incredibly slow, but gains great speed going down hills. The acceleration is poor, as are the brakes, but it is very sturdy and withstands a lot of ramming before giving out and exploding (for example, the one parked at the top of Mount Chiliad can survive the plunge off the top of the mountain without blowing up). The steering is also below-par and it tends to roll a lot.

The Journey has the same engine sound as the Ambulance, Berkley's RC Van, BoxBurg, Burrito, Mule, Newsvan, Pony, Securicar, Tow Truck and the Utility Van.

title: Kart
text:
The Kart is depicted with a simple tubular steel frame chassis and basic flooring, where the front area houses a small bumper, the front wheels, the steering mechanism, a single headlight, the fuel tank and the two laterally-mounted pedals providing the corresponding throttle and braking controls, while the rear area houses the main seat, the small engine with a small exhaust, a single tail light and the rear axle with a single brake disk on the left and the chain drive and sprocket on the right side, connected to the engine. As the vehicle is not intended for use on main roads, it lacks any form of dials, although a radio is still available.

The Kart can spawn with additional matching side skirts and a small fairing over the steering wheel frame, and may spawn with a variety of primary colors applied on the tubular chassis. It uses small wheels fitted with racing slicks.

title: Kart
text:
The Kart has average speed, good acceleration and good off-roading. It is compact and capable of making sharp turns, although it can oversteer. Its low profile and light weight makes ordinarily small obstacles more dangerous.

The Kart is classed as a car, like the Mower, so CJ does not fall out of his seat when the vehicle flips over, additionally, the player cannot shoot forward from the Kart, despite having a clear view of doing so. The Kart is also able to drive under other vehicles with high ground clearance such as the Tanker trailer and the Monster.

The Kart is powered by a 2-stroke engine, judging by the engine size, which is apparently coupled to a 4-speed gearbox in a rear engine, rear wheel drive configuration. The engine sound is rather noisy because it is mounted open-air, like a motorcycle engine.

text:
The Dundreary Landstalker is a full-size luxury SUV driven by people you assume must be drug dealers or trophy wives, because that's easier than dealing with the very real possibility that they might just be more attractive and successful than you are. 
The Landstalker is a four-door SUV available in every game since Grand Theft Auto III, excluding and GTA Chinatown Wars. It is manufactured by Dundreary in the HD Universe.

title: Landstalker
text: The Landstalker has many different designs between Grand Theft Auto III and GTA Vice City Stories, usually combined from a variety of sources.

title: Landstalker
text: In Grand Theft Auto III, the Landstalker resembles a slightly altered , the , and the . It spawns in a variety of colors, with the lower sides in a gray color. In GTA Liberty City Stories, the Landstalker is based on a . Some models may also come with a roof rack and boxes in the rear compartment with the ZIP label on them. Its color distribution is the same. In Grand Theft Auto: Vice City and GTA Vice City Stories, the Landstalker resembles a , with the front fascia and taillights of the . Landstalkers feature a wood texture along the body, a feature that the Wagoneer was known for. In the iOS and enhanced versions of GTA Vice City, the Landstalker has the same "4X4 POWER" rear wheel cover that the GTA Vice City Stories rendition has, compared to the blank one seen in the original version. This version always spawns with brown/wooden strips on the sides.

In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the Landstalker generally resembles the GTA Vice City and GTA Vice City Stories renditions, but with a few changes that make its design more upscale, with the vertical grille strips and taillight design evoking the feel of a and the chrome trim evoking the original . It no longer carries a rear-mounted spare wheel; instead, a wheel is visible inside the rear compartment. It still carries the brown/wooden strips.

title: Landstalker
text: The HD Universe rendition of the Landstalker resembles both the , as seen in the front fascia and overall appearance, and the , as evidenced by its extended wheelbase, chrome trim along the lower edge of the doors and window frames, lettering along the front doors, and large roof rails. Several details are taken from the , including the headlights, tail lights, upper front bumper vent, tailgate, and blacked-out pillars. The side and rear profiles are somewhat similar to the . The grille, albeit smaller in size, bonnet, side-steps, and front bumper strongly resemble those of the , while the rear bumper seems to be taken from the .

title: Landstalker
text: The Landstalker has a light weight, a short wheelbase, high ground clearance, full-time 4WD, great grip, making for what seems at first to be a good off-road vehicle. However, the SUV is anything but that; its performance is almost ruined by monstrously stiff suspensions with little give, meaning instead of simply inducing body roll, turning causes the entire vehicle to tip over. Attempting to off-road with the vehicle can often lead to nasty surprises, as hitting the slightest bump will often send the SUV into the air, due to the stiff suspension being very bouncy. The vehicle also has a hard time transferring its traction to the ground, as the SUV tends to continue bouncing a few times, after hitting even mediocre bumps, like curbs and rocks. These attributes make the vehicle vastly inferior as an off-road vehicle when compared to the Patriot, Rancher, Sandking and Huntley.

The Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories rendition is noticeably more stable—its redesigned body features a lowered ground clearance (resulting in a slight redistribution of weight to the bottom) and a longer, heavier body (2000 kg), reducing the likelihood of rollovers. This is decidedly not the case with the version used in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories, which has some of the poorest handling and highest likelihood of rollovers of any car in the , especially when attempting the Robbery missions.

title: Launch
text:
The Launch is evidently based on the used by the .

The vessel is a medium-sized armored boat with a relatively long hull and short hand rails that reach almost to the transom, as well as a small compartment on the bow. The cabin quarters are exposed and feature an angular windshield with sectioned windows, tall frames/supports above and a frontal steel arch mounting the radar and antenna, while the rear deck mounts a rear steel arch with no features on top. The stern area after the deck consists of the large vents for the engine bay, small antennas on either side and a rear-facing seat with an unusable machine gun on the back (which resembles a and incorporates a small shield), both located on a dedicated compartment. Directly on the rear end, there are two propellers and an additional frame for protection.

The boat is available with minor roof configurations, being a black canopy over the cabin quarters or the rear deck (sometimes with no canopy at all). The vehicle spawns in a bluish primary color for most of the body, with a slightly darker shade of blue as the secondary color on the lower portions of the hull and the flat sections of the steel arches.

title: Launch
text:
The Launch's speed and handling are fairly good, on par with similarly sized speedboats such as the Speeder and Predator, but it is affected by its "heavy" armor.

The boat appears to use two inboard engines given the twin propellers and the two vents on the deck, and it uses the same engine sound as all other boats.

title: Linerunner
text: The Linerunner is designed as a typical American standard cab-styled semi truck resembling a . Its name is most likely a parody of .

title: Linerunner
text: The truck remains largely similar throughout its appearances, having a large front bumper with the license plate in the center and square indicators on either side, as well as a long nose with large fenders, rectangular headlights and an air filter on the driver side. The bottom features large access steps and large fuel tanks, while the cab features large mirrors on the doors, a trumpet horn on the roof, long exhaust stacks and the extended driver's cab quarter, with a single rear-facing window. The rear section mostly consists of the main chassis with a set of trailer cables above, the tail light units and the license plate.

title: Linerunner
text:
tion mostly consists of the main chassis with a set of trailer cables above, the tail light units and the license plate. Depending on the game, there are minor cosmetic changes between each model:

title: Linerunner
text: The performance of the Linerunner is what would be expected for a vehicle of its size and weight; it is slow to accelerate and hard to maneuver in tight spaces, but once it gets going, it has a decent top speed. Disappointingly, though, it is not quite as strong as its intimidating appearance and size would suggest, and it gets knocked around by other vehicles surprisingly easily. Nevertheless, the truck proves effective breaking through police roadblocks, provided it is sufficiently speedy. The handling of the truck is fairly steady, but if the player does manage to roll it over, it is very difficult to get it back onto its wheels due to its height. In GTA Vice City Stories, it can easily be driven and balanced on only one side, making it the easiest vehicle to get a two-wheel bonus in.

title: Mesa Grande
text: The general design of the Mesa Grande remained largely similar across its 3D Universe appearances, being a compact SUV with boxy, rugged styling and a high ground clearance for off-roading. However, as a compact SUV, it only has a moderate top speed. Its light weight and stiff suspension may also result in frequent rollovers on uneven terrain or in accidents. It is powered by a diesel engine, which is large and powerful. The engine has been an inline throughout the 3D universe.

However, in GTA Vice City Stories, the SUV is now a bit different. It weights a bit more, it has a higher top speed, and is powered by a petrol engine.

title: Monster (3D Universe)
text: The Monster Truck (formerly simply Monster) is a vehicle featured in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and .

title: Monster (3D Universe)
text: In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the Monster is depicted as a generic two-door pickup truck that appear to be a "Stage Three" monster truck, with a tubular chassis, four-link suspension and nitrogen gas shocks. However, it also appears to have a real metal body, whereas "Stage Three" monster trucks use fiberglass replica bodies. The vehicle always has a black cover on the bed, single red tail lights and a red chassis with the tubular frames exposed.

title: Monster (3D Universe)
text:
e vehicle always has a black cover on the bed, single red tail lights and a red chassis with the tubular frames exposed.

The vehicle resembles a 1992-1997 , with the headlight design of a 1994-1997 . It has painted bumpers and a rectangular grille in the front with two horizontal and two vertical elements, followed by single headlights with amber indicators beside them. It is also the only version of the Monster which can be visually damaged – at the doors. The vehicle spawns in a white/light gray primary body color with a variety of secondary colors applied to the bumpers, lower portions and wheel arches (sometimes the same color as the primary, resulting in a single body color scheme).

The vehicle uses large-profile tires with wide track and a detailed tread pattern.

title: Monster (3D Universe)
text:
The overall performance of any variant of the Monster depends on where the vehicle is driven. Overall, the Monster is more suited for off-road driving, and performance stats between all variants of the Monster are identical.

Generally, its acceleration and top speed are only average, making the vehicle unsuitable for high-speed driving. However, the vehicle compensates with good handling and off-road capabilities, being able to drive up steep terrain and traverse bumpy obstacles. In place of a handbrake turn, the Monster features a four-wheel steering "mode", where the rear tires will also turn alongside the front ones, reducing its turning radius. In addition, the Monster, much like the Dumper, is capable of running over smaller vehicles and subjecting them to a moderate rate of damage; this ability can, however, risk flipping the Monster.

title: Monster (3D Universe)

smaller vehicles and subjecting them to a moderate rate of damage; this ability can, however, risk flipping the Monster.

Whilst the vehicle is very stable while upright, the vehicle can rest sideways or upside down if it flips from a crash or has tumbled down very rough terrain, due to its evenly heavy design. With usage on urban roads, the vehicle's larger size increases the susceptibility of the player hitting vehicles and street furniture.

The vehicle uses a petrol engine with a 5-speed gearbox and an all-wheel-drive layout, and it uses a distinctively loud engine sound, likely to denote its immense power delivered to the large wheels.

In Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and GTA Vice City Stories, it resembles a typical American ice-cream truck, based on the Boxville but considerably smaller, making it closer to the real-life Chevrolet P10 Step-Van, whereas the standard Boxville is based on the larger P30 Step-Van. In most of its appearances, the ice-cream ornaments on top of the van serve as sexual references, in keeping with Rockstar's traditional sexual humor. In GTA Vice City and GTA Vice City Stories, it resembles a pair of breasts, whereas in GTA San Andreas, it resembles a penis. The GTA III and GTA Liberty City Stories renditions are exceptions, with only a single ice cream swirl and a chocolate bar.

title: Mr Whoopee
text:
GTA III and GTA Liberty City Stories renditions are exceptions, with only a single ice cream swirl and a chocolate bar.

As an ice-cream van, the vehicle is equipped with a musical jingle that can be toggled with the horn button. The jingle is the same as the one used by a similar vehicle in , except for GTA San Andreas. The GTA III version has no horn or radio, and holding the horn button will simply sound the jingle. The GTA Vice City version has a radio, but lacks a horn; holding the horn button does nothing.

title: Mr Whoopee
text: Due to its size, Mr Whoopee is fairly slow and suffers in steering and braking. In addition, the Boxville-style renditions are top heavy and lead to proneness to rolling if not driven carefully. The van in GTA San Andreas is significantly slower than the van in other games. The van in GTA Liberty City Stories can also easily blow up after few collisions, thereby making it the weakest vehicle in GTA Liberty City Stories. Most renditions have powerful-sounding diesel engines, however, the van in GTA III has a gasoline engine, while the GTA San Andreas version has a much weaker-sounding diesel. The Mr. Whoopee vans are front-wheel drive in GTA III and GTA Vice City, and rear-wheel drive in all other games.

"Whoopee" is a 1920s slang term for sexual intercourse, another reference to the van's sexual nature.
Mr. Whoopee is most likely a portmanteau of "", a brand of ice cream vans and products in the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand, and "", an ice cream van brand operating in the United States.

title: Mr Whoopee
text: The Grand Theft Auto III and GTA Liberty City Stories versions of the truck feature an ice cream swirl with a chocolate flake, a reference to the popular served in the United Kingdom and Ireland. The jingle of the GTA III rendition is the same as that of "Mr Lolly", another ice cream van from the DMA Design (later Rockstar North) game . The slogans on the Mr Whoopee, "Please Stop Me!" and "I Will Chill Again!", foreshadow the later Rockstar North game Manhunt (specifically the blood-inscribed writing on the masks of some of the ) which was in concurrent development with GTA III. These slogans are retained on the GTA Liberty City Stories model. The driver of the Mr Whoopee in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is depicted as an obese ice cream man dressed as a clown. His appearance is made to be similar to the clown pictures seen on the truck.

title: Mule
text: Each model of the Mule has different features, which depend of the game's settings. The Liberty City models have design cues with the Pony for the cabin (albeit with tweaked headlights), tail lights on the rear bumper and a straighter box shape. In GTA Liberty City Stories, the headlights are moved slightly upwards. In Grand Theft Auto III, the vehicle assigns a primary color for the body and a secondary color for the front bumper and lower fuel tanks, while in GTA Liberty City Stories, the secondary color is assigned to the box, while the front bumper and lower fuel tanks are permanently black. The Vice City and San Andreas models are of an entirely unique cabin design, with the turn signals moved to below the headlights, removed bumper lights in favor of marker lights around the top of the box's rear and a rounded upper front section on the box.

title: Mule
text: The Mule serves as a mid-size truck that is a step below the Yankee, thus being smaller in size (in actuality being narrower) and lighter. As a result, the Mule fares better in speed and acceleration, but still possesses average-to-poor cornering. In addition, the high center of gravity of the truck may also result in easier rollovers and an inability to return upright in many occasions. The small wheels on the Mule also relate to this problem.

Overall, the Mule has good durability, but not as good as any other truck. However, the truck has a good top speed, and an acceptable acceleration, capable of getting to a decent speed without causing too much oversteer. The brakes of the truck are its main downside, as they seem to take a while to make the Mule come to a complete stop, and when they do, it usually results in a crash, or the truck taking a while to regain speed, making it a bad choice for a getaway vehicle.

The Packer is a two-door industrial truck appearing in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, Grand Theft Auto IV, Grand Theft Auto V and GTA Online, and due to appear in . It is manufactured by MTL in the HD Universe.

title: Packer
text: In all of its appearances, the Packer bears resemblance to a 1986 Peterbilt 379 Car Carrier, with a single body setup (without a dedicated trailer to transport cars) and a 10-wheeled design layout.

In Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, the cab design is strongly similar to that of the Linerunner (albeit with larger headlights), while the rear section consists of the main chassis with side fuel tanks, guard rails with yellow-black warning patterns, various marker lights on the sides, and a set of square tail lights and license plate on the rear end. The Packer is unable to transport vehicles, as they cannot be attached, and remain stationary while the Packer simply rolls out from beneath them. However, it can be used as an ideal portable ramp to set up for stunts, as players usually approach it at speed to jump and clear walls, fences and low buildings, and to drive onto rooftops (either by jumping from or driving up the ramp to climb them) and other high places.

It is possible to safely store one car on the Packer due to its ability to move the upper ramp up and down; this is done by driving it onto the bottom ramp and slowly closing the top ramp down. It can transport up to three vehicles due to the ability to elevate part of the ramp; however, cars can still roll off at sudden stops, so the player must operate it with high sensitivity to keep the cars safely in place. title: Jetpack
text:
The Jetpack allows for directional control with two omnidirectional nozzle-like jets providing thrust. It is unique as it spawns like a weapon pickup when not in use, it is activated instantly when the player walks into it, and is dropped when the vehicle exit button is pressed. The Jetpack has a much lower altitude limit than the other aircraft vehicles, and it is not ideal for scaling taller buildings, such as the Big Pointy Building in San Fierro.

The Jetpack is indestructible as it is not considered a vehicle, and it also makes the player invulnerable to falling, crashing into walls or moving vehicles, landing on top of a moving helicopter and other dangers. It can also be fully submerged without damage by diving into water at high speeds.

The Jetpack is a prototype created in the US military's underground lab in Area 69. Carl Johnson is dumped in front of Area 69 and is told to steal the 'Black Project' by The Truth in the mission of the same name. According to dialogue, the vehicle is the result of a $60,000,000 project. Due to the secrecy of the project, The Truth is the only civilian other than Carl to know of its existence. CJ later uses it to attack a military train in the mission Green Goo. After the said mission, the Jetpack will be unlocked and will spawn at the Verdant Meadows Airfield, beside the asset collectible. The Jetpack is a great choice for collecting Horseshoes in the Las Venturas area.

title: LHD-069
text: LHD-069, also known as the USS Liberty, is an uncontrollable Naval amphibious assault ship featured in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

title: LHD-069
text:
LHD-069 is the first large-scale military ship to physically appear in a Grand Theft Auto game and is located at the Easter Basin Naval Station in Easter Basin, San Fierro. The ship carries a number of Hydras.

Accessible areas aboard LHD-069 include the flight deck and two internal decks. Players do not have access to interiors of the upper levels of the ship's superstructure.

The flight deck is actually capable of functioning as a short takeoff and landing strip for nearly any plane. In addition to the superstructure, two S.A.M. sites which are only active during Vertical Bird are installed there, while a Hydra will also spawn occasionally at the same level after completion of the mission.

title: LHD-069
text:
Bird are installed there, while a Hydra will also spawn occasionally at the same level after completion of the mission.

The internal decks resemble warehouses, with crates and explosive military armaments (which obviously explode when shot at, similarly to explosive barrels) scattered and stacked around the area. Large loading bays on the upper deck and an amphibious vessel wet dock in the lower deck are also incorporated into the ship, although it is only during Vertical Bird that both the loading bays are functional and the wet dock rear door is opened.

title: LHD-069
text:
although it is only during Vertical Bird that both the loading bays are functional and the wet dock rear door is opened.

Vending machines are available in a recreational room on the upper internal deck, next to the stairwell to and from the lower deck. There are forklifts on the upper internal deck and a Vortex hovercraft close to the lower deck's wet dock which can also be commandeered and driven out up the stairs. In addition, a Tear Gas pickup may be found near a small box in the lower internal deck.

If the player attempts to board the ship by land, they need to pass through the Easter Basin Naval Station, obtaining an automatic five-star wanted level; attempts to reach the ship via aerial means will also result in the player obtaining such a wanted level.

title: LHD-069
text: LHD-069 is modeled after the real-life . It was first commissioned in 1989 and also uses an "LHD-x" classification to identify multiple Wasp class ships. As only eight Wasp class ships (numbered LHD-1 to LHD-8) were built, "LHD-069" is clearly a non-existent designation, with the "069" numbering deliberately selected as a running gag.

title: LHD-069
text: Vertical Bird Carl Johnson infiltrates the ship on Mike Toreno's orders, in order to steal a Hydra VTOL jet and use it to destroy a flotilla of Tropic spy ships in the Sherman Reservoir. This is the only time military personnel is present on board and the ship's S.A.M. sites are active, as well as the ship's rear door and loading bays.

title: Monster (monstera)
text: In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the Monster is depicted as a generic two-door pickup truck that appear to be a "Stage Three" monster truck, with a tubular chassis, four-link suspension and nitrogen gas shocks. However, it also appears to have a real metal body, whereas "Stage Three" monster trucks use fiberglass replica bodies. The vehicle always has a black cover on the bed, single red tail lights and a red chassis with the tubular frames exposed.

title: Monster (monstera)
text:
e vehicle always has a black cover on the bed, single red tail lights and a red chassis with the tubular frames exposed.

The vehicle resembles a seventh generation and features silver bumpers with a rear plate, a rectangular grille with three horizontal separations, single square-shaped headlights with small indicators below, and silver strips running through the sides. The vehicle only spawns in a red, blue, white and yellow racing paintwork (with the files indicating it spawning in a white color), and includes various optional accessories, including a bed-mounted rollbar with attached lights, roof-mounted lights or a roof-mounted spoiler.

The vehicle uses large-profile tires with wide track and a detailed tread pattern.

title: Monster (monstera)
text:
The overall performance of any variant of the Monster depends on where the vehicle is driven. Overall, the Monster is more suited for off-road driving, and performance stats between all variants of the Monster are identical.

Generally, its acceleration and top speed are only average, making the vehicle unsuitable for high-speed driving. However, the vehicle compensates with good handling and off-road capabilities, being able to drive up steep terrain and traverse bumpy obstacles. In place of a handbrake turn, the Monster features a four-wheel steering "mode", where the rear tires will also turn alongside the front ones, reducing its turning radius. In addition, the Monster, much like the Dumper, is capable of running over smaller vehicles and subjecting them to a moderate rate of damage; this ability can, however, risk flipping the Monster.

title: Monster (monstera)
text:
smaller vehicles and subjecting them to a moderate rate of damage; this ability can, however, risk flipping the Monster.

Whilst the vehicle is very stable while upright, the vehicle can rest sideways or upside down if it flips from a crash or has tumbled down very rough terrain, due to its evenly heavy design. With usage on urban roads, the vehicle's larger size increases the susceptibility of the player hitting vehicles and street furniture.

The vehicle uses a petrol engine with a 5-speed gearbox and an all-wheel-drive layout, and it uses a distinctively loud engine sound, likely to denote its immense power delivered to the large wheels.

title: Monster (monstera)
text: The Monster's tires cannot be shot off like real monster trucks. They probably have air in them to provide normal tire function, but the tires are likely constructed of thick rubber, enough to be drivable without air in them. The doors of the second and third variants cannot be damaged, unlike the first variant. If the player places the monster's front wheel on a car's engine, the car might go flying up or flip over, sometimes the car might even get stuck in the ground and grow extremely large, doing this may result in the monster flipping over from the car though. Due to the front end being non-damageable, there is nothing modeled under the hood. Even despite the clear seams for the hood, they cannot be opened nor damaged in any way. Like the Dumper, the Monster has the ability to drive over cars rather than into them. They are the only two vehicles in the game capable of doing so.

On a related note, the Monster is the third largest drivable land vehicle in the game. If hydraulics were to be installed on the Monster Truck, then the wheels would be stuck up in the air. text:
The Glendale is a four-door sedan appearing in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and GTA Vice City Stories.

title: Glendale (3D Universe)
text:
The Glendale, conceived as a sedan from the late 1950s to early 1960s, seems to be a composite of two distinct real-world vehicles. The front end bears a resemblance to the , incorporating features from the , while the rear and side profile are inspired by the .

This design stands in contrast to the Oceanic, which features the Polara's front and rear elements along with the sides of the Oldsmobile 88.

title: Glendale (3D Universe)
text:
While commonly featuring a two tone paint scheme along with the roof being set to white as the secondary colour, the Glendale in GTA San Andreas has a colour variation that is totally red — the roof color can also be modified in via a Transfender mod shop.

Along with the Broadway, Hustler, Savanna, Tornado, and the Voodoo, the Glendale in GTA San Andreas does not appear to have fuel caps. However, it will explode if shot on the rear registration plate, perhaps indicating that the fuel cap is behind the number plate, in a similar fashion to some real life cars manufactured in that era.

title: Glendale (3D Universe)
text:
In terms of performance, the Glendale is only average, with an average top speed, mediocre acceleration, moderate endurance and average cornering. However, the Glendale seems to be quite durable, especially in comparison to newer cars. The power-to-weight ratio of the Glendale may be a contributing factor to its below-average acceleration, as the car is heavy, but also possesses a weak engine, and as a result, is also a poor hill climber.

However, the GTA Vice City Stories rendition of the Glendale has a much higher top speed in comparison to its other counterparts, being able to go up to 200 km/h. Its stats are shared with the Greenwood.

title: Greenwood (3D Universe)
text:
The Greenwood is a four-door sedan appearing in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and GTA Vice City Stories.

The car also appears in the HD Universe where it is manufactured by Bravado.

title: Greenwood (3D Universe)
text: In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the Greenwood makes a return with minor design modifications compared to its earlier version. The most significant changes include the front bumper and grille, which appear to be inspired by the . Additionally, the Landau roof has been slightly adjusted to accommodate an opera window, resembling the . The layout of the tail lights was also simplified.

title: Greenwood (3D Universe)
text: The Greenwood is designed as a boxy four-door sedan with traditional features, where the front end bears a large gray/silver bumper with black trim, a tall grille with vertical elements and gray/silver housings with dual headlights on the upper side and dual indicators on the lower side, along with a traditional hood with an elevation in the center, where the grille is located. The sides of the car have gray/silver trim at the bottom and on the flared wheel arches, traditional door handles and a squared-off greenhouse area with a landau on the back section. The rear is relatively simple and bears a small emblem in the center and wide tail lights on either side, while the lower area bears a similar gray/silver bumper with black trim, a license plate in the center and small plate light casings beside it.

title: Greenwood (3D Universe)
text:

The Greenwood in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories has the grille marked up to the hood and has a pointed shape to the front, as well as a straight front bumper with a similar pointed shape on the front. In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, however, the grille has been shifted down the front fascia and is more flattened, with the pointed shape shifting from the front of the grille to its upper border. The front bumper becomes slightly curved lower towards the middle to adapt to this redesign. On the rear door, there is an extra pillar that separates the bodywork from the landau on both sides of the car, forming an . Similarly to many cars, a fuel cap is added to the rear left fender.

The car will spawn in multiple primary colors for the bodywork and secondary colors for the landau in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City and Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, but in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories, the car's body colors are normally restricted to a light blue-gray body with a white landau.

title: Greenwood (3D Universe)
text:
Though the speed and acceleration of the Greenwood are less than ideal, the handling is improved over comparable vehicles found in the same areas, and the braking is pretty good. The front-engine, rear-wheel-drive vehicle is heavy and relatively sturdy, capable of withstanding a good deal of damage and making it a relatively solid choice for drive-bys and primary transport.

The vehicle has a V8 engine under the hood (mistaken to be a V4 due to the poorly textured valve cover and sparkplug inlets). In GTA Vice City and GTA Vice City Stories, it uses a relatively mid engine sound shared with the Regina, Top Fun and Kaufman Cab. while in GTA San Andreas, it uses a mid-revving sound shared with the Perennial, Regina, Tampa, Manana, Moonbeam, Bobcat, Sadler, Washington, Virgo and Romero.

title: Maverick (3D Universe)
text:
The Maverick is a two-bladed helicopter appearing in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, GTA Liberty City Stories and GTA Vice City Stories.

As well appearing as a fully controllable helicopter, static or otherwise non-controllable helicopters assuming the design of the Maverick have also appeared throughout the . The Maverick goes on to appear in the HD Universe with a similar design based on that of the family of helicopters.

title: Maverick (3D Universe)
text: In all its appearances, the Maverick assumes the design of a four-door, four-seater helicopter inspired by that of the .

title: Maverick (3D Universe)
text:
Executive helicopter for high rollers, big spenders, and tourists. 
The Maverick in the 3D Universe is depicted with a large fuselage, rounded nose and large windows, as well as long skids, tall engine compartment with a two-bladed main rotor, and a long tail boom with the corresponding stabilizers and four-bladed tail rotor. The interior of the aircraft has a bench seat for the rear passengers and two control sticks for the front occupants (although only the left occupant takes control of the vehicle).

The part of the Maverick's tail connecting to the fuselage appears slightly thicker in GTA Liberty City Stories and GTA Vice City Stories, a trait that isn't carried over to its police variant in these games.

text:

In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the Maverick is slightly scaled up, becoming bigger in contrast to the other 3D Universe depictions. This unique trait is also carried over to all of the helicopter's variants.

All renditions of the Maverick followed an identical color distribution, consisting of a primary color for most of the fuselage and tail boom, and a secondary color in the form of dual stripes at the bottom. In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the skids are painted with the secondary color.

title: Maverick (3D Universe)
text:
In the 3D Universe, the Maverick is a short, nimble, basic helicopter. It has a high top speed, forward thrust is acceptable, and its maneuverability is on par with most competitors. Durability is rather slack due to its thin bodywork and overall 'light' design, making it unsuitable for long-time air pursuits or for purposeful crashing, as it can only take several crashes, and a small amount of bullets before it begins to smoke and break down.

The aircraft is powered by a single engine.

title: Maverick (3D Universe)
text: In all of its appearances in the 3D Universe, the rear passengers of the Maverick (as well as its police variant) will sit in the exact same location - in the middle of the rear bench seat. This results in both passengers seating "inside one another" if the player manages to get both passengers to seat in the rear. This glitch is actually present, because the rear passengers have not been given defined seating coordinates inside the model of the helicopter - as a result they simply seat in its geometric center (centroid), as this is the default position for any vehicle's occupants. A similar glitch happens with Romero's Hearse in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.

The Moonbeam is a four-door minivan appearing in Grand Theft Auto III, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, GTA Liberty City Stories and GTA Vice City Stories.

The Moonbeam goes on to appear throughout the , later returning in the HD Universe.

title: Moonbeam (3D Universe)
text: The Moonbeam is straightforwardly modeled after a , albeit featuring tall tail lights. The Grand Theft Auto: Vice City version's tail lights are similar to those found on vans, while other renditions have single red lights.

title: Moonbeam (3D Universe)
text: The Moonbeam is generally depicted as a bulky 1980s van, but minor cosmetic changes have been made throughout its appearances. The Grand Theft Auto III, GTA Liberty City Stories and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories renditions of the Moonbeam features a split grille, a smaller front and rear reverse lights attached to the rear bumper, while the Grand Theft Auto: Vice City rendition, albeit similar in design, features a single grille, larger front and rear amber lights attached to the rear bumper, along with a unique "MOONBEAM" badging on the rear compartment door. The Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas rendition is based upon the Grand Theft Auto: Vice City model, but the badge is absent and the rear single red lights from the Grand Theft Auto III rendition are now used again.

Only GTA Vice City Stories features bumpers that have a proper secondary color.

During the development of GTA III, the van was originally known as the "Aster", a clear reference to the Chevrolet Astro name. The van is depicted in the Capital Autos website.

title: Moonbeam (3D Universe)
text: Moonbeams between GTA III and GTA Vice City Stories all possess similar handling properties. Performance is poor, due to the under-powered engines, rear wheel drive layouts (However, Moonbeams in GTA III and Vice City are front-wheel drive), heavy bodies, soft suspension, and high center of gravity (leading to a tendency to flip on rough terrains). As a result, the Moonbeam is generally unsuitable for high-speed driving and has little practical use aside from its fundamental function as a mode of transport. In GTA San Andreas it is one of the worst vehicles, as not only does the vehicle have bad performance, it also has a bad build quality and low durability. The Moonbeam only holds a maximum of four occupants.

All renditions of the Stallion remained largely the same, retaining the front bumper with fog lights, dual grilles, circular headlights, twin ram-air hood, square tail lights on either side of the rear bumper and twin exhaust pipes. The Liberty City models are generally simple, with visible door handles and a central handle on the trunk.
The Vice City models have chrome details running through the sides, while the trunk handle was downscaled and moved to the driver side.
The San Andreas model retains the chrome details from the VC models, but the trunk handle was moved back to the center. A fuel cap can be also seen on the rear left fender.

Liberty City and Vice City versions may spawn with an open top or soft top, while the San Andreas version features a hard top. The soft top always has a secondary color, but the hard top has the car's primary color.

title: Stallion
text:
The Stallion's handling varies in each game. In Grand Theft Auto III, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City and GTA Liberty City Stories, it has reasonable acceleration, though its rear wheel drive layout and huge amount of low-down torque led to it being easy to perform professional-grade drifts around corners, doughnuts and wheel-spin when taking off. 

The GTA Vice City Stories version is altogether slower than the other renditions, but its tail-happy traits remained. In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, it handles much like the Clover and Sabre (even having the same engine sound to the latter), but fishtailing rarely occurs.

Unlike most other muscle cars, the Stallion has a low-revving V8 that sounds more like an inline engine (except for GTA San Andreas), coupled to a four-speed gearbox in a front engine, rear wheel drive layout. The engine sound is shared with the Manana, Perennial, and Idaho.

title: Stallion
text: The Stallion name, when first adopted in the first , appears to be a play of the name. Both names refer to equestrian terms for horses that are not fully domesticated. A "" is "a free-roaming feral horse of the that first descended from horses brought to the Americas by the Spanish", while a "" is simply "a male horse that has not been neutered, castrated, or gelded". A version of the Ford Mustang called the Stallion Special was sold exclusively by Mainway Ford in 1967. The Stallion is the longest surviving car in the , and also one of the most frequently featured civilian cars in the series, appearing in 9 out of 12 GTA games, the exceptions being the two Grand Theft Auto: London expansion packs, and , although the Diablo variant appears in the latter. Even though the Stallion does not appear in , the Crapi is sometimes referred to as the Stallion's British variant.

title: Regina
text:
Signature Dundreary grille, opulent wood panelling, roomy luggage compartment, and a roof rack for the family dog - the ultimate vehicle to live the 1960s suburban dream today. 
The Regina is a four-door station wagon which has appeared in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, GTA Vice City Stories, , Grand Theft Auto V and GTA Online, and is due to appear in . It is manufactured by Dundreary in the HD Universe.

title: Regina
text: The Regina is designed as a quintessentially 1980s American station wagon which bears a strong resemblance to the (specifically the ones from 1982 and onward) in overall design – the bulging grille, metal side trim that runs from back to front, and the mono-colored tail lights being the dead giveaways of the car. The car itself also resembles the , Parisienne's platform-mate (specifically the ones from 1980 and onward), judging by its front and rear bumper.

title: Regina
text:
In the HD Universe, the Regina's overall body design and greenhouse are now based on the older while also taking influence from a mix of the and the in the front fascia design. The rear is mostly an original design, with cues from the . The wheels take inspiration from 1960s rally wheels.

In Grand Theft Auto V and Grand Theft Auto Online, the facelifted aspects of the Regina's headlights, hood design, and roof racks are seemingly influenced by the , specifically the 1973 model.

title: Regina
text: All renditions of the Regina are identical in design, with the exception of the GTA San Andreas rendition, which has single headlights on either side (opposed to the dual ones from the GTA Vice City and GTA Vice City Stories renditions) and separated tail lights that have similar design to those from the Rancher.

title: Regina
text: In The Lost and Damned, the Regina is designed as a lean 1960s/1970s station wagon, but retains the dual headlight setup from the GTA Vice City and GTA Vice City Stories renditions, though the lamps themselves are rounded, and the turning lights are moved onto the bumper. The tail lights are somewhat identical (albeit smaller) and it features reverse circular lights on the rear bumper. The rear compartment has "DUNDREARY" on the lower side between the tail lights, and the car's name is seen on the passenger side. The Regina now sports a combination of a primary color on the body and the secondary color on the roof (normally dark grey or black), as well as a chrome roof rack.

title: Regina
text:
Between GTA Vice City and GTA Vice City Stories, the acceleration of the Regina is modest, and its speed is severely lacking - with its front-wheel drive powertrain, the underpowered struggles to move this behemoth. Handling is sluggish, the car suffers from obvious understeer, and the brakes do a barely acceptable job of slowing down the enormous chassis. The Regina is not especially sturdy, nor capable of withstanding heavy damage, and is a generally undesirable vehicle.

The FWD layout is the opposite of its real-life inspirations, as these cars are usually RWD.

title: Regina
text:
With a significant cosmetic change, the Regina in The Lost and Damned sports several noticeable differences in its performance. Due to its heavier weight, the car is less nimble than its predecessors, occasionally requiring the aid of the handbrake in tight corners or high speed turns. Braking power is correspondingly below average. The suspension may be insufficient on the road, as the heaviness on the rear section will disrupt it when sorting out low obstacles such as curbs.

The car is also classified as one of the Beaters cars in GTA IV, emitting a knocking sound from the engine at high revs, occasionally taking a noticeably long time to start, and backfiring through its exhaust pipe.

The Regina is powered by a high displacement V8 engine coupled to a five-speed manual transmission in an FR layout. The car shares its handling with the Solair, but its engine sound is the same as that of pickup trucks such as the Bobcat and the Rancher.

title: Ranger
text: GTA San Andreas Ranger handles somewhat the same as the original Rancher, but it is much faster, having a top speed similar to that of some sport cars. title: Shamal
text:
The Shamal is seemingly based on the , although the nose is considerably longer than most Learjets, resembling later models. The Shamal bears characteristic features from most conventional planes, being the left-side access door/ladder, the and the . The aircraft is only seen in a light gray colour similar to the Hydra (though not listed in the car color files).

The Shamal's interior can be seen during Freefall. The size of the interior appears larger than usual for an aircraft with a relatively small fuselage, and the interior incongruously features 16 windows (nine on the left and seven on the right) when the plane features only eight outside. Despite this, the plane has a very limited passenger capacity.

title: Shamal
text:
The Shamal is available to the player at the beginning of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, in Los Santos International Airport, acquirable by trespassing over the security booth if the player still hasn't got the pilot's licence. It is a considerably fast jet, being on par with the Rustler, and due to its availability, the Shamal is a good choice for players who are just learning to fly jets, as its handling is balanced and it is easy to land on runways. Also, despite it visually having a large passenger capacity, it can transport only the player. The Shamal is somewhat decently agile in terms of manoeuvrability, and its availability to the player early in the game provides an easy way to grind their Flying Skill stat before even reaching Verdant Meadows Airfield much later in the storyline.

The Shamal is powered by twin engines, sharing the engine sound with most jet-powered aircraft.

title: Sea Sparrow (3D Universe)
text:
The Sea Sparrow (also known as the Seasparrow) is a two-bladed amphibious utility helicopter appearing in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and GTA Vice City Stories.

The Sea Sparrow goes on to appear in the HD Universe, where it also assumes the design of an amphibious variant of the in-universe Sparow.

title: Sea Sparrow (3D Universe)
text: The Sea Sparrow is an amphibious version of the Sparrow and is based on the . It features pontoons attached to the landing skids and a single greyish color for the fuselage. The vehicle is equipped with a machine gun, which is mounted below its fuselage.

title: Sea Sparrow (3D Universe)
text:
In all of its appearances, the Sea Sparrow has the same performance as the Sparrow, but has the ability to land on water (just like the Leviathan). This makes the aircraft a good choice to collect Oysters in GTA San Andreas. On the water, it will be steady and can be accessed easily. The Sea Sparrow has good handling and quick maneuvering, just like its basic counterpart. While on water, the rotors of the Sea Sparrow can spin to full speed almost instantly.

Similarly to the regular Sparrow, the aircraft is powered by a single piston engine, and shares the engine sound with the Maverick and its variants.

title: Sea Sparrow (3D Universe)
text: The Sea Sparrow also has a .50 caliber machine gun, which is very similar to that of the Hunter, being able to lock on to pedestrians and vehicles within a 45-degree radius, approximately. Due to the high firepower of the gun, it can make short work of groups of enemies and vehicles.

This is a good way to store a Sea Sparrow earlier on in the game, provided the player can get a Sea Sparrow.

text: The Raindance is a medium-sized helicopter featured in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

text:
The Raindance is based on the , the civilian version of the famous , with its livery modeled after the 's colors.

The helicopter always spawns in a white body with yellow and blue stripes painted from the front to the back along the fuselage, as well as the Fire Department of San Andreas stencil on the sides, the FDSA logo on the engine covers and large identification numbers (always labeled as 371) on the side doors.

Despite its implied use by the Fire Department, the Raindance is never seen flying around San Andreas or otherwise being used or associated with the Fire Department.

title: Rustler
text: The Rustler draws inspiration from various real-life fighter planes, primarily the . However, it also appears to take inspiration from the , the and the . Despite its evident inspiration on combat planes, the Rustler is seemingly treated as a recurring civilian/trainer plane.

title: Rustler
text:
espite its evident inspiration on combat planes, the Rustler is seemingly treated as a recurring civilian/trainer plane.

The Rustler takes the design of a single-seater "interceptor" aircraft with a relatively large and sectioned fuselage, where the nose houses a large four-bladed propeller, a large intake below the spinner and numerous exhausts on the sides. Around the middle section, there is the small cockpit with a sliding canopy and the main wings mounted at the base of the aircraft (low-wing setup) with the corresponding ailerons, while the underside has dedicated hatches for the main landing gear. The tail boom houses the empennage with the horizontal stabilizers and the vertical stabilizer, while the lower side has a single tail wheel. Carl Johnson stands on top of the plane's left wing to open the hatch to reach the cockpit.

text:

The Rustler is seen with a gray body and black/white stripes on the lower surfaces of the main wings and the tail boom, representing that signified aircraft during . The primary color is applied to the upper surfaces of the fuselage, wings and horizontal stabilizers, while the secondary color is applied to the end of the nose, the wing tips and the vertical stabilizer.

The vehicle is armed with a set of six built-in machine guns fixed into the wings.

title: Rustler
text:
As expected from a fighter plane, the Rustler has impressive speed in the air and is very maneuverable, making it one of the easiest planes to fly, and it is also the first one provided to the player during the course of the story. However, it has a relatively long take-off time compared to other propeller-planes of its size. Like other propeller planes, it will stall when the player attempts to fly it vertically. The plane is also incredibly susceptible to damage.

The Rustler is powered by a V12 engine similar to its real-life inspirations, and uses a low-pitched sound also used on the Stuntplane.

title: Rustler
text: The machine guns deal a moderate amount of damage, but they do not lock onto targets. Being coupled with the plane's impressive speed while in the air, this makes them difficult to use effectively. However, the Rustler can shoot down an AI-controlled Hydra in a dogfight with no problems, due to its maneuverability, speed, the machine guns' power and the guns' rate of fire.

title: Rustler
text: It uncommonly spawns on the bottom floor of the police impound lot in Roca Escalante, occasionally alongside a Leviathan and a Hydra on the PS2 and Xbox versions. Sometimes, the plane intersects the ground, making it nearly impossible to even enter the plane. On the PC version, the spawning frequency of the Rustler in the LVPD impound lot is largely reduced, though it may still spawn, unlike the Leviathan or the Hydra. In the remastered versions of the game, the Rustler is no longer found inside the impound lot. In a hangar in the southern part of Easter Bay Airport, the hatch is locked until the player completes Learning to Fly. It spawns at Verdant Meadows after completing the mission Learning to Fly, in a small hangar east of the AC tower. It is occasionally seen being flown in the sky by invisible NPCs.

The Skimmer is a propeller seaplane featured in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and GTA Vice City Stories.

title: Skimmer
text: In all of its appearances, the Skimmer is simply a Dodo (based on the ) with a pair of large pontoons on the bottom in place of landing gears; the Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas rendition further includes reinforcement on the connection between the pontoons and the fuselage, as well as harnesses between the pontoons and fuselage and the tailfin. While the Grand Theft Auto: Vice City and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories renditions have a two-bladed propeller, the Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas rendition comes with a four-bladed propeller.

title: Skimmer
text:
renditions have a two-bladed propeller, the Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas rendition comes with a four-bladed propeller.

While able to land on water, the Skimmer in GTA Vice City does not feature any functional doors, resulting in the player getting warped inside the plane when entering. If the player exits the plane, however, they are immediately spawned on top of the wing of the plane. This problem was rectified in GTA San Andreas, in which the door of the plane can be opened, and the player can enter and exit through the doors, a feature only possible with Carl Johnson's ability to swim, which Tommy Vercetti does not have. Similarly, in GTA Vice City Stories, if the player enters the Skimmer, they will be warped.

Unlike the Dodo, the Skimmer in GTA Vice City and GTA San Andreas may come in a variety of two-tone body colors (as opposed to the same red-and-white color scheme of the Dodo). The Skimmer in GTA Vice City Stories simply comes with an all-grey body color.

title: Skimmer
text: Aside from its beneficial amphibious nature, the performance of the Skimmer in the air is very much similar to the Dodo in that they both have the same sluggish acceleration and poor top speed, owing to a low-power engine. However, the Skimmer has a tendency of stalling easier. In GTA Vice City, the Skimmer can reach high speeds by moving the plane up and down in an undulating motion, but this takes a while to achieve and is not necessarily useful given the relatively small size of Vice City. This makes the plane only suitable for steady, slow air travel. In GTA San Andreas, the Skimmer uses a four-bladed propeller instead of the two-bladed version that the Dodo has. This means the engine may have higher performance, but is offset by the increased weight of the pontoons of the Skimmer.

title: Skimmer
text: The name "Skimmer" comes from a family of tropical birds with the same name. Similarly, the term "skimming" can refer to dragging something quickly across the surface of water. The Skimmer may run very slowly on the water resulting in inability to take off. This problem appears frequently if the game is running above 30 frames per second, with the greater amount of FPS resulting in more issues. The easiest way to solve it is to turn on the frame limiter in the settings of the game. In the game files of GTA Vice City, the Skimmer is defined as a boat instead of a plane because of its ability to float on water, with the latter type being reserved for uncontrollable aircraft. The Skimmer also retains this type in GTA Vice City Stories, even though the plane type is used for the Biplane. This is why the Skimmer has no functional doors in these games.

title: Skimmer
text: The Skimmer is the only airplane in the game that will not explode if it collides head-on with any solid object. This is because of its pontoons, which have a solid area that extends past the front end of the airplane. If the plane was to be crashed slightly pitched down, or by crashing into a hanging object, the plane will explode instantly like other airplanes. The propellers of the Skimmer suffer from a visual glitch. When they are not rotating, they look exactly like the propellers of a Dodo. However, when they start to rotate and pick up speed, they appear wider and with a more rigid, triangular shape, just like the Skimmer from GTA Vice City. This is because the texture files of the plane have been handed down from GTA Vice City. This visual glitch is only found on the PS2 version of the game.

title: Picador
text:
1960's entry in a long, esteemed line of Cheval coupé utility vehicles. Combining all the style of a two-door hardtop with the practicality of an integrated cargo tray, this most certainly isn't a jack of all trades and a master of none. 
The Picador is a featured in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, Grand Theft Auto V, and GTA Online. It is manufactured by Cheval in the HD Universe.

title: Picador
text: The Picador shares a likeness to the Buccaneer. As a result, it is implied to be a coupé utility variant of the Buccaneer, which shares a similar grille and headlight design. It may occasionally be depicted with different items on its bed as two separate extras, the first one being two planks and the second one being several Sprunk cans. The vehicle is seen in a variety of primary colors on the body, as well as secondary colors on the inner bed walls and wheel wells (though this color cannot be changed through a mod shop).

title: Picador
text:
The Picador has the highest top speed and acceleration for any pickup in the game, possibly due to the large V8 diesel engine. However, it is also the lightest and lacks the torque of the stronger trucks; its cornering is also a little unstable, owing to its rear-wheel-drive layout. The Picador can only carry two in the cab.

The vehicle uses a low-revving and noisy engine from the Cabbie, Fortune, Intruder, Sunrise, Vincent, Willard and Yosemite.

title: Pony
text: The Pony is a medium-sized civilian and commercial van featured in both the and HD Universe. It is manufactured by Brute in the HD Universe.

title: Pony
text:
Between Grand Theft Auto III and GTA Vice City Stories, the Pony is depicted as a generic, medium-sized van that has appeared in two different forms:

In GTA III and GTA Liberty City Stories, the Pony features a modern appearance with a high roof (compared to the lower roof of the Rumpo) and resembles a slightly generic .

The Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories renditions, however are directed in an older form with a conventionally low roof which makes the van aesthetically similar to Ford vans from the late 1980s and 1990s such as the , with influences from the .

In all its portrayals, the Pony is capable of carrying four passengers (two in the front, two in the back), and can be found driving around industrial areas.

Regular Ponies in San Andreas may occasionally appear with stereo systems in their cargo holds. One such Pony is seen during the mission Life's a Beach, where it is used by a DJ for a beach party (see Variants for more details).

title: Pony
text: In GTA III and GTA Liberty City Stories, despite being a van, the Pony is able to accelerate finely and reach top speed very quickly, making it one of the best vans in the games. Although the steering is not as favorable, it can easily be overcome by using the handbrake in sharp turns and corners.

title: Pony

Although the steering is not as favorable, it can easily be overcome by using the handbrake in sharp turns and corners.

The performance of the Pony was harshly redesigned in GTA Vice City and GTA Vice City Stories. While it has retained its decent top speed, its acceleration is now poor. Unless the van is being driven on a lengthy road with no interruption -which is almost never the case- it will never have enough time on full-throttle to reach top speed. The heavy weight of the van prevents it from being able to effectively steer without using the handbrake, but even that is not straightforward because using the handbrake tends to cause the van to come to a complete stop before continuing to accelerate, unless it is being driven on top speed, which is very unlikely due to the aforementioned reasons.

text: In all of its appearances, the Predator serves as the main patrol vessel used by law enforcement. It is usually seen roaming waters or pursuing the player when they have a Wanted Level.

title: Predator
text:
The Predator in the 3D Universe is depicted as a police-issued speed boat with a small cabin and an open rear, loosely based on a Cougar Enforcer patrol boat (possibly a combination of the 35 and the 40 Gen4 models). It has two built-in .50 caliber machine guns on both sides of the hull.

In Grand Theft Auto III and Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories, the boat is relatively simple, featuring a simplistic hull, a rotating radar antenna and two large aerials on the back of the cabin roof. It is only seen in a blue primary color on the lower side with a white secondary color on the upper side, with "POLICE" markings on the sides. In the Xbox and mobile versions of GTA III, the Predator features a bow rail, a small ladder on the back, and buoys attached to the sides.

In Grand Theft Auto: Vice City and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories, the boat retains most of the design and features, but the upper hull area has vented details on the sides and the lower hull area has a worn appearance. In GTA Vice City, it is seen in an entirely white color (PC) or with the lower hull being painted green (PS2), while in GTA Vice City Stories, the lower hull is painted in a sky blue color.

In Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the boat assumes the same features as the GTA Vice City rendition, but adds a rear surfing-style rack with mounted police light beacons. These lights are permanently activated, though no siren sound is heard or activated. The Predator has a light beige colored lower hull and a white colored upper hull.
